*Priest's verse:* Through the prayers of our holy fathers...  
*And we say:* Amen. *Then we say:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *Glory: Both now:* Lord, have mercy *(Thrice).* *Bless! Then the Priest gives the dismissal, and we conclude the Hour. But if there is no Priest, the senior says:* Through the prayers of our holy fathers... *And we say:* Amen. *Then we say:* Memory eternal unto you, O worthy of beatitude, ever-memorable Founders!  
*In this manner it is chanted for the Third Hour, for the Sixth, and for the Ninth Hour, and for Compline once, likewise also for the Midnight Office, even until Thomas Sunday.*  
*And the Third Hour, the Sixth, and the Ninth we chant together in the narthex. When the senior directs, we strike the clapper as is customary for the resurrection. And we enter into the narthex. And we chant, having said:* Through the prayers... *and* Amen. *At the conclusion of the Hour for the 3rd, we strive likewise a second time, and say:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice), and the rest of the Hour for the 6th Hour. Then also the third time, for the 9th.*  
*If, however, by necessity there is no Liturgy, then in place of* "Bless the Lord, O my soul": Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship... *(Once).*  
*We chant:* Anticipating the dawn... *Glory: Kontakion:* Though Thou didst descend into the tomb, O Immortal... *Both now:* Only-begotten Son... *We chant the Beatitudes, from the Canon, Odes 3 and 6, once. Priest:* Wisdom! *Reader, the Title of the Apostle and the reading itself. Then the Priest reads the Gospel.[^499] Then:* Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest... *Then the choir sings, and we chant:* I believe in one God... Remit, pardon... *And after the* Our Father: *Kontakion:* Though Thou didst descend into the tomb, O Immortal... *Glory: Both now: Kontakion:* Rejoice, O hallowed divine dwelling... Lord, have mercy *(40 times).* *Then:* One is Holy, One is Lord, Jesus Christ, to the glory of God the Father, Amen. *And we sing in place of* "Blessed be the Name of the Lord": Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *Then Psalm 33:* I will bless the Lord at all times... *The conclusion, unto* "shall not want any good thing". *And we chant the dismissal, and depart to the refectory.*  
*If, however, there is the Liturgy, the Apostle and Gospel are not read at the Hours, for they are read at the Liturgy. But only after chanting the third in the narthex, when he has said:* Lord, have mercy *(40 times).* *Then we go from the narthex into the church, saying:* More honorable than the Cherubim... *and* In the Name of the Lord, bless, father! *And the Priest desiring to sing the Holy Liturgy, standing before the Holy Doors, says:* God be gracious unto us and bless us, cause His face to shine upon us, and have mercy on us! *Glory: Both now:* Lord, have mercy *(Thrice).* *Bless! The Priest gives the dismissal and forgiveness, and begins the Divine Liturgy.*

*Concerning the Moleben on Holy Pascha:[^500]*  
*It is fitting to know how the Moleben on Holy Pascha is chanted. The Priest says:* Blessed is our God! *And we say:* Amen. *Then the Priest:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *And we at the last proclaim:* And upon those in the tombs bestowing life! *Then:* Christ is risen... *thrice on the kliros. The Priest saying the verses:* Let God arise... *Verse:* As smoke vanishes... *Verse:* So let the sinners perish... *Verse:* This is the day which the Lord hath made... *And we at each verse sing:* Christ is risen... *once. Then the Priest:* Glory: *And we:* Christ is risen... *Priest:* Both now: *We:* Christ is risen... *In place of Alleluia, the Priest says:* Christ is risen from the dead... *And we:* And upon those in the tombs bestowing life! *Then Glory: Both now: The Ypakoë:* Anticipating the dawn...  
*If thou desirest to append a Canon to any Saint, thou dost likewise first say the Troparion of the Saint once. Glory: Both now:* Anticipating the dawn... *After this the Great Ektenia:* In peace let us pray to the Lord. *Then the Canon of Pascha, with the Heirmos to 6, with the refrain:* Christ is risen! *Note: And to the Saint, if there be one, to 4. On Wednesday and Friday of Bright Week, we chant the Canon of Pascha to 8, with the Theotokia of that same Canon, two troparia. Katavasia:* Let the people sing... *After Ode 6, the Kontakion and Ikos of Pascha. Then the Prokeimenon, Tone 3:* This is the day which the Lord hath made... *Verse:* Give thanks unto the Lord... *Then to the Saint, the Prokeimenon, Gospel from Luke, Resurrectional 6, Pericope 114. Then to the Saint. After Ode 9, in place of "It is truly meet", the Heirmos:* Shine, shine... *Then:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *Then the Ypakoë:* Anticipating the dawn... *Glory: Troparion of the Saint: Both now, Kontakion:* Though Thou didst descend into the tomb... *Then the Ektenia:* Have mercy on us, O God... *After this the Priest says:* Wisdom! *We say:* Christ is risen... *Then the Priest in place of "Glory to Thee, O Christ God":* Christ is risen from the dead... *And we:* And upon those in the tombs bestowing life! *And the dismissal with the Cross, he says thus:* May Christ Who is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life, our true God, through the intercessions of His all-pure Mother... *Then he proclaims:* Christ is risen! *And we answer:* Truly He is risen! *And again we chant:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *Then:* Lord, have mercy *(Thrice), with chanting.*  
*And the Liturgy takes place early.*  
## On the Holy and Great Sunday of Pascha: Beginning of the Divine Liturgy[^501]
*First Antiphon, Psalm 65, Tone 2. Verse 1:*  
Shout with jubilation unto the Lord, all the earth!  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*And the other choir, the same verse:* Shout with jubilation unto the Lord, all the earth; sing now unto His Name, give glory to His praise!  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Verse 2:* Say unto God: How awesome are Thy works! In the multitude of Thy power shall Thine enemies flatter Thee.  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Verse 3:* Let all the earth worship Thee and chant unto Thee; let it chant unto Thy Name, O Most High!  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Glory: Both now: Both choirs together with a most exalted voice:*  
Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Second Antiphon, Psalm 66, Tone 2. Verse 1:*  
God be gracious unto us and bless us.  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who didst rise from the dead, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!  
*The other side, the same:* God be gracious unto us and bless us; cause His face to shine upon us and have mercy on us!  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God...  
*Verse 2:* That we may know Thy way upon the earth...

...Thy way upon the earth, Thy salvation among all nations.  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who didst rise from the dead...  
*Verse 3:* Let the peoples give thanks unto Thee, O God; let all the peoples give thanks unto Thee.  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who didst rise...  
*Glory: Both now:* Only-begotten Son...  
*Third Antiphon, Psalm 67, Tone 5:*  
Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered.  
*Troparion:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).*  
*The other side, the same:* Let God arise, and let His enemies be scattered; let them also that hate Him flee before His face.  
*Troparion:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).*  
*Verse 2:* As smoke vanishes, so let them vanish; as wax melts before the fire.  
*Troparion:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).*  
*Verse 3:* So let the sinners perish at the presence of God; but let the righteous be glad, let them rejoice before God.  
*Troparion:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).*  
*The Entrance:*  
*The Deacon or the Priest proclaims:* Wisdom, stand upright! *elevating the Holy Gospel. And we chant the Introit:* In the churches bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel! Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *Glory: Both now: Kontakion:* Though Thou didst descend into the tomb... *In place of the Trisagion:* As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ, Alleluia!  
*It is fitting to know that these Antiphons and "As many as have been baptized into Christ" we sing throughout the entire Bright Week, even until New Sunday; likewise also the Communion verses.*  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* This is the day which the Lord hath made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.  
*Verse:* Give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures unto the ages.  
*Verse:* Let the house of Israel now say: For He is good, for His mercy endures unto the ages.  
*The Epistle, from the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 1:* The former treatise have I made...  
The former treatise have I made...  
*Alleluia, Tone 4:* Thou, having risen, shalt have mercy upon Zion.  
*Verse:* The Lord looked down from heaven upon the earth.  
*The Gospel according to John, Pericope 1.*  
*And when the time for the reading of the Holy Gospel hath arrived, the Superior stands in the sanctuary at the High Place, on the eastern side of the Altar-Table facing west, and the Holy Gospel is held before him by two clerics. The Senior Deacon, desiring to read the Gospel, proclaims with a loud voice:*  
**Deacon:** Bless, master, the evangelist of the holy, glorious, and all-praised universal herald of God, the Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian!  
*Having taken the Holy Gospel, he makes a bow unto the Superior. Then the Superior says:*  
**Superior:** God, through the intercessions of the holy, glorious, and all-praised universal apostle... *and the rest.*  
*And the Deacon goes forth and stands at the customary place directly facing the royal gates, elevating his face. And the Superior having first proclaimed:* "Wisdom, stand upright! Let us listen to the Holy Gospel!" *The Deacon says the same:* "Wisdom, stand upright!" *Superior:* "The reading of the Holy Gospel according to John." *Likewise also the Deacon. Superior:* "Let us attend!" *Deacon, the same.*  
*And the other deacons do not proclaim, as is customary. Then the Superior reads:* "In the beginning was the Word..." *facing west, while the Deacon faces east. And at each exclamation or verse of the Gospel they strike the church bell once: and the Paraecclesiarch outside the church strikes the great wooden clapper and the great bell. And at the final exclamation, they strike all the bells and the great clapper a little.[^502]*  
*In Little Russia there is a custom that all concelebrating PRIESTS, as many as there are, and likewise the Deacons, read after the Superior, having taken their stand in various places, the Gospel by strophes as the Superior arranges, and breaks off; concerning which see above in order.*

*And in order the Divine Liturgy of Chrysostom proceeds according to custom. Communion verse:* Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality, Alleluia! *And when the Priest says:* With the fear of God and with faith... *we, in place of "Blessed is He that comes in the Name of the Lord", sing:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *And in place of "Let our mouths be filled":* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *Likewise in place of "Blessed be the Name of the Lord":* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *And in place of the Psalm "I will bless the Lord": we sing:* Christ is risen... *(12 times), and continuously until the antidoron has been distributed by the Superior. Then the Deacon:* Wisdom! *We:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *After this the Priest says the dismissal, according to custom as indicated at Matins.*  
*Let it also be known that the Doors of the Church and of the Sanctuary, both the Great and the small side doors, across all churches throughout the entire Bright Week, are not shut, except during the time of Communion.*  
*Then Prayers at the Offering of Meats in the Narthex:*  
*When the Priest has begun:* "Blessed is our God:", *and after we have chanted:* "Christ is risen..." *(Thrice).* *The Priest again:* "Let us pray to the Lord."  
*And this First Prayer:*  
Look down, O Lord Jesus Christ, upon these meats of flesh, and sanctify them, as Thou didst sanctify the ram which the faithful Abraham offered unto Thee, and the ram which Abel offered unto Thee as a whole burnt offering; likewise also the fatted calf which Thou didst command to be slain for Thy prodigal son when he returned again unto Thee; that even as he was accounted worthy to delight in Thy goodness, so we also may receive as sanctified and blessed by Thee these foods for the nourishment of us all. For Thou art the true Food and the Giver...  
...and the Giver of good things, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.  
*Second Prayer, for the blessing of Cheese and Eggs:[^503]*  
**Priest:** Let us pray to the Lord.  
O Sovereign Lord our God, Maker and Creator of all things, bless the curdled milk and with it also the eggs, and preserve us in Thy goodness; that partaking of these Thine ungrudgingly bestowed gifts, we may be filled with Thine ineffable goodness. For Thine is the majesty, and Thine is the Kingdom, and the Power, and the Glory, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen. *And the dismissal.*  
*And he sprinkles with the lesser sanctified water. And the poor and needy distribute from these offerings, and take a little for themselves home for a blessing.*  
*Be it known that swine's flesh and the offering of pascha is not the Pascha, nor the Lamb, as some say and receive, and partake thereof with all reverence as if of some holy thing:[^504] but it is a simple offering: for it is not to be offered as a Sacrifice unto God. But only that for them that begin to eat meat and cheese after the Fast, it may be blessed for food by the prayers appointed by the Priest. For Christ Himself is the Pascha and the Lamb Who takes away the sins of the world, offered by the Priest unto God and the Father upon the Altar in the unbloody Sacrifice in the All-Pure Mysteries of His Precious Body and Life-Giving Blood; and they that worthily partake thereof eat the True Pascha. And for this reason it is not proper to bring those offerings into the Sanctuary or into the Church, seeing they are not the Pascha, but to bless them with prayer outside the Church or in the Narthex, according to the Third Canon of the Holy Apostles, which says:* If...

"If any Bishop or Presbyter, contrary to the Lord's ordinance concerning the Sacrifice, shall bring any other things to the Altar, honey or milk, or coffee, or instead of wine, strong drink, that is to say, beer, or mead, or fowl, or any animals, or pulse, except fresh ears of corn or grapes in their season, and oil for the lamp, and incense at the time of the Liturgy, let him be deposed." *And according to the Sixth Council in Trullo, in Canon 99, which says:* "We have learned that this also takes place in the land of the Armenians: that some, boiling parts of meats within the Holy Sanctuaries, offer portions to the Priests, dividing them in the Jewish manner. Therefore, keeping the Church blameless, we decree that it is not lawful for any Priest to receive divided portions of meat from them that bring them, but let them be content with whatever the bringers shall see fit to give them, such offering being made outside the Church. And if anyone do not this, let him be excommunicated."  
*After the dismissal of the Divine Liturgy:[^505]*  
*The Priest having taken the festal icon of Christ's Resurrection, and the Deacon having received from the Priest the Artos through the Royal Doors, if both are in the sanctuary; but in monasteries it is placed on the iconostasion on the left side before the patronal icon of the All-Pure Mother of God: and at the antidoron where the first kiss the icon of the Feast, and then also the Artos; and the Deacon in sticharion takes it from the place, and carries it in his hands, one or two lamps preceding. And the Superior and all the brethren according to their rank go forth with the Artos, that is, the Bread, a whole Prosphora prepared with the Cross inscribed upon it, from the church into the Refectory, chanting in place of the Psalm "I will exalt Thee":* Christ is risen... *while the Paraecclesiarch and other brethren ring all the bells and clappers. And having entered into the Refectory, they place the Feast icon and the Artos in their places. And the Superior having said:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice), and the* Our Father: *Glory: Both now:* Lord, have mercy *(Thrice).* *Bless! Superior:* O Christ God, bless the food... *and the rest. Then:* Through the prayers of Thine all-pure Mother and of all the saints, O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on us! *And we say:* Amen. *We sit down, each in his own place, with all silence and reverence. And in the Refectory there is great consolation for all.*  
*If, however, by reason of some great necessity there was no Liturgy, then after the Hours he takes the Antidoron brought from the Prothesis where the Liturgy was served, or left for that purpose from a previously celebrated Liturgy. We go to the Refectory, as said above.*  
*We ought to know this also, brethren: NOTE: That our consolation should not be carnal, but spiritual, remembering the divine saying of the Savior:* "Let not your hearts be weighed down with surfeiting and drunkenness." *And the Apostle saying:* "Whether ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God." *Rather let our consolation be in listening to the Holy Scriptures and in being filled with them, especially on such great Feasts, and not in filling the belly beyond the measure handed down by rule to monks from the holy and God-bearing Fathers.*  
*We begin to read in the Refectory, from this light-bearing day, Chrysostom's Commentaries on the Acts of the Holy Apostles: which we complete unto the Sunday of All Saints.*  
*The Order of the Panagia performed in Monasteries at the customary Refectory on Holy Pascha, and throughout all Bright Week even until Saturday of New Week:*  
*The Artos, which is the Prosphora, and around the Cross which is on the Prosphora we write this:* "Christ is risen! Truly He is risen!" *(Thrice).* "We worship His third-day Resurrection!" *And he places it covered in the Panagiarion, and the prayer over the Artos:* "With joy and gladness..." *and the rest. After this, rising from the table, the brethren place it upon the table, singing:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice), and:* Lord, have mercy *(Twice).* *Lord, bless! Then the Cellarer, having received the customary forgiveness from the Superior and the brethren:* "Bow down, holy fathers, and forgive me a sinner!" *We say:* "May God forgive and bless!" *Then taking off his kamilavka, he proclaims in place of the great Name of the Holy Trinity, saying:* "Christ is risen!" *(Thrice).* *And we answer:* "Truly He is risen!" *The same, having signed the Artos cruciformly, says:* "We worship His third-day Resurrection!" *and places it upon the Panagiarion. Then the Cellarer brings the Artos upon the Panagiarion unto the Elder, and the Superior kisses the Artos, and all the brethren after him, chanting Ode 9 Heirmos:* Shine, shine... *and the other two troparia of that Ode, and again the Heirmos:* Shine, shine... *And after the kissing of the Prosphora by all, the Cellarer returning sets it before the Superior, and says:*

*And he says the verse:* Through the prayers of our holy fathers, O Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us! *And we say:* Amen. *And we sing:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *Glory: The Ypakoë, we say not to chant:* Anticipating the dawn... *Both now: Kontakion, likewise not to chant:* Though Thou didst descend into the tomb... Lord, have mercy *(Twice).* *Lord, bless! The Priest, or if there is no Superior:* Blessed is God Who shows mercy unto us and nourishes us from His great and rich gifts, by His grace and love toward mankind, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. *And we say:* Amen. *Then the Superior:* May God forgive and have mercy on them that have served us. *And immediately he goes forth from the Refectory into the Church; and all the brethren according to their rank, the Priest preceding with the Icon of Christ's Resurrection, and the Deacon with the Artos, and the clerics singing:* Christ is risen... *Then the Paraecclesiarch and the other brethren strike all the bells and clappers. And when the Superior and brethren have gone out into the Church, the Priest and Deacon place the Icon and the Artos in their places. And we chant:* And unto us He hath given eternal life! *And we go unto our cells.*  
*In this manner takes place the kissing of the Prosphora, which is the Artos, throughout all the week of the holy Bright Sunday, even unto Saturday.*  
*Note: It is fitting to know this also: That if it happen that any brother fall asleep and depart unto the Lord during this holy Week of Pascha:[^506]*  
*We do not sing over him the customary Order for the Departed, but the entire Resurrectional Order; that is to say: After the Priest says:* Blessed is our God! *We sing:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *And:* Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the holy Lord... *The Canon, the Exapostilarion of Sunday, the Epistle and the Gospel of the Feast, on the Praises, the Kiss of Peace, and the Dismissal.*  
*This office was translated from the Greek dialect into the Slavonic tongue by Gabriel the Hieromonk, Protos of the Holy Lavra of Athos.*  
## On the Holy and Great Sunday of Pascha: At the Service of Vespers[^507]
*The Paraecclesiarch, having received a blessing from the Superior, goes into the Church, and lights all the tapers and the church lamps. He rings all the bells abundantly. NOTE: Even as they began to ring today from the morning on all the clappers and all the bells: so do we do throughout all Bright Week at every Office. On Bright Saturday evening, at Vespers, we again begin to ring as on other days.*  
*And when they have assembled in the Church, the Priest or the Superior, and the Deacon, vest in the sanctuary from the beginning. If it be the Superior, for the Entrance he vests in all the priestly bright vestments according to his rank. And the Priests, as many as are at the Entrance, only in phelonia; likewise also the Deacons. And standing before the Holy Table with the censer, he censes cruciformly, saying:* Blessed is our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. *And we answering:* Amen.  
*The Priest or Superior begins with the Deacon:* Christ is risen... *with singing, thrice. Likewise also we sing:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *The verses the Priest himself alone says: Verse 1:* Let God arise... *Verse 2:* As smoke vanishes... *Verse 3:* So let the sinners perish... *Verse 4:* This is the day which the Lord hath made... *And we, at each verse, sing:* Christ is risen... *thrice. The Priest:* Glory: *We:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *The Priest:* Both now: *We:* Christ is risen... *(Thrice).* *And again the Priest:*

*Priest:* Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death! *We complete the ending:* And upon those in the tombs bestowing life. *Then the Great Litany:* In peace let us pray to the Lord. *"Blessed is the man"* is not read.  
*Instead, we sing "Lord, I have cried" in Tone 2, and the Resurrectional Stichera on 6, Tone 2:*  
*Stichos:* For with Thee there is forgiveness. (Ps. 129:4)  
*Sticheron:* Come, let us worship God the Word, begotten of the Father before the ages, incarnate of the Virgin Mary; for having endured crucifixion, He was delivered unto burial as He Himself willed, and having risen from the dead, He saved me, a wandering man.  
*Stichos:* My soul hath waited for Thy word; my soul hath hoped in the Lord. (Ps. 129:5)  
*Sticheron:* Christ our Savior, having nailed to the Cross the handwriting that was against us, tore it up, and abolished the dominion of death: we worship His third-day Resurrection.  
*Stichos:* From the morning watch until night, from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord. (Ps. 129:6)  
*Sticheron:* With the Archangels let us hymn the Resurrection of Christ; for He is the Redeemer and Savior of our souls; and in awesome glory and mighty power He comes again to judge the world which He created.  
*Stichos:* And He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities. (Ps. 129:8)  
*Anatolian Sticheron:* An Angel proclaimed Thee, O Master, Who wast crucified and buried, and said unto the women: Come, see where the Lord lay! For He is risen as He said, being almighty. Therefore do we worship Thee, the only Immortal One: O Giver of Life, Christ, have mercy on us!  
*Stichos:* O praise the Lord, all ye nations; praise Him, all ye peoples. (Ps. 116:1)  
*Sticheron:* By Thy Cross Thou didst abolish the curse of the tree; by Thy Burial Thou didst put to death the dominion of death; and by Thy Rising Thou didst enlighten the human race. Therefore do we cry aloud unto Thee: O Benefactor, Christ our God, glory to Thee!  
*Stichos:* For His mercy is confirmed upon us, and the truth of the Lord endures unto ages of ages. (Ps. 116:2)  
*Sticheron:* The gates of death opened to Thee in fear, O Lord, and the gatekeepers of Hades were terrified when they beheld Thee; for Thou didst shatter the bronze gates and crush the iron bars, and Thou didst lead us forth from darkness and the shadow of death, and didst tear our bonds asunder.  
*Glory:*  
*Sticheron:* Singing the saving hymn, we cry aloud from our mouths: Come, all ye, let us fall down in the House of the Lord, saying: O Thou Who wast crucified upon the Tree, and didst rise from the dead, and art in the bosom of the Father, cleanse our sins!  
*Both now: Theotokion (Dogmatikon of Tone 2):*  
The shadow of the Law passed away when grace arrived; for as the Bush burned without being consumed, so as a Virgin thou didst give birth, and a Virgin thou didst remain. In place of a pillar of fire, the Sun of Righteousness hath shone forth; in place of Moses, Christ, the Salvation of our souls.  
*Entrance with the Gospel. Deacon or Priest:* Wisdom! Stand upright! *O Joyful Light. Then the Deacon or Priest:* Let us attend! *Priest:* Peace be unto all! *Deacon:* Wisdom, let us attend! *Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:[^508]* Who is a god so great as our God? Thou art the God Who workest wonders! (Ps. 76:14)  
*Verse 1:* Thou hast made Thy power known among the peoples. (Ps. 76:15)  
*Verse 2:* And I said: Now have I begun; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High. (Ps. 76:11)  
*Verse 3:* I remembered the works of the Lord; for I will remember Thy wonders from the beginning, and will meditate. (Ps. 76:12)  
*And again:* Who is a god so great as our God... *And immediately the Deacon or Priest:* And that we may be accounted worthy...  

...to hear the Holy Gospel: and: Wisdom! Stand upright, let us hear the Holy Gospel. *Then the Superior reads from the Holy Gospel according to John, Pericope 65 (John 20:19–25):[^509]* "The same day at evening..." to the end: "...I will not believe." *We sing the Litany:* "Let us all say..." *And:* "Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening..." *Then:* "Let us complete our evening prayer..."  
*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 2:*  
Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, hath enlightened the whole universe, and Thou hast called back Thine own creation: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!  
*Then the Paschal Stichera, Tone 5: "A Pascha sacred..." with their verses. Glory: Both now: "The Day of Resurrection, let us be radiant in festivity..." After "Christ is risen...":* *(Some say the Theotokion according to the Tone throughout the entire week.)*  
*Priest:* Wisdom! *We:* Bless, Father! *Priest:* Blessed and most glorified is Christ our God always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. *We:* Amen. Establish, O God, the Orthodox Christian faith... *And in place of "Glory to Thee, O Christ God", the Priest says:* Christ is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death! *And we:* And upon those in the tombs bestowing life. *And immediately the Priest says the Prayerful Dismissal with the Cross, as set down at Matins (see fol. 184)[^510]. And the kissing of the holy icon. And we go into the Refectory. And so throughout the entire Bright Week at the evening service.*  
*Be it known that at Matins in the beginning the Priest alone says "Christ is risen..." with the verses from Psalm 117: "Give thanks unto the Lord..." which are used at "God is the Lord". At Vespers, however, it is from Psalm 67: "Let God arise..." as was appointed at Sunday Vespers.*  
*Compline and Midnight Office are sung in this manner throughout the entire Bright Week, as indicated here (see fol. 180 and 181). After the verses: "Through the prayers of our holy fathers...", the Dismissal is on the same fol. 181.*  
*Then the Monastic Forgiveness before the Superior; if there is none, before the Priest:* Bless me, holy fathers, and forgive me a sinner! *We answer:* May God forgive and have mercy. *The Superior does not recite the Commemoration Roll (Pomennyk); but the Priest intones the litany of the Pomennyk:* Let us pray for the pious and Christ-loving... *the entire Pomennyk down to the departed, because throughout the entire week we omit commemorations of the departed. Then the Superior gives the blessing, and we make our mutual forgiveness before the Superior, or if there is none, before the Priest, two by two, and go unto our cells.*  
*Typikon Chapter Concerning the Annunciation:*  
*It is fitting to know that if the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos should coincide on Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday of Bright Week (Tone 4): but here only when the Paschalion numeral falls on 4, the Feast of the Annunciation occurs. Then see here the Chapters, and the heading of April 23, as was said (see fol. 196), and examine the proper rubrics both here and there.*  
*On the Holy and Great Sunday of Pascha: At Small Vespers (in the evening):*  
*After the Priest says:* Christ is risen... *(thrice), and the customary verses. Glory: Both now:* Christ is risen... *Immediately the Deacon intones: "Lord, I have cried". Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 2, on 4. Glory: Both now: Dogmatikon, Tone 2:* The mystery hidden from all eternity... *If it be for St. George, then Glory to the Saint, and Both now: Theotokion in the same tone. Then: "O Joyful Light", without an entrance. Prokeimenon:* Who is a god so great... *(thrice), and "Vouchsafe, O Lord". At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 2:* Thy Resurrection, O Christ... *And of the Feast, idiomela, 3, Tone 4, of Great Vespers with their verses. Glory:* Gabriel proclaimed the good tidings... *Both now, Tone 5:* The Day of Resurrection... Christ is risen... *(thrice). Glory: Both now: Troparion:* Today is the salvation... *If April 23, Glory: Troparion of the Saint; Both now: Theotokion:* The mystery hidden from all eternity... *Little Litany, and Dismissal.*  
*At Great Vespers:* *The Priest, having censed, says:* Glory to the Holy and Consubstantial... *He sings:* Christ is risen... *(thrice), with its customary verses.* *Glory: Both now:* Christ is risen... *(thrice). And the Deacon intones: "Lord, I have cried". Resurrectional Stichera, 3, and of the Annunciation, 4, and of the Saint on 6. Glory: Both now: of the Feast, Tone 6:* The Archangel was sent... *If April 23, Glory to the Saint (see fol. 143), Both now: Theotokion in the tone of the Saint. Entrance, "O Joyful Light". Prokeimenon of Pascha:* Who is a god so great... *Readings of the Feast, 5. After this the Priest says:* And that we may be accounted worthy... *Gospel according to John, Pericope 65: "The same day at evening..." to the end: "...I will not believe." If it be on Monday or Tuesday evening: the Prokeimena of those days are read with their verses, and the Gospel is not read. Then the Litany: "Let us all say..." And: "Vouchsafe, O Lord..." "Let us complete our evening prayer..." At the Litiya, idiomelon stichera of the Feast, 3. Glory: Both now, Tone 2:* Gabriel proclaimed the good tidings... *If St. George: at the Litiya, an idiomelon sticheron of the Temple, and to the Saint...*  

...and to the Saint, from Tone 1, 4 stichera, and from Tone 3, 4 stichera. *Glory, Tone 5:* Spring hath shone forth... *Both now: Theotokion in the tone of the Saint. At the Aposticha: one Resurrectional sticheron, and the Paschal Stichera with their verses. Glory: of the Feast, Tone 4:* Today is joy... *Both now: of Pascha:* The Day of Resurrection... *And:* Christ is risen... *(thrice). Troparion of the Feast (thrice). If St. George: Troparion of the Saint (twice), and "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos" (once). And the blessing of the loaves, and distribution, and reading of the Feast.*  
*At Matins: The Priest having given the blessing, says:* Christ is risen... *(thrice), and its verses. Glory: Troparion of the Feast. Both now: the same. Then the Great Litany, Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, and reading of the Feast. Anabathmoi: 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon and Gospel of the Feast. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." (thrice). Psalm 50 is not read. But immediately: Glory: Through the intercessions of the Theotokos... Both now: the same. Then the stichos in Tone 6:* Declare His salvation from day to day... *And the Sticheron of the Feast:* The Archangel was sent... *Then the Priest:* Save, O God, Thy people... *Lord, have mercy (12 times). And after the exclamation, the Paschal Canon with its heirmos on 6, and of the Feast with heirmos on 8. Katavasia of the Annunciation, the heirmos sung by both choirs together. After Ode 3, Paschal Kontakion, verse of the Feast; if St. George, also his Ikos. Glory to the Saint (twice). Glory: Both now: Paschal Hypakoë:* Anticipating the dawn... *and litany. Again joy: After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, and the reading from Chrysostom's Commentary on John. At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable than the Cherubim", but the refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the earth proclaiming good tidings... *Svitylen: of Pascha, 1; and of the Feast, 2; if St. George, Svitylen of the Saint (twice). Glory: Both now: of Pascha. At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera, 3; and of the Feast, 3. And the Paschal Stichera with their verses. Glory: of the Feast, Tone 8:* Let the heavens be glad... *Both now: of Pascha, Tone 5:* The Day of Resurrection... *Christ is risen...* *(thrice). Glory: Both now: Troparion of the Feast. Litany, Catechetical Homily of the Feast, and Dismissal. The holy anointing oil is given to the brethren. And the Litiya outside the monastery.*  
*If St. George: We sing the Paschal Canon with the heirmos and its Theotokia on 8, and the Canon of the Saint, Tone 1, on 4. Melodic model: Tone 1, Podoben: "The Day of Resurrection" (Въскрⷵнїа дн҃ь): Katavasia: that same Heirmos, not observing the other.*  
*The Hours are according to Paschal custom.*  
*At the Divine Liturgy: Paschal Antiphons. After the Entrance, we say the verse:* In the congregations bless ye God... *Christ is risen...* *(thrice), and Troparion of the Feast. Glory: Kontakion of Pascha. Both now: Kontakion of the Feast. In place of the Trisagion:* As many as have been baptized into Christ... *Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel first of the Annunciation, then of the day, and in order the Divine Liturgy of Chrysostom. Communion verse of the day and of the Feast.*  
*Commemoration of the Holy Great-Martyr George: If it fall on one of the days of Bright Week: Concerning this see the Typikon chapter above on Great Friday, Chapter 104 (see fol. 196 and 143).*  
*If the patronal feast of any saint occur on any day from Bright Monday unto the First Sunday after Pascha: on those days we sing the service of the temple just as for St. George.*  
*Be it known that concerning how the order of the Annunciation is to be sung on the days of Holy Forty Days, during the weeks of Great Week, and on Holy Pascha, we have followed not any private opinion of our own, but the Typikon of the Holy Great Church. It is also well certified by having examined the Synaxarion of the venerable Studite Monastery and other great Typika of Jerusalem.[^511] Therefore let no one marvel at the changes made in the stichera, canons, readings, prokeimena, epistles, alleluia verses, gospels, and communion verses: for so it hath been commanded.*  
*When the Annunciation falls on any fasting day of the Holy Forty Days: then the service of the Feast precedes the daily order, because the fast is relaxed. Only on the paramon of the Feast, when it falls on a fasting day, do we sing the stichera first of the day, and then of the Annunciation, and the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts, out of honor for the Holy Forty Days, because it is a fast.*  
*In the days of Great Week, if the Annunciation occurs: at Vespers the Stichera of the day precede, and then of the Annunciation, on account of the Fast, as we said before regarding the paramon of the Feast. Likewise on Bright Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, if the Annunciation occurs, the daily service precedes the order of the Feast, on account of the transcendent glory of the bright days.*  
*Some say that on Great Friday, when the Annunciation or the commemoration of the Holy Great-Martyr George occurs, the Liturgy of Chrysostom should be celebrated, especially where the temple is dedicated to that feast: but since the Canons forbid it, and this is not customary, it ought not to be, unless there be for this the blessing of the Patriarch or Metropolitan in his own Metropolia, and of the whole synod of hierarchs, out of honor for the temple; for the patron saint of a temple in his own monastery is counted as a great feast.*  

## On Bright Monday: At Matins

*Before the beginning, the Paraecclesiarch, having lit the church lamps and candles, strikes the great iron simandron. And when they have assembled in the church, the Priest and the Deacon, having made the customary reverence to the Superior and entered into the sanctuary, vest in bright priestly vestments. The Priest, standing before the Holy Table with the censer, censes cruciformly, saying:* Blessed is our God, always, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. *And we:* Amen. *The Priest sings:* Christ is risen... *(thrice). Likewise also we sing:* Christ is risen... *(thrice), with its verses, as at Sunday Vespers (see fol. 186).*  
*(Note: Especially according to the Greek Typikon, these verses are taken from Psalm 117: "Give thanks unto the Lord..." which are also said at "God is the Lord". See after Vespers on Sunday described above, which was set down on fol. 187).*  
*Then the Great Litany, and after the exclamation the Superior or Priest begins:* The Day of Resurrection, let us be radiant...  
*It is fitting to know that after the Priest gives the blessing, while we sing "Christ is risen...", the Priest censes the Holy Table according to custom, and the entire sanctuary. At the beginning of the Canon, he goes forth and censes the church and the choirs according to their rank. After "Christ is risen...", it is not permitted for us to say, neither is it written to say "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" as on Sundays, nor Psalm 50. Then we sing the Canon: Heirmos twice, and the troparia on 6. After each ode, Katavasia: the Heirmos sung by both choirs together.*  
*Know that the Priest does not sing the heirmos on the other odes, as at the Resurrection service, nor are deacon's litanies intoned, except visibly after Odes 3, 6, and 9. After Ode 3, Hypakoë:* Anticipating the dawn... *and the Reading.[^512] (Note: In the Ninth Book, at the beginning, is the Homily on John, St. John Chrysostom's Commentary. From this day we begin this Book, and complete it unto All Saints; and then we begin the second). After Ode 6, Kontakion:* Though Thou didst descend into the grave... *The Ikos is not read, but we read the Prologue (Synaxarion). Then:* Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship... *(thrice), and:* Jesus having risen from the tomb... *with Glory: Both now:* *(thrice). And the remaining odes; the Svitylen (Exapostilarion) thrice.*  
*At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera on 4, Tone 2:*  
*Stichos:* Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to the multitude of His greatness. (Ps. 150:2)  
*Sticheron:* Every breath and all creation glorifies Thee, O Lord; for by the Cross Thou didst abolish death, that Thou mightest show unto the peoples Thy Resurrection from the dead, as the only Lover of mankind.  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet; praise Him with psaltery and harp. (Ps. 150:3)  
*Sticheron:* Let the Jews say: How did the soldiers lose the King they were guarding? Why did the stone not preserve the Rock of Life? Either let them produce Him that was buried, or worship Him that is risen, saying with us: Glory to the multitude of Thy compassions; O our Savior, glory to Thee!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and flute. (Ps. 150:4)  
*Sticheron:* Rejoice, ye peoples, and be glad! An Angel sat upon the stone of the tomb; he proclaimed good tidings unto us, saying: Christ is risen from the dead, the Savior of the world, and hath filled...  

...all things with fragrance! Rejoice, ye peoples, and be glad!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with well-tuned cymbals; praise Him with cymbals of jubilation. (Ps. 150:5)  
*Sticheron:* An Angel indeed brought the "Rejoice!" unto her that is Full of Grace before Thy Conception, O Lord; and an Angel rolled away the stone of Thy glorious tomb at Thy Resurrection. The one, in place of sorrow, uttered tokens of gladness; the other, in place of death, proclaimed unto us the Master, the Giver of Life. Therefore do we cry aloud unto Thee: O Benefactor of all, Lord, glory to Thee!  
*And the Paschal Stichera with their verses. "Christ is risen..." (thrice). Litany, and Dismissal with the Cross. And the First Hour, according to the order indicated (see fol. 184). (Note: In this manner the Matins service takes place throughout all Bright Week).*  
*It is fitting to know that we make a Procession outside the monastery today,[^513] carrying banners before us, and holding in our hands the Holy Gospel, the Precious Cross, and the icons of Christ's Resurrection, the All-Pure Theotokos, and the Venerable Wonderworkers. And singing: the Paschal Canon, with the Theotokia of the same Canon, two troparia on 8. And Katavasia: the Heirmos. Then, after Ode 9, the reading of the Gospel pericope, we say: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ" (thrice); then the sticheron: "Jesus having risen from the tomb" (thrice); then the Ode, and the rest of the Moleben (see fol. 181).*  
*At the Divine Liturgy, the Paschal Antiphons are sung without change, as indicated on Sunday of Pascha (see fol. 182).*  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5) *Stichos:* The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims His handiwork. (Ps. 18:2)  
*Epistle in the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 2 (Acts 1:12–17, 21–26):* In those days, the Apostles returned unto Jerusalem...  
*Alleluia, Tone 1:* The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord. (Ps. 88:6) *Stichos:* God is glorified in the counsel of the saints. (Ps. 88:8)  
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 2 (John 1:18–28):* No man hath seen God at any time...  
*Communion verse:* Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality. *We go forth into the Refectory with the Artos, as indicated (see fol. 189). In the Refectory there is consolation for the brethren. If there is no Divine Liturgy, see the rubric (see fol. 181).*  

## On Bright Monday: At Vespers

*The Priest having given the blessing, and begun:* Christ is risen... *(thrice). We likewise, with the customary verses (see fol. 186). Great Litany. "Lord, I have cried" in Tone 3. And we sing Resurrectional Stichera on 6, Tone 3:*  
*Sticheron:* By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, the dominion of death was destroyed, and the deception of the devil abolished; and the human race, saved by faith, ever offers a hymn unto Thee.  
*Sticheron:* All things have been enlightened by Thy Resurrection, O Lord, and Paradise opened again; and all creation, praising Thee, ever offers a hymn unto Thee.  
*Sticheron:* I glorify the power of the Father and the Son, and hymn the dominion of the Holy Spirit: undivided, uncreated Godhead, Consubstantial Trinity, reigning unto ages of ages.  
*Anatolian Sticheron:* We worship Thy Precious Cross, O Christ, and hymn and glorify Thy Resurrection; for by Thy wound we all were healed.  
*Sticheron:* Let us hymn the Savior Who was incarnate of the Virgin; for He was crucified for our sake, and rose on the third day, granting us great mercy.  
*Sticheron:* Christ, descending unto those in Hades, proclaimed the good tidings: Take courage, He said, now have I conquered! I am the Resurrection, I will lead you forth, having destroyed the gates of death!  
*Glory:*  
*Sticheron:* Standing unworthily in Thine all-pure house, we send up an evening hymn, crying out from the depths, O Christ God: O Thou Who didst enlighten the world by Thy third-day Resurrection...  

...by Thy Resurrection, deliver Thy people from the hand of Thine enemies, O Lover of mankind!  
*Both now: Theotokion (Dogmatikon of Tone 3):*  
How can we not marvel at thy God-manbearing childbearing, O All-Pure One? For without receiving trial of man, O all-blameless one, thou didst bear in the flesh without a father a Son Who before the ages was begotten of the Father without a mother, without undergoing alteration, or mixture, or division, but preserving intact the properties of both natures. Therefore, O Lady Virgin Mother, entreat Him that our souls may be saved, who in Orthodox manner confess thee to be the Theotokos.  
*Entrance with Censer and Candle, without the Gospel. "O Joyful Light". Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:[^514]* Our God is in Heaven and on earth; all things that He hath willed, He hath done. (Ps. 113:11)  
*Verse 1:* In the exodus of Israel out of Egypt, of the house of Jacob from a barbarian people. (Ps. 113:1)  
*Verse 2:* The sea saw it and fled; Jordan was driven back. (Ps. 113:3)  
*Verse 3:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back? (Ps. 113:5)  
*And again:* Our God is in Heaven and on earth; all things that He hath willed, He hath done.  
*Priest:* Let us all say... *and the other litanies:* Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening... *Then:* Let us complete our evening prayer... *and after the exclamation:*  
*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 3:*  
O Christ, Who by Thy Passion didst darken the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection didst enlighten all things, receive our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind.  
*Then the Paschal Stichera with their verses. And the Dismissal as indicated on Sunday at Vespers (see fol. 187). Likewise Compline (see fol. 180).*  
*(Note: The Priest performs the reservation of the Holy Lamb consecrated on Great and Holy Thursday for the sick at this Matins according to custom).[^515]*  

## On Bright Tuesday: At Matins

*The entire order takes place without change, as described above (see fol. 194).*  
*At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera on 4, Tone 3:*  
*Stichos:* Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to the multitude of His greatness. (Ps. 150:2)  
*Sticheron:* Come, all ye nations, understand the power of the awesome mystery: for Christ our Savior, the Word Who was in the beginning, was crucified for our sake and buried willingly, and rose from the dead to save all things; let us worship Him!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet; praise Him with psaltery and harp. (Ps. 150:3)  
*Sticheron:* Thy guards recounted all the wonders, O Lord; but the council of vanity filled their right hand with bribes, thinking to conceal Thy Resurrection, which the world glorifies: have mercy on us!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and flute. (Ps. 150:4)  
*Sticheron:* All things were filled with joy, having received the proof of the Resurrection. For Mary Magdalene came to the tomb, and found an Angel sitting upon the stone, gleaming with raiment, and saying: Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen, as He said, going before you into Galilee!  
*Stichos:* Let every breath praise the Lord. (Ps. 150:6)  
*Sticheron:* In Thy light, O Master, we shall see light, O Lover of mankind; for Thou didst rise from the dead, bestowing salvation upon the human race, that all creation may glorify...  

...may glorify Thee, the only sinless One: have mercy on us!  
*And of the Feast, Pascha sacred, with their verses. Then:* Christ is risen... *(thrice). Litany, and Dismissal. And the First Hour.*  
*At the Divine Liturgy, Paschal Antiphons. Prokeimenon: Song of the Theotokos (Tone 3):* My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior. (Luke 1:46–47) *Stichos:* For He hath regarded the lowliness of His handmaiden. (Luke 1:48)  
*Epistle in the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 4 (Acts 2:14–21):* In those days, Peter stood up with the eleven...  
*Alleluia, Tone 8:* Arise, O Lord, into Thy rest, Thou and the ark of Thy holiness. (Ps. 131:8) *Stichos:* The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David, and He will not turn from it. (Ps. 131:11)  
*Gospel according to Luke, Fifth Matins Gospel, Pericope 113 (Luke 24:12–35):[^516]* At that time, Peter arose and ran unto the sepulchre...  
*Communion verse:* Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality. *In the Refectory, consolation for the brethren.*  

## On Bright Tuesday: At Vespers

*The service is according to the custom set forth for the day (see fol. 187).*  
*"Lord, I have cried" in Tone 4. And we sing Resurrectional Stichera on 6, Tone 4:*  
*Sticheron:* Constantly worshipping Thy Life-Creating Cross, O Christ God, we glorify Thy third-day Resurrection; for thereby Thou hast renewed corrupted human nature, O Almighty One, and renewed for us the ascent into Heaven, as the only good One and Lover of mankind.  
*Sticheron:* Thou didst abolish the condemnation of the tree of disobedience, O Savior, being willingly nailed to the Tree of the Cross; and having descended into Hades, O Mighty One, Thou didst tear up the bonds of death as God; therefore do we worship Thy Resurrection from the dead, crying out with joy: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!  
*Sticheron:* Thou didst break down the gates of Hades, O Lord, and by Thy death didst destroy the kingdom of death, and delivered the human race from corruption, granting life and incorruption unto the world, and great mercy.  
*Anatolian Sticheron:* Come, ye peoples, let us hymn the Savior's third-day Resurrection, whereby we were delivered from the indissoluble bonds of Hades, and all received incorruption and life, crying: O Thou Who wast crucified, and buried, and didst rise, save us by Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind!  
*Sticheron:* Angels and men, O Savior, hymn Thy third-day Resurrection, whereby the ends of the universe were illumined, and we all were delivered from the servitude of the enemy, crying: O Life-Creating, Almighty Savior, save us by Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind!  
*Sticheron:* Thou hast shattered the bronze gates and crushed the iron bars, O Christ God, and hast raised up fallen mankind; therefore with one accord do we cry aloud: O Lord Who didst rise from the dead, glory to Thee!  
*Glory:*  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, Thy generation from the Father is timeless and co-eternal; Thine Incarnation from the Virgin is ineffable to men and beyond telling; and Thy descent into Hades is fearful to the devil and his angels; for having trampled down death, Thou didst rise on the third day, granting incorruption unto men, and great mercy.  
*Both now: Theotokion (Dogmatikon of Tone 4):*  
David the Prophet, who through thee became the forefather of God, in song proclaimed concerning thee to Him that has done great things for thee: *The Queen stood at Thy right hand.* For God, Who was well-pleased without a father to become incarnate of thee, showed thee forth as the Mother and mediatress of life, that He might recreate His own image which had been corrupted by passions, and having found the sheep that had strayed among the hills and was caught by the wolf, take it upon His shoulders and bring it to the Father, and according to His own will unite it with the Heavenly Powers, and that Christ, Who has great and rich mercy, may save the world, O Theotokos!  

*Entrance with Censer. "O Joyful Light". Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8:[^517]* With my voice have I cried unto the Lord, with my voice unto God, and He gave ear unto me. (Ps. 76:2)  
*Verse 1:* In the day of my trouble I sought God. (Ps. 76:3)  
*Verse 2:* My soul refused to be comforted. (Ps. 76:3)  
*Verse 3:* Thy way, O God, is in the sanctuary. (Ps. 76:14)  
*And again:* With my voice have I cried unto the Lord, with my voice unto God, and He gave ear unto me.  
*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 4:*  
Having ascended upon the Cross, Thou didst wipe out our ancestral curse; and having descended into Hades, Thou didst set free the eternal prisoners, granting incorruption unto the human race; therefore chanting we glorify Thy life-creating and saving Resurrection.  
*And the Paschal Stichera with their verses. And the rest as indicated before. And the Dismissal.*  

## On Bright Wednesday: At Matins

*The order of the entire service is as set forth for Monday (see fol. 194 and 190).*  
*At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera on 4, Tone 4:*  
*Stichos:* Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to the multitude of His greatness. (Ps. 150:2)  
*Sticheron:* O Thou Who didst endure crucifixion and death, and didst rise from the dead, Almighty Lord, glory to Thy Resurrection!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet; praise Him with psaltery and harp. (Ps. 150:3)  
*Sticheron:* By Thy Cross, O Christ, Thou didst deliver us from the ancient curse, and by Thy death Thou didst abolish the devil that tormented our nature, and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst fill all things with joy; therefore do we cry unto Thee: O Lord Who didst rise from the dead, glory to Thee!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and flute. (Ps. 150:4)  
*Sticheron:* By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, guide us into Thy truth, and deliver us from the snares of the enemy; O Thou Who didst rise from the dead, raise us up who have fallen into sin, stretching forth Thy hand, O Lord, Lover of mankind, through the prayers of Thy saints!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with strings and flute. (Ps. 150:4)  
*Sticheron:* Without separating Thyself from the Father's bosom, O Only-Begotten Word of God, Thou didst come upon earth for love of mankind, becoming man without alteration, and didst endure crucifixion and death in the flesh, being impassible in Thy Godhead; and having risen from the dead, Thou didst bestow immortality upon the human race, as the only Almighty One!  
*Then the Paschal Stichera with their verses. And the customary Dismissal. And the Procession outside the monastery with crosses. The Hours are according to Paschal custom.*  
*At the Divine Liturgy, Paschal Antiphons. Prokeimenon of the Theotokos, Tone 3:* I will make mention of Thy name in every generation and generation. (Ps. 44:18) *Stichos:* Give ear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear. (Ps. 44:11)  
*Epistle in the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 5 (Acts 2:22–36):* In those days, Peter said unto the people...  
*Alleluia, Tone 5:* My soul magnifies the Lord. *Stichos:* For behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.  
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 4 (John 1:35–51):[^518]* At that time, John stood, and two of his disciples...  
*Communion verse:* Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality. *In the Refectory, consolation for the brethren.*  

## On Bright Wednesday: At Vespers

*The service is as indicated on Sunday.*  
*"Lord, I have cried" in Tone 5. Resurrectional Stichera on 6, Tone 5:*  
*Sticheron:* By Thy Precious Cross, O Christ, Thou didst put the devil to shame, and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst blunt the sting of sin, and hast saved us from the gates of death; we glorify Thee, O Only-Begotten One!  
*Sticheron:* O Thou Who grantest resurrection unto the human race, as a sheep was He led to the slaughter...  

...led to the slaughter: the princes of Hades were affrighted at Him, and the gates of grief were lifted up; for Christ, the King of Glory, entered in, saying unto those in bonds: Go forth! and unto those in darkness: Show yourselves!  
*Sticheron:* A great wonder! The invisible Creator, having suffered in the flesh for love of mankind, rose from the dead! Come, kindreds of the nations, let us worship Him; for delivered from deception by His compassions, we have learned to hymn one God in three Persons!  
*Anatolian Sticheron:* We offer evening worship unto Thee, the Unwaning Light, Who at the end of the ages didst shine forth through the flesh as in a mirror upon the world, and didst descend even unto Hades, and didst destroy the darkness there, and by Thy Resurrection didst show forth light unto the nations: O Giver of Light, Lord, glory to Thee!  
*Sticheron:* Let us glorify Christ, the Author of our salvation; for when He rose from the dead, the world was saved from deception: the angelic choir rejoices, the deception of demons flees, fallen Adam arises, and the devil is abolished!  
*Sticheron:* They that were instructed by the guard of the lawless: Conceal the Resurrection of Christ, and receive the pieces of silver, and say that while we were sleeping the corpse was stolen from the tomb! Who hath seen, or who hath heard of a dead body ever being stolen, especially an anointed and naked one, leaving His burial wrappings in the tomb? Be not deceived, O Jews! Learn the sayings of the Prophets, and understand that He is truly the Redeemer of the world and the Almighty!  
*Glory:*  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, Who didst despoil Hades and trample down death, our Savior, Who didst enlighten the world by Thy Precious Cross: have mercy on us!  
*Both now: Theotokion (Dogmatikon of Tone 5):[^519]*  
In the Red Sea an image of the unwedded Bride was inscribed of old: there Moses, the divider of the water; here Gabriel, the minister of the wonder. Then Israel traversed the deep dryshod; now the Virgin hath given birth to Christ without seed. The sea remained impassable after the passing of Israel; the Blameless One remained incorrupt after the childbearing of Emmanuel. O Thou Who art, and Who wast before, and hast appeared as man, O God, have mercy on us!  
*Entrance with Censer. "O Joyful Light". And the Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:[^520]* Give ear, O God, unto my prayer, and despise not my supplication. (Ps. 54:2)  
*Verse 1:* Attend unto me, and hear me. (Ps. 54:3)  
*Verse 2:* For they have brought iniquity upon me. (Ps. 54:4)  
*Verse 3:* I cried unto God, and the Lord heard me: evening, and morning, and at noon. (Ps. 54:17–18)  
*And again:* Give ear, O God, unto my prayer, and despise not my supplication.  
*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 5:*  
Thee, the incarnate Savior Christ, Who wast not separated from Heaven, we magnify in voices of song; for Thou didst accept the Cross and death for our race, as the Lord and Lover of mankind; and having overthrown the gates of Hades, Thou didst rise on the third day, saving our souls.  
*And the Paschal Stichera with their verses. And the rest as indicated on Sunday at Vespers (see fol. 186). And the Dismissal.*  

## On Bright Thursday: At Matins

*The service is as indicated for Monday (see fol. 194).*  
*After "Christ is risen...", verses: "Give thanks unto the Lord..." (see fol. 187).*  
*At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera on 4, Tone 5:*  
*Stichos:* Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to the multitude of His greatness. (Ps. 150:2)  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, while the tomb was sealed by the lawless, Thou didst go forth from the tomb, even as Thou wast born of the Theotokos; Thy bodiless Angels understood not how Thou wast incarnate; the soldiers guarding Thee perceived not when Thou didst rise; for both were sealed to them that sought to examine: but the wonders were made manifest unto them that worship the mystery in faith; which do Thou grant unto us who sing, joy and great mercy!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with the sound of the trumpet; praise Him with psaltery and harp. (Ps. 150:3)  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, having shattered the eternal bars and broken the bonds asunder, Thou didst rise from the tomb, leaving behind Thy burial wrappings as a witness of Thy true third-day Burial; and Thou didst go before into Galilee, Thou Who wast guarded in the cave: great is Thy mercy, O Incomprehensible Savior, have mercy and save us!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and flute. (Ps. 150:4)  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, the women ran to the tomb to see Thee, O Christ, Who didst suffer for our sake; and having arrived, they found an Angel sitting upon the stone, which had been rolled away in fear, and he cried unto them, saying: The Lord is risen! Tell the disciples that He is risen from the dead, saving our souls!  
*Stichos:* Praise Him with strings and flute. (Ps. 150:4)  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, even as Thou didst go forth from the sealed tomb, so didst Thou enter in unto Thy disciples while the doors were shut, showing unto them the bodily passions which Thou didst endure, O long-suffering Savior; as of the seed of Judah Thou didst endure wounds; as the Son of God Thou didst free the world: great is Thy mercy, O Incomprehensible Savior, have mercy and save us!  
*Then the Paschal Stichera with their verses. And the customary Dismissal. Paschal Hours.*  
*At the Divine Liturgy, Paschal Antiphons. Prokeimenon, Tone 3:* Sing praises to our God, sing praises; sing praises unto our King, sing praises! (Ps. 46:7) *Stichos:* O clap your hands, all ye nations! (Ps. 46:2)  
*Epistle in the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 6 (Acts 3:1–8):* In those days, Peter and John went up together into the temple...  
*Alleluia, Tone 4:* Bend Thy bow, and prosper, and reign. (Ps. 44:5) *Stichos:* Thou hast loved righteousness and hated iniquity. (Ps. 44:8)  
*Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 50:[^521]* At that time, a certain man...  
*Communion verse:* Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality. *In the Refectory, consolation for the brethren.*  

## On Bright Thursday: At Vespers

*According to custom:* Christ is risen... *with its verses, as indicated on Sunday evening (see fol. 186).*  
*AND WE CHANT HERE, if the Superior so wills, the Office composed by the Lord Nikephoros Kallistos Xanthopoulos, in honor of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos, the Life-Giving Spring.[^522] For although we have not found such an Office in the Typika, nevertheless, out of love for the Most Holy Theotokos, it is placed at the end of this Book.*  
*"Lord, I have cried" in Tone 6. Resurrectional Stichera on 6, Tone 6:*  
*Sticheron:* Having the victory over Hades, O Christ, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, that Thou mightest raise with Thyself those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, being free among the dead, gushing forth life from Thine own Light: O Almighty Savior, have mercy on us!

*Sticheron:* Today Christ, having trampled down death, is risen even as He said, and hath bestowed joy upon the world, that we all, shouting aloud the hymn, may say thus: O Fountain of Life, Unapproachable Light, Almighty Savior, have mercy on us!  
*Sticheron:* Whither can we sinners flee from Thee, O Lord, Who art in all creation? In Heaven Thou dwellest; in Hades Thou didst trample down death; into the depths of the sea, there is Thy hand, O Master! Unto Thee do we flee, and falling down before Thee, we pray: O Thou Who didst rise from the dead, have mercy on us!  
*Anatolian Sticheron:* In Thy Cross do we glory, O Christ, and Thy Resurrection do we hymn and glorify; for Thou art our God, and beside Thee we know none other!  
*Sticheron:* Glory to Thy power, O Lord, for Thou didst abolish the dominion of him that held death; and Thou hast renewed us by Thy Cross, bestowing upon us life and incorruption!  
*Sticheron:* Ever blessing the Lord, we hymn His Resurrection; for having endured the crucifixion, by death He destroyed death.  
*Glory:*  
*Sticheron:* Thy Burial, O Lord, broke asunder the bonds of Hades and opened them; and Thy Resurrection from the dead enlightened the whole world: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!  
*Both now: Theotokion (Dogmatikon of Tone 6):*  
Who will not call thee blessed, O Most Holy Virgin? Who will not sing of thy childbearing without travail? For the Only-Begotten Son, Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, came forth from thee, pure Maiden, ineffably incarnate, being God by nature, and having become man by nature for our sake, not divided into two persons, but known in two natures without confusion: Him do thou entreat, pure and all-blessed Maiden, that our souls may be saved!  
*Entrance with Censer. "O Joyful Light". And the Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:[^523]* I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my foundation. (Ps. 17:2–3)  
*Verse 1:* My God is my helper, and I will hope in Him. (Ps. 17:3)  
*Verse 2:* Praising, I will call upon the Lord, and I shall be saved from mine enemies. (Ps. 17:4)  
*Verse 3:* He heard my voice from His holy temple. (Ps. 17:7)  
*And again:* I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my foundation. *Then the Litany:* Let us all say... *And:* "Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening..." *and the rest.*  
*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 6:*  
Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, the Angels hymn in the heavens; and make us on earth worthy to glorify Thee with a pure heart!  
*Then the Paschal Stichera with their verses. And the Dismissal.*  

## On Bright Friday: At Matins

*The service is according to the customary order previously shown, as we indicated (see fol. 196 and 187).*  
*At the Praises, Resurrectional Stichera on 4, Tone 6:*  
*Sticheron:* Thy Cross, O Lord, is life and resurrection unto Thy people; and trusting therein, we hymn Thee, our Risen God: have mercy on us!  
*Sticheron:* Thy Burial, O Master, opened Paradise unto the human race; and delivered from corruption, we hymn Thee, our Risen God: have mercy on us!  
*Sticheron:* With the Father and the Spirit let us hymn Christ, Who is risen from the dead; and let us cry out unto Him: Thou art our life and resurrection, have mercy on us!  
*Sticheron:* On the third day Thou didst rise from the tomb, O Christ, as it is written, raising our forefather with Thyself...  

...therefore doth the human race glorify Thee and hymn Thy Resurrection!  
*Then the Paschal Stichera with their verses. And the Dismissal. First Hour of the Paschal Hours.*  
*At the Divine Liturgy, Paschal Antiphons. Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world. (Ps. 18:5) *Stichos:* The heavens declare the glory of God. (Ps. 18:2)  
*Epistle in the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 7 (Acts 3:1–8):* In those days, Peter and John went up together...  
*Alleluia, Tone 8:* The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord. (Ps. 88:6) *Stichos:* God is glorified in the counsel of the saints. (Ps. 88:8)  
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 7 (John 2:12–22):* At that time, Jesus went down to Capernaum...  
*Communion verse:* Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality. *In the Refectory, consolation for the brethren.*  

## On Bright Friday: At Vespers

*After "Christ is risen...", litany. "Lord, I have cried" in Tone 8. And we set Resurrectional Stichera on 6, Tone 8:*  
*Sticheron:* An evening hymn and rational worship do we offer unto Thee, O Christ, for Thou didst deign to have mercy on us by Thy Resurrection!  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, O Lord, cast us not away from Thy presence, but deign to have mercy on us by Thy Resurrection!  
*Sticheron:* Rejoice, O holy Zion, Mother of the Churches, the dwelling of God! For thou didst first receive the remission of sins by the Resurrection!  
*Anatolian Sticheron:* The Word, begotten of God the Father before the ages, in the latter times was voluntarily incarnate of the unwedded Virgin, and endured death by crucifixion; and by His Resurrection He saved man, slain of old!  
*Sticheron:* We glorify Thy Resurrection from the dead, O Christ, whereby Thou didst set free the race of Adam from the tyranny of Hades, and didst grant unto the world, as God, eternal life and great mercy!  
*Sticheron:* Glory to Thee, O Christ Savior, Only-Begotten Son of God, Who wast nailed to the Cross, and didst rise from the tomb on the third day!  
*Glory:*  
*Sticheron:* We glorify Thee, O Lord, Who didst willingly endure crucifixion for our sake, and we worship Thee, O Almighty Savior: cast us not away from Thy presence, but hear and save us, by Thy Resurrection, O Lover of mankind!  
*Both now: Theotokion (Dogmatikon of Tone 8):*  
The King of Heaven, through love for mankind, appeared upon the earth and dwelt among men; for having taken flesh from a pure Virgin, and having come forth from her with what He assumed, He is one Son, twofold in nature, but not in hypostasis. Therefore, truly proclaiming Him to be perfect God and perfect man, we confess Christ our God: Whom do thou entreat, unwedded Mother, that our souls may be saved!  
*Entrance with Censer. "O Joyful Light". And the Great Prokeimenon, Tone 8:[^524]* Thou hast given an inheritance unto them that fear Thy Name, O Lord. (Ps. 60:6)  
*Verse 1:* From the ends of the earth have I cried unto Thee. (Ps. 60:3)  
*Verse 2:* I will be sheltered under the cover of Thy wings. (Ps. 60:5)  
*Verse 3:* So will I sing unto Thy Name, O Most High. (Ps. 60:9)  
*And again:* Thou hast given an inheritance unto them that fear Thy Name, O Lord. *Then the Litany:* Let us all say... *And:* "Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening..." *and the rest.*  
*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 8:*  
Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, O Jesus, Who camest down from Heaven; Thou camest unto death, O immortal Life; unto those in darkness, the true Light; unto the fallen, the Resurrection of all: our Enlightenment and Savior, glory to Thee!  
*Then the Paschal Stichera with their verses. "Christ is risen..." And the Dismissal.*  

## On Bright Saturday: At Matins

*The order of service is as previously set down for Monday (see fol. 194). After "Christ is risen...", the verses: "Give thanks unto the Lord..." (see fol. 187).*  
*At the Praises, "Let every breath praise the Lord." We set 4 stichera, Tone 8:*  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the judgment seat to be judged by Pilate, yet Thou didst not depart from the Throne, sitting together with the Father; and having risen from the dead, Thou didst free the world from the bondage of the alien, as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, though the Jews laid Thee in the tomb as dead, yet the soldiers guarded Thee as a sleeping King; and as the Treasure of Life, they sealed Thee with a seal: but Thou didst rise and bestow incorruption upon our souls!  
*Sticheron:* O Lord, Thou hast given us Thy Cross as a weapon against the devil; for he trembles and shakes, not being able to endure the sight of its power, for it raises the dead and hath abolished death. Therefore do we worship Thy Burial and Thy Rising!  
*Sticheron:* Thine Angel, O Lord, having proclaimed the Resurrection, struck fear into the guards, and cried unto the women, saying: Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is risen, being God, and hath granted life unto the universe!  
*Then the Paschal Stichera with their verses. "Christ is risen..." (thrice). Litany, and Dismissal (see fol. 194). And the First Hour, see there. Paschal Hours (see fol. 180).*  

*At the Divine Liturgy, Paschal Antiphons.*  
*Prokeimenon, Psalm 26, Tone 3:* The Lord is my light and my Savior; whom shall I fear? (Ps. 26:1) *Stichos:* The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid? (Ps. 26:1)  
*Epistle in the Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 8 (Acts 3:11–16):[^525]* In those days, as the lame man who was healed held...  
*Alleluia, Tone 8:* The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty. (Ps. 92:1) *Stichos:* For He hath established the world which shall not be shaken. (Ps. 92:1)  
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 7 (John 3:22–33):* At that time, Jesus and His disciples came...  
*Communion verse:* Receive ye the Body of Christ; taste ye of the fountain of immortality. *And the rest of the Liturgy. We process unto the Refectory as is customary on Bright Week (see fol. 189).*  
*In the Refectory, when the brethren are seated: The Cellarer, having broken into pieces the Artos, which was elevated throughout the entire week in place of the Panagia, brings it to the Superior; and the Superior takes the portion of the Panagia, and then distributes it to the brethren to eat before the customary meal, and so we consume it. First having said the "Our Father", and the customary blessing of the table, we sit down to eat. And the Reader begins the Reading. In the Refectory there is great consolation for the brethren.*  
*After rising from the table: "Christ is risen..." (thrice). And: "Blessed is God Who hath mercy upon us and nourishes us from our youth..." Then: "Glory to Thee, O Lord; glory to Thee, O King; glory to Thee, O Holy One." Glory: Both now: Lord, have mercy (thrice). Bless, O Lord. The Cellarer...*  

*Here the serving Deacon, taking the bread with three fingers of both hands, signs the Panagiarion with it cruciformly,[^526] saying, in place of the Great Name of the Holy Trinity:* Christ is risen! *(thrice). We answer likewise:* Truly He is risen! *Then holding the bread he says:* Most Holy Theotokos, help us! *We say:* Through her prayers, O Christ God, have mercy and save us! *And:* All generations call thee blessed. *And the Heirmos of Ode 9. Svitylen: with both of its Troparia. And again, this Svitylen. Then the Superior says, or if there is none, the Priest:* Unto the exceeding prayers of the all-blessed Lady: *We say:* Through her prayers! *And the Priest:* The merciful and compassionate Lord hath given food unto them that fear Him. *Then:* Christ is risen! *(thrice), not chanted. Trisagion; after "Our Father": Hypakoë:* Anticipating the dawn... *Glory: Both now: Kontakion:* Though Thou didst descend into the grave... *Lord, have mercy (twice). Bless, O Lord. And the Priest says the Dismissal:* Blessed is God Who hath mercy upon us and nourishes us from His rich gifts by His grace and love for mankind! *We say:* Amen. *And the customary forgiveness.*  
*And this we do until the Apodosis of the Feast of Pascha.*  
*It is fitting to know that at the 9th Hour, we sing the three psalms, as on every day: and we say the Troparion:* O Compassionate One, Thou didst descend from on high... *And the Kontakion:* Though Thou didst descend into the grave, O Immortal One...

---

# PART III: SUNDAYS AND WEEKS OF PASCHALTIDE (SAINT THOMAS THROUGH BLIND MAN)

## Sunday of Saint Thomas (Antipascha)
*Which is the Touching of the Holy and Glorious Apostle Thomas.*

*It is fitting to know that on this holy First Sunday, Antipascha, the Resurrectional service is not sung, but all of the Feast. And the service of the Menaion saint occurring on this day is sung at Compline on the same Sunday.*  
*(Note: On Saturday evening, at Small Vespers, we set 4 stichera. And we sing on "Lord, I have cried" and on "Vouchsafe, O Lord" from the festal prosomoia, doubling the feast. In this manner it is done at Small Vespers when the Octoechos is not sung at Vigils. Glory: Both now: if the Ecclesiarch wills to bless Kolyvo for the Saint, the idiomelon of the day).*  
*On "Lord, I have cried", Stichera, Tone 1:*  
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the Celestial Ranks" (Не́бны чинѡ):*  
Christ patiently endures being touched in His love for mankind, even as He endured the Cross before this and the unjust slaughter; and having risen on the third day from the tomb, He did not break the seals, and while the doors were shut He stood among the disciples, being almighty!  
The unbelief of Thomas confirms the world-saving rising from the treasuries of Hades of the God-man, the Word; with searching right hand he boldly touches the wounds of His hands and feet unto the assurance of the world!  
When the Apostles were gathered together in fear because of Thy Passion, O Word, and while the doors were locked, Thou didst suddenly come into their midst granting them peace...  

...and stretching forth unto Thomas to touch the precious wounds of Thy side!  
*Glory: Both now: Tone 2:*  
After Thy rising, O Lord, when Thy disciples were gathered together and the doors were shut, Thou didst stand in their midst, granting them peace; and Thomas, assured by the sight of Thy hands and side, confessed Thee to be Lord and God, Who savest those that hope in Thee, O Lover of mankind!  
*At the Aposticha, Prosomoia, Tone 2:*  
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме Еѵфра́ѳѡвъ):*  
With precious hymns, ye men, sing with the Angels unto Him Who is risen on the third day from the tomb and hath raised the world with Himself!  
*Stichos:* Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise thy God, O Zion. (Ps. 147:1)  
Thou didst appear unto Thine ordained Apostles, O Savior, while the doors were shut, renewing for us through them Thy Holy Spirit!  
*Stichos:* For He hath strengthened the bars of thy gates. (Ps. 147:2)  
Having seen Thee now, not with our eyes, but having believed in God with heartfelt love, we magnify Thee in hymns!  
*Glory: Both now: In the same Tone and Podoben:*  
Granting the Savior and Redeemer unto the world, grant also unto Thy people remission of debts, through the prayers of the all-pure, only Mother of God!  
*Then:* Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace, O Master... *Troparion, Tone 7:*  
While the tomb was sealed, Thou didst shine forth Life from the tomb, O Christ God; and while the doors were shut, Thou didst stand among the disciples, the Resurrection of all, renewing an upright spirit in us through them, according to Thy great mercy!  

*At Great Vespers:*  
*After the Priest gives the blessing, "Christ is risen..." (thrice). And immediately we sing Psalm 103, the Introductory Psalm, with chanting according to custom. Likewise the Stichology: the entire 1st Kathisma. On "Lord, I have cried", we set 10 stichera. Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 1:[^527]*  
*Sticheron:* On the eighth day of Thy rising, O Lord, Thou didst appear unto Thy disciples in the place where they were gathered, and having proclaimed unto them: Peace be unto you! Thou didst show Thy hands and Thy most pure side unto the disbelieving disciple; and he, having believed, cried out unto Thee: My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!  
*Sticheron:* While the doors were shut and the disciples were gathered together, Thou didst enter suddenly, O Almighty Jesus our God; and standing in their midst, having given peace, Thou didst fill them with the Holy Spirit, and didst command them to wait, and by no means to depart from Jerusalem, until they were clothed with power from on high.
