Intercede unceasingly, O Pure One, with Him Who came forth from thy womb, that they who sing of thee as the Mother of God may be delivered from the deception of the devil!

*Another Heirmos [Canon 2, Ode 3]:*
"Thy hymn-singers, O Mother of God, the living and abundant Fount, who have formed a spiritual choir, establish in Thy divine glory, vouchsafing them crowns of glory!"

*Troparia:*
"Lift up the Heavenly gates, behold, Christ the King of creation hath come, clothed in an earthly body!" the lowest Powers cried unto the highest!

Having sought out Adam, who was deceived by the serpent's deceit, O Christ, as having clothed Thyself in him, Thou didst ascend and sit at the right hand, as co-enthroned with the Father, while Angels sang praise unto Thee!

*Glory...*
The earth keeps festival and dances, and Heaven rejoices today at the Ascension of the Creator of creation, Who formerly by His will united what had been sundered!

*Theotokion:*
Having borne the Destroyer of death, the only immortal God, O Virgin all-immaculate Mother, pray Him ever to put to death my deadening passions and save me!

*Katavasia: "The womb of barrenness..."*

*On Thursday of the Ascension:*
"The womb of barrenness broke its bonds, and the shameful reproach of childlessness, by the sole prayer of the Prophetess Anna of old, who bore a contrite spirit unto the Mighty One and God of knowledge!"[^764]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of the Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^765]
Mounted upon the Heavenly Clouds, leaving peace unto those on earth, Thou didst ascend and sit down at the right hand of the Father, being co-essential with Him and the Spirit; for Thou didst appear in the flesh, yet didst remain unchangeable: therefore Thou awaitest the fulfillment of the end, coming to judge all the world! O Righteous Judge and Lord, spare our souls, granting remission of sins, as the merciful God, unto Thy servants! *Glory... both now and ever... the same. And the reading of the Feast.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
"I have heard the report of the power of Thy Cross, that paradise was opened thereby, and I cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"

*Troparia:*
Thou didst ascend in glory, O King of Angels, having sent the Comforter unto us from the Father; therefore we cry: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ!

As the Savior ascended unto the Father in the Flesh, the angelic hosts were amazed at Him and cried: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ!

The angelic Powers cried unto the higher ranks: "Lift up the gates for Christ our King, Whom we hymn together with the Father and the Spirit!"

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin bore, and knew not a mother's estate, yet is she a Mother, and hath remained a Virgin: hymning her, we cry: Rejoice, O Mother of God!

*Another Heirmos [Canon 2, Ode 4]:*
"He Who sits in glory upon the Throne of the Godhead, Jesus the most divine, hath come upon a light cloud, and with His incorrupt hand hath saved them that cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!"

*Troparia:*
Jesus the Giver of life, having taken those whom He loved, ascends unto the Mount of Olives, and blessed them, and borne upon a cloud reached the Father's bosom, which He had in no wise left!

The whole world keeps festival, both visible and invisible; the Angels dance with joy, and men unceasingly glorify the Ascension of Him Who in goodness united Himself unto us in the flesh!

Having destroyed the dominion of death as immortal, O Lord, Thou didst grant immortality unto all, O Lover of mankind; and Thou didst ascend in glory, while Thy honorable disciples beheld Thee, O all-powerful Jesus!

*Theotokion:*
Blessed was thy womb, O all-immaculate one, for thou wast accounted worthy ineffably to contain Him Who wondrously emptied the womb of hades: pray Him to save us who hymn thee!

*Katavasia:*
"O King of kings, Sole Word coming forth from the uncaused Father, Thine equal-in-power Spirit hast Thou truly sent unto the Apostles as Benefactor, unto them that sing: Glory to Thy dominion, O Lord!"[^766]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
"Rising early we cry unto Thee: O Lord, save us, for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know none other!"

*Troparia:*
Having filled all things with joy, O Merciful One, Thou didst come unto the Supernal Powers with the flesh!

The angelic Powers, beholding Thee taken up, cried aloud: "Lift up the gates for our King!"

The Apostles, beholding the Savior lifted up, cried with trembling unto our King: "Glory to Thee!"

*Theotokion:*
We hymn thee as Virgin after childbirth, O Mother of God, for thou didst bear God the Word in the flesh unto the world!

*Another Heirmos [Canon 2, Ode 5]:*
"All creation was amazed at thy divine glory: for thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in thy womb the God of all, and didst bear the timeless Son, granting salvation unto all that hymn thee!"

*Troparia:*
Having put death to death by Thy death, O Lord, taking those whom Thou didst love, Thou didst ascend unto the holy Mount of Olives, and from thence, O Christ, Thou didst mount up unto Thy Father, borne upon a cloud!

Strange is Thy Nativity, O Christ, and Thy Resurrection; strange and fearful is Thy divine Ascension from the Mountain, O Giver of life, which was foreshadowed by the four-horse ascent of Elijah...[^767]

...ascended, singing praise unto Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory...*
As the Apostles beheld, the Angels cried aloud: "Men of Galilee, why marvel ye at the Ascension of Christ the Giver of life? He shall come again in like manner upon earth to judge all the world, as the most righteous Judge!"

*Theotokion:*
Having preserved thee an incorrupt Virgin after childbirth, Christ ascends unto the Father, O Mother of God, Whom He did not leave, even though He received from thee flesh endowed with mind and soul, on account of His ineffable mercy!

*Katavasia [Ode 5]:*
"Receive the fire-breathing dew of the Spirit, the redeeming cleansing of sins, O radiant children of the Church; for now the Law hath gone forth from Zion, the tongue-of-fire grace of the Spirit!"[^768]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
"The deep encompassed me, and the whale became my grave; but I cried aloud unto Thee, O Lover of mankind, and Thy right hand saved me, O Lord!"

*Troparia:*
The Apostles leaped for joy, beholding today the Creator lifted up on high, and with hope in the Spirit and with fear they cried aloud: "Glory to Thy rising up!"

The Angels stood by, crying unto Christ's disciples: "In the same manner as ye have seen Christ ascending in the flesh, He shall come again as the righteous Judge of all!"

When the Heavenly Powers beheld Thee, our Savior, taken up on high with the body, they cried aloud, saying: "Great is Thy love for mankind, O Master!"

*Theotokion:*
The unburnt bush, the mountain, the living ladder, and the heavenly gate, do we worthily glorify, O glorious Mary, the boast of the Orthodox!

*Another Heirmos [Canon 2, Ode 6]:*
"This divine and all-honorable [feast of the Mother of God, come, let us clap our hands, glorifying God Who was born of her]..."

*Troparia:*
Let the clouds drop down eternal gladness upon us from above: for Christ, borne upon a cloud as upon the Cherubim, ascends today unto His Father!

Having appeared in the likeness of flesh, Thou didst gather into one what was formerly sundered, O Lover of mankind, and didst ascend unto the Heavens, O Merciful One, while Thy disciples beheld Thee!

"Why are the garments red of Him Who hath been united unto the coarseness of the flesh?" the holy Angels cried as they beheld Christ: "He bears the divine marks of the honorable Sufferings!"

*Glory... both now and ever... Theotokion:*
We sing of thy conception, O Maiden, we sing of thine ineffable childbirth, whereby we have been delivered, O Pure One, from corruption, affliction, and the grievous confinement of hades!

*Katavasia:*
"Christ our Master, Thou didst shine forth from the Virgin as cleansing and salvation for us, that as Thou didst snatch the Prophet Jonah from the belly of the sea-monster, so Thou mightest deliver from corruption the whole fallen race of Adam!"[^769]

*Kontakion, Tone 6:*
Having fulfilled the dispensation for our sake, and having united earthly things with heavenly, Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God, in no wise departing, but remaining inseparable, and crying unto them that love Thee: "I am with you, and no one is against you!"

*Ikos:*
Leaving the things of earth upon earth, and yielding dust unto ashes, come, let us be aroused, and lift up our eyes and minds on high; let us, mortal men, direct our sight and senses together toward the Heavenly Gates; let us imagine ourselves to be upon the Mount of Olives, and gaze upon the Redeemer borne upon clouds; for from thence the Lord ascended into the Heavens, and there He bestowed gifts of love upon His Apostles, comforting them as a Father, and strengthening them by guiding them as sons, and He said unto them: "I depart not from you: I am with you, and no one is against you!"

*And the reading of the Prologue. And after it, the verses:*

*Synaxarion for the Ascension of the Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ.*[^770]

*Verses:*
*Thou hast sat at the right hand of the Father, O Word,*  
*Bestowing firm faith upon the disciples whom Thou didst redeem.*

*On the same day, on Thursday of the Sixth Week after Pascha, we celebrate the Ascension of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ:*  
For while He was yet with the disciples before His Passion, He promised the coming of the All-Holy Spirit, saying: "It is expedient for you that I go away; for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come." And again: "When He comes, He will guide you into all truth." And after the Resurrection...

...from the dead, during forty days He appeared unto them not continuously, but from time to time, eating and drinking with them, and presenting His Resurrection more certainly; and finally He spoke many things concerning the Kingdom of God, commanding them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to remain there, awaiting the reception and coming of the Holy Spirit, and thereby to be baptized; for previously baptism was by water and only once from John, although later Saint Epiphanius of Cyprus related that John the Theologian baptized the Mother of God, and he in turn baptized the other Apostles.[^771] He commanded them to remain in Jerusalem, so that there the preaching of the Gospel might first be confirmed, lest going into foreign regions they might easily be slandered, and because it was necessary that they, like soldiers, should be equipped with the armor of the Spirit, and so go forth to battle against the enemies of Christ. But when the time of the Ascension arrived, He led them out unto the Mount of Olives, which is so called because it was planted with very many olive trees. And He spoke unto them concerning what had taken place in His preaching, and furthermore concerning His incomprehensible Kingdom in the future; and since He saw that they did not wish Him to depart, and His all-pure Mother was also present there, He appointed Angels for them, showing His ascent into the Heavens. And as they beheld, He was taken up from their midst, a cloud receiving Him, and so He was escorted by Angels, who commanded one another that the Heavenly Gates should be lifted up, and who marveled at the crimson of the blood of His flesh. He ascended and sat at the right hand of the Father, having deified the flesh, and—I dare to say—having shown it to be twofold together with the divine nature, on account of which we have been reconciled, the ancient enmity having been abolished. And the Angels in the appearance of men stood by the Apostles, saying: "Men of Galilee, why stand ye wondering, looking up into Heaven? This Jesus, Whom ye see with the flesh as God, shall come again with the flesh in like manner, yet not as formerly, in poverty and silence, but with great glory, as ye now behold Him escorted by Angels." Then the Apostles departed and returned from the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, being a distance of two thousand and forty paces, for this is a Sabbath day's journey; for so it was ordained by Moses, to walk that many paces on the Sabbath, because the Tabernacle of Witness was that many paces distant from the camp of the Israelites.[^772] For it was permitted for some to walk there on the Sabbath to worship, and in some measure to extend their walking, and therefore it was called a Sabbath day's journey. And some from this supposed that Christ's Ascension took place on a Sabbath, but they erred:

And having returned, the Apostles entered into the Upper Room, in which they had been staying, together with the Myrrh-bearing Women and the Mother of the Word, occupying themselves in fasting, prayers, and supplication, and awaiting the descent of the All-Holy Spirit, according to the promise. O Christ God, Who didst ascend in glory, have mercy upon us, now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
"Thou Who didst save the children that praised Thee in the fiery furnace: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

*Troparia:*
O Thou Who didst ascend upon clouds of light and didst save the world: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Having taken upon Thy shoulders our straying nature, O Savior, Thou didst ascend and bring it unto God the Father!

Thou Who didst ascend in the flesh unto the bodiless Father: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Having taken our nature which was slain by sin, Thou didst bring it, O Savior, unto Thine own Father!

Born of the Virgin, Thou hast made [man] divine: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another Heirmos [Canon 2, Ode 7]:*
"The godly youth did not worship [the creature rather than the Creator]..." (Incipit: *They did not serve:*)[^773]

*Troparia:*
As the Heavenly hosts, together with the Apostles, beheld Thee, Who art radiant Light, taken up from the earth above understanding beneath a cloud, O Lord, they sang praises, saying: "Blessed art Thou, O God!"

Let us all clap our hands with joy, let us praise His Ascension and shout aloud: "God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet, and hath sat down at the right hand, as co-enthroned with the Father unto the ages!"

Great Moses of old cried aloud: "Let the heavenly Angels worship Christ as He ascends, as King of all!" Unto Whom we cry: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord and God of our fathers!"

*Glory... both now and ever... Theotokion:*
O most marvelous wonders! How didst thou contain the uncontainable God, O full of grace, Who impoverished Himself in the flesh, and today hath ascended into heaven with great glory, and hath brought mankind to life!

*Katavasia:*
"The harmonious..."

..."song of the pipes ordered reverence for the lifeless image made of gold; but the radiant grace of the Comforter inspires us to cry aloud: O sole Trinity, equal in power, without beginning, blessed art Thou!"[^774]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
"The Son and God, Who was begotten of the Father before the ages, and in latter times became incarnate of the Virgin Mother: O ye priests, praise Him, ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Troparia:*
Christ the Giver of life, Who soared up to Heaven in glory in two natures and sits together with the Father: O ye priests, praise Him, ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

O Savior, Who hast delivered creation from the servitude of idols and presented it free unto Thine own Father: Thee we hymn, and Thee we supremely exalt unto all ages!

O Thou Who by Thy descent didst cast down the adversary, and by Thine ascent didst lift up mankind: O ye priests, praise Him, ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast revealed higher than the Cherubim, O pure Mother of God, having carried in thy womb Him Who is borne by them; Whom men glorify together with the bodiless hosts unto all ages!

*Another Heirmos [Canon 2, Ode 8]:*
"The godly youth [in the furnace]..." (Incipit: *The godly youth:*)

*Troparia:*
The spiritual beings appeared unto the Apostles at the Ascension and said: "Why stand ye gazing and wondering? This One Who ascends into the heavens shall come again to judge men on earth, being the only Judge!"

Let us give majesty unto God, let us shout an exclamation of praise, let us sing, let us dance, let us clap our hands: our God hath ascended into the Heavens from the earth, while Angels and Archangels sing praise unto Him as Master and Creator of all!

*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit:*
Our nature, which of old fell away, was taken up higher than the Angels and seated upon a divine Throne beyond comprehension: come, let us celebrate and cry aloud: "Bless the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Both now and ever...:*
Behold, thy Son, O Mother of God, having despoiled death by His Cross and risen on the third day, having appeared unto His disciples, hath ascended into the heavens: together with them worshipping Thee, we hymn and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Then: "We praise, bless, and worship the Lord." Katavasia:*
"The radiant image of the Threefold Principle looses the bonds and bedews the flame; the children sing, and all created nature blesses the only Savior and Creator as Benefactor."[^775]

*We do not sing the Magnificat.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
"Thee who beyond mind and speech didst ineffably give birth in time unto the timeless Mother of God, we the faithful magnify with one accord in songs!"

*Troparia:*
Beholding Thee, Christ God, the Redeemer of the world, divinely exalted, the Apostles with fear leaped for joy and magnified Thee!

Beholding Thy deified flesh on high, O Christ, the Angels said one to another: "Truly this is our God!"

Beholding Thee, Christ God, taken up upon a cloud, the bodiless Ranks cried aloud: "Lift up the gates for the King of glory!"

Thee Who didst descend even unto the lowest parts of the earth, and didst save man, and by Thine Ascension didst exalt him, do we magnify!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O Mother of God, Mother of Christ God: for beholding Him Whom thou didst bear being lifted up today from the earth, together with the Apostles thou didst magnify Him!

*Another Heirmos [Canon 2, Ode 9]:*
"Every earthborn man [leap for joy in spirit]..." (Incipit: *Every earthborn man:*)

*Refrain [Megalynarion]:*
*The Angels, beholding the ascent of the Master, were amazed at how He was taken up with glory from earth unto the highest!*[^776]

*Troparia:*
O gifts surpassing comprehension! O fearful mystery! For He Who rules over all, ascending from earth unto the heavenly realms, sent the Holy Spirit unto the disciples, Who enlightened...

...their mind and made them fiery by grace!

*Refrain [Megalynarion]:*
*The Angels, beholding the ascent of the Master, were amazed at how He was taken up with glory from earth unto the highest!*

*Troparia:*
"O company of disciples," the Lord said, "tarry ye in Jerusalem, and I will send down unto you the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, Who is co-enthroned with the Father and equally honored with Me, Whom ye behold being taken up and borne upon a radiant cloud!"

*Refrain [Megalynarion]:*
*The Angels, beholding the ascent of the Master, were amazed at how He was taken up with glory from earth unto the highest!*

The majesty of the Heavens was again taken up: He Who impoverished Himself in the flesh, and by sitting with the Father honored our fallen nature: let us celebrate and with one accord cry aloud, clapping our hands in joy!

*Theotokion:*
The Light that shone forth from Light, O all-immaculate one, shone forth from thee, and destroyed all the darkness of godlessness, and enlightened those sleeping in the night: therefore we all worthily bless thee ever unto the ages!

*Katavasia:*
"Rejoice, O Queen, the boast of mothers and virgins! For no eloquent, well-speaking mouth is capable of praising thee worthily, nor can any mind comprehend thy childbirth: therefore with one accord we glorify thee!"[^777]

*Then, the Exapostilarion thrice:*
While the disciples beheld Thee, Thou didst ascend, O Christ, to sit with the Father; the Angels ran ahead, crying aloud: "Lift up the gates, lift them up! For the King hath gone up unto the primal light of glory!"

*At the Praises, Let every breath praise the Lord. We set 4 Stichera.*

*Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́снымъ чино́мъ):*
O Angels, let us celebrate in the world for God Who is borne upon the Throne of glory, leaping for joy in song: "Holy art Thou, O Heavenly Father, and co-eternal Word; Holy art Thou also, O All-Holy Spirit!"

The leaders of the Angels, contemplating Thy strange Ascension, were in perplexity one with another: "What vision is this? He Who is seen as a man in form ascends in the flesh above the Heavens as God!"

The Galileans, beholding Thee, O Word, taken up in the flesh from the Mount of Olives, heard the Angels crying unto them: "Why stand ye gazing? He shall come again in the flesh in the same manner as ye have seen!"

*Glory... both now and ever... Tone 2:*
Thou wast born as Thou Thyself didst desire: (see fol. 346).[^778]

*Then the Great Doxology. Troparion of the Feast. Litany, and Dismissal.*

*The brethren are anointed with holy oil. And Compline according to the Studite rule in the Narthex. Troparion and Theotokion of the Feast, and the complete Dismissal.*[^779]

*AT THE DIVINE LITURGY. First Antiphon. Psalm 46 [LXX 46]. Tone 2. 4 verses:*
*Verse 1:* Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with the voice of rejoicing.  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Mother of God, Savior, save us.  
*Verse 2:* For the Lord most high is terrible; He is a great King over all the earth.  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Mother of God, Savior, save us.  
*Verse 3:* He hath subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet.  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Mother of God, Savior, save us.  
*Verse 4:* God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Mother of God, Savior, save us.  
*Glory... both now and ever...*  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Mother of God, Savior, save us.

*Second Antiphon. Psalm 47 [LXX 47]. Tone 2. Verse 1:*
*Verse 1:* Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, in His holy mountain.  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who didst ascend in glory, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
*Verse 2:* The mountains of Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who didst ascend in glory, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
*Verse 3:* God is known in her palaces for a refuge, when He helps her.  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who didst ascend in glory, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
*Verse 4:* For, lo, the kings of the earth were assembled, they came together.  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Son of God, Who didst ascend in glory, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.  
*Glory... both now and ever...* Only-begotten Son...

*Third Antiphon. Psalm 48 [LXX 48]. Tone 4. Verse 1:*
*Verse 1:* Give ear, all ye nations; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the earth.  
*Troparion, Tone 4:* Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God...  
*Verse 2:* Both earthborn and sons of men, rich and poor together.  
*Troparion:* Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God...  
*Verse 3:* My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart understanding.  
*Troparion:* Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God...  
*Verse 4:* I will incline mine ear to a parable, I will open my dark saying upon the harp.  
*Troparion:* Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God...

*Entrance Verse:*
God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.  
*Troparion:* Thou didst ascend in glory, O Christ our God...  
*Glory... both now and ever... Kontakion:* Having fulfilled the dispensation for our sake...  
*Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Be Thou exalted, O God, above the Heavens, and Thy glory over all the earth. *Verse:* My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready.  
*The Epistle from the Acts, Pericope 1:* The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus...[^780]  
*Alleluia, Tone 2:* God is gone up...

...God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet. *Verse:* Clap your hands, all ye nations.

*The Gospel from Luke, Resurrection Gospel 6, Pericope 114 [Luke 24:36-53].*[^781]

*Communion Hymn:*
God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet. Alleluia, thrice.

*On the same Thursday evening. We do not chant the Kathisma.*[^782]

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 6 Stichera: 3 of the Feast, and 3 from the Menaion.*

*Idiomel Stichera, Tone 4:*
O Thou Who didst ascend into the Heavens, whence also Thou hadst descended, leave us not orphans, O Lord: let Thy Spirit come, bringing peace unto the world; show unto the sons of men the works of Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

Thou didst ascend, O Christ, unto Thy Father Who is without beginning, not having departed from His uncircumscribed bosom; and the Powers that joined in praise did not receive a threefold praise, but recognized Thee, O Lord, as the only-begotten Son of the Father even after the Incarnation: in the multitude of Thy compassions, have mercy upon us!

Thine Angels, O Lord, said unto the Apostles: "Men of Galilee, why stand ye looking up into Heaven? This is Christ God Who hath ascended from you into Heaven; He shall come again in the same manner as ye have seen Him going into Heaven: serve Him in holiness and righteousness!"

*Glory... both now and ever... Tone 2:*
Thou wast born as Thou Thyself didst desire: (see fol. 346).[^783]

*Then the Entrance. Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*
Our God is in Heaven and on earth: He hath done all things whatsoever He pleased.  
*Verse 1:* When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from among a barbarous people.  
*Verse 2:* The sea saw it and fled: Jordan was driven back.  
*Verse 3:* What ailed thee, O thou sea, that thou fleddest, and thou Jordan, that thou wast driven back?  
*And again:* Our God is in Heaven and on earth: He hath done all things whatsoever He pleased.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Тридне́венъ):*
On account of Thine infinite compassion, O Christ, Thou wast born in the flesh of the Virgin, and of Thine own will didst endure the Crucifixion, and having risen from the tomb on the third day, O Most-bountiful One, Thou didst raise us up with Thyself and bring us to life!

*Verse:* Clap your hands, all ye nations.  
While Thy divine disciples beheld Thee taken up into Heaven, O Christ God, Thou wast taken up from earth unto Heaven, and didst promise them to send, O Giver of life, the Holy Spirit from the Father!

*Verse:* God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.  
The multitudes of Angels marvel at Thy strange and fearful entrance, O Jesus, King of all; and the higher powers cried aloud that the heavenly gates should be lifted up!

*Glory... both now and ever... Tone 6:*
On the holy mountains, beholding Thine Ascension: (see fol. 340).[^784]

*Then "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart." Trisagion. And after "Our Father": Troparion of the Feast:* Thou didst ascend in glory: (see fol. 344).[^785] *Litany, and Dismissal.*

*And the service of the Menaion for the Saint of the day we sing at Small Compline.*

*Rubric:*
The service of the grace-filled Feast is celebrated until the Friday before Pentecost, and is then taken leave of. And at Vespers on Thursday and at Matins on Friday, the entire service is celebrated without change, exactly as visibly appointed on the Feast itself.[^786]

## FRIDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK AFTER PASCHA

*AT MATINS. At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast, thrice.*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "While the stone was sealed" (Ка́мени зна́менану):*
Hades having been despoiled by Thee, O Giver of life, and the world having been enlightened by Thy Resurrection, Thou didst ascend in glory, O Savior, holding all things in Thy hand: therefore with the Angels we glorify Thee, O Almighty Lord: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ! Glory to Thy Kingdom! Glory to Thy compassion, O only Lover of mankind!  
*Glory... both now and ever... the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-beginningless" (Събезна́чалное Сло́во):*
Having descended from Heaven unto earthly men, and having raised up as God the Adamite nature lying below in the prison of hades, by Thine Ascension, O Christ, having gone up into the Heavens, Thou didst make it co-enthroned upon the Father's Throne, as the merciful Lover of mankind!  
*Glory... both now and ever... the same. And the reading of the Feast.*

*On Friday of the Sixth Week after Pascha:*

*Canon of the Feast with the Heirmos on 8, one by one alternating each day; from the Menaion on 4. But if it happen that there is a Saint on 6: we sing the Canon of the Feast with the Heirmos on 6, and for the Saint on 6. After Ode 3, Theotokion of the Saint, and Ikos, and his Sessional Hymn. Glory... both now and ever... of the Feast. After Ode 6: Kontakion of the Feast and Ikos. After Ode 9: Exapostilarion of the Feast; Glory... Exapostilarion of the Saint, if he have one; Both now and ever... of the Feast. But if not: Glory... both now and ever... of the Feast.*[^787]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast, Tone 2, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме Е҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Having fulfilled the Father's good pleasure, and having united what is above with what is below, Thou didst ascend in glory unto Him Who was first!

*Verse:* Clap your hands, all ye nations.  
A cloud of light received Thee on high, and the Angels with fear and trembling ministered unto Thy divine Ascension!

*Verse:* God is gone up with a shout.  
"I will not leave you orphans, whom I have gathered," the Lord said unto His friends, "but I will send unto you the All-Holy Spirit!"

*Glory... both now and ever... Tone 6:*
As Thou wast lifted up from the Mount of Olives, O Christ, the Powers beholding cried one unto another: "Who is this?" And they said unto them: "This is the strong and mighty One; this is the mighty in battle; this is truly the King of glory! And why are His garments red? He comes from Bozrah, which is of the flesh!" Then having sat down at the right hand of the Majesty, Thou hast sent down unto us the Holy Spirit, that He may guide and save our souls!

*Then, the First Hour. And the customary Dismissal.*

*AT THE BEATITUDES, THREE-ODE CANON. Tone 4.*

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
"The ungodly shall not see [Thy glory, O Christ]..."

*Troparia:*
In Thine ascent from earth unto Heaven, Thou wast in no wise separated from the Father, and being united, O Master, also with the Spirit, Thou didst send down the Comforter unto the disciples from Heaven!

When the Ranks of the Bodiless Powers beheld Thee, O Jesus, ascended with the flesh into Heaven, they marvelled with joy at Thy great compassion toward men, O Lord!

Having seated our corrupted nature upon the Father's Throne, O Master, Thou didst adorn it, O Lord, with which Thou shalt come to judge the world, O Almighty One!

*Theotokion:*
Let us honor spiritually the honorable and all-pure Beauty of Jacob, and being adorned with divine virtues, let us piously sing praise unto the Mother of our God!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
"O Redeemer of all..."

*Troparia:*
Borne upon the Cherubim's shoulders, Thou didst ascend in glory, O Lord, while Thy disciples beheld Thee and unceasingly cried aloud: "All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

Having broken down the enmity of the middle wall of partition, Thou didst reconcile the dead unto Thy Father, and having ascended, O Word without beginning, Thou didst bring with Thyself the flesh which Thou didst assume, above Principalities and Powers!

Blessing the disciples, Thou didst ascend on high, O Christ, having sent the Comforter unto them, who with one accord cry aloud: "All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Theotokion:*
The common cleansing-place for the faithful, the ready help for men, and the bridge leading all unto salvation unto the Creator, do we glorify as the Mother of God!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
"Eve indeed by the disease [of disobedience]..."

*Troparia:*
From the Mount of Olives, O Christ, a cloud received Thee as a throne, while all Thy divine disciples beheld, and with trembling unceasingly cried unto Thee: "Leave not orphans those whom Thou hast loved on account of Thine ineffable compassion!"

"Why stand ye looking upon this fearful ascent?" the Angels of old said unto the divine Apostles: "In the same manner as ye see Him ascending, He shall come again upon earth to judge all with ineffable glory!"

Thou didst descend at first incorporeally, but Thou didst ascend bearing the flesh which Thou hadst assumed; and with fear the heavenly gates were opened unto Thee, and the spiritual heavenly hosts, beholding, were amazed, saying: "Glory to Thy descent, O Master, for our sake!"

*Glory... both now and ever... Theotokion:*
Assembled together with the divine disciples, O All-Pure One, and beholding Him Whom thou didst bear being lifted up from the earth, thou didst cry aloud: "Ascending unto the Father Who is without beginning, O Lord Who fillest all things with Thy glory, Thou art supremely glorified, the only Lord!"

*On Friday Evening at "Lord, I have cried," we set 6 Stichera: 3 of the Feast, and 3 from the Menaion. Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ есѝ знаме́нїе):*
Thou didst suffer as man, being impassible in Thy Godhead, and didst rise on the third day, having despoiled death and raised up with Thyself all who were corrupted by transgression; Thou didst ascend, O Christ, unto the Father, having promised to send the Comforter unto Thy sacred Apostles, O Jesus Almighty, Savior of our souls!

"Why stand ye gazing up into Heaven?" the Angels visible as men said unto the initiates of the Word: "This One Whom ye see being taken up upon a radiant cloud shall come again in the same manner as ye have seen Him, to judge the world, as it is written: go ye therefore and do all that hath been spoken!"

After Thine ineffable rising from the tomb, O Almighty Lord, having taken those whom Thou didst love, Thou didst lead them out as far as Bethany, O Word; and having come unto the Mount of Olives, having blessed them, Thou didst ascend in such wise while the Angels submitted unto Thee, O Jesus Almighty, Savior of our souls!

*Glory... both now and ever... Tone 6:*
Thou didst ascend in glory upon the Mount of Olives: (see fol. 342).[^788]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме Е҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
The Angels cried unto the wise Apostles: "O men of Galilee, in the same manner as ye have seen Him, He shall come again!"

*Verse:* Clap your hands, all ye nations.  
Thy disciples came down from Olivet in joy, O Word, crying aloud and glorifying Thy divine Ascension!

*Verse:* God is gone up with a shout.  
In deed unto the disciples, as Thou didst give command, O Word, Thou hast sent Thy divine and Holy Spirit, and hast enlightened them!

*Glory... both now and ever... Tone 4:*
When Thou didst come unto the Mountain, O Christ: (see fol. 341).[^789]

*Then "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart." Trisagion, and after "Our Father": Troparion of the Feast, and Dismissal.*

## SATURDAY OF THE SIXTH WEEK AFTER PASCHA

*AT MATINS. At "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast, thrice.*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "While the stone was sealed" (Ка́мени зна́менану):*
Thou didst come down incorporeally from Heaven unto the earth, O Word, that Thou mightest raise up all with Thyself; and Thou didst ascend with the flesh, O Christ: therefore the heavenly Powers cried aloud, saying: "Glory to Thy descent, O Savior! Glory to Thine Ascension! Glory to Thy Dispensation, O only Lover of mankind!"  
*Glory... both now and ever... the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Я҆ви́лся дне́сь):*
Thou hast mounted up again unto Thine own Father, O Creator; leave not Thy servants orphans! When the disciples beheld Thee being lifted up, they cried aloud, O Lover of mankind!  
*Glory... both now and ever... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast on 8, and from the Menaion on 4.*

*On Saturday of the Sixth Week after Pascha:*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Angelic hosts" (А҆́ггельскїя Си́лы):*
That Thou mightest raise up fallen me, who am common upon the earth, Thou didst come unto the earth, and having taken me, Thou dost unite me hence, and dost enlighten me with the Light of the Father, having in Thine Ascension cast down him who of old cast me down: I sing, O Master, of the incomprehensible depth of Thy love for mankind!

*Verse:* Clap your hands, all ye nations.  
Leap for joy, Adam, and rejoice together, Eve! For in that corruptible garments ye were clothed of old in Paradise, hoping for incorruption: these the Creator received, ineffably transformed unto incorruption, and honored today with Ascension and the Father's Light!

*Verse:* God is gone up with a shout.  
Having trampled the tyrant, the apostate enemy, by divine power, having clothed Thyself in my nature inalterably, unconfusedly, and indivisibly, He ran up again with it unto the Father! Let the heretics be put to shame for their grievous raging, while we, the godly-minded faithful, magnify Him!

*Glory... both now and ever... Tone 4:*
Lord, the mystery which was from the ages: (see fol. 342).[^790]

*Then the First Hour, and the customary Dismissal.*

*AT THE BEATITUDES, FOUR-ODE CANON. Tone 4.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
"I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord..."

*Troparia:*
Having filled the earth with Thy glory, Thou didst ascend with ineffable glory, and didst bring unto the Father the flesh in which Thou didst clothe Thyself for our sake in Thy compassion; and the heavenly Powers sang praise unto Thee, O only Lover of mankind!

"Lift up, ye heavenly gates, and receive God the flesh-bearer!" cried the spiritual Powers in submission: "Who is this Whom ye proclaim? And unceasingly offer praise unto Him as Creator of all!"

Beholding the fearful ascent of the Word, the disciples cried aloud: "Send down unto us the All-Holy Spirit, and leave not orphans Thy servants, who know Thee to be true God and sinless man!"

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast deified human nature, having been ineffably born of the Virgin, O Word co-essential with the Father, and Thou didst ascend in glory: grant peace unto Thy disciples, and abundant mercy unto the world!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
"The Hebrew children [in the furnace]..."

*Troparia:*
Having endured passion and death, and having risen on the third day as Thou didst say, Thou didst ascend unto the Heavenly realms, while Thy disciples sang unto Thee: "O Lord God, blessed art Thou unto the ages!"

"Send down unto us the All-Holy Spirit, as Thou didst promise, O Merciful One," the wise disciples cried aloud, "Who makes wise and gives understanding unto all the faithful unto the ages!"

Clap your hands, all ye nations, and shout unto God in gladness: Christ hath ascended, and sits in glory at the right hand, as co-enthroned with the Father, unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Without leaving the Father's bosom, the Word became incarnate in thy bosom, delivering us, O Virgin, who sing: "O Lord God, blessed art Thou unto the ages!"

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
"Sevenfold [the tyrant of Babylon in his rage kindled the furnace]..."

*Troparia:*
Transforming beyond mind into another nature, as it is written, and by His sufferings clearly granting impassibility unto all the faithful: He ascends from the earth, now to appear before the Father's face, while Angels, Archangels, Thrones, and Dominions glorify Him unto all ages!

White-robed Angels stood by the Apostles as they were bewildered at the new vision of Thine Ascension, O Word co-beginningless with the Father, saying: "Why look ye thus on high? This same Jesus shall come again to judge the world, in the same manner as ye see Him!"

Having accomplished all things, O Lord, as immutable God, Thou didst mount up unto the heavenly realms with the flesh, while the angelic Powers submitted, and the disciples joyfully cried unto Thee and glorified Thee with fear: "O ye priests, praise Him, ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Mother of God, cleanse the wounds of my soul and the sores of my sin, pouring forth streams from the side of Him Who was born of thee, cleansing me with the flows from Him: for unto thee I cry, unto thee I fall down, and thee I invoke, the only deliverer!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
"Every ear was terrified [at the ineffable condescension of God]..."

*Troparia:*
Lift up the spiritual gates, ye heavenly powers! Our King hath come, having received an abhorred nature, and having become man, He entered unto His Father, accomplishing strange and most glorious wonders! Sing with understanding, all ye people, shout aloud unto God Who hath wrought most glorious deeds, Who hath ascended unto the heavenly realms, and sent down the Holy Spirit unto the Apostles, enlightening us who glorify His Godhead!

*Glory...*
The burial bound hades, and the Resurrection was granted unto men; and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst greatly illuminate heavenly things, O Christ, the only unchangeable and almighty One, Giver of good things and our Savior!

*Both now and ever... Theotokion:*
The voice of Gabriel we bring unto thee with all the Angels: Rejoice, O longed-for Palace of the King! Rejoice, thou who hast united earthly things with heavenly! On account of whom being saved, we bless thee, the pure Mother of God!

*At the Divine Liturgy: Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye righteous. *Verse:* Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven. *The Epistle from the Acts, Pericope 43 [Acts 20:7-12]:* In those days, when the disciples came together to break bread... *Alleluia:* Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken unto Thyself, O Lord. *The Gospel from John, Pericope 48 [John 14:10-21]:* The Lord said unto His disciples: I am in the Father, and the Father in Me... *Communion Hymn:* Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous. Alleluia.[^791]

## SEVENTH SUNDAY OF PASCHA: OF THE THREE HUNDRED AND EIGHTEEN HOLY FATHERS OF THE FIRST ECUMENICAL COUNCIL IN NICAEA

*On Saturday evening, we celebrate the customary All-Night Vigil.*

*At Small Vespers, in the Octoechos according to custom.*

*At the Aposticha: one Resurrection Sticheron, Tone 6:* Thy Resurrection, O Christ our Savior... *Then of the Ascension, Tone 2, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме Е҆ѵфра́ѳовъ): and the rest as written at Small Vespers of the Ascension.*

*AT GREAT VESPERS. After the customary Psalm.*

*We chant the Kathisma: "Blessed is the man," the entire kathisma.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 Stichera: and we sing 3 Resurrectional, 3 of the Ascension, and 4 of the Holy Fathers.*

*Resurrection Stichera, Tone 6, Idiomel:*
Holding victory over hades, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, O Christ, that Thou mightest raise up with Thyself those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, being free among the dead, pouring forth life from Thine own light: O Almighty Savior, have mercy upon us!

Today Christ, having trampled death, hath risen as He said, and granted rejoicing unto the world, that we all, shouting aloud, may speak thus in hymns: "O Fount of life, unapproachable Light, Almighty Savior, have mercy upon us!"

Whither shall we sinners flee from Thee, O Lord, Who art in all creation? In Heaven Thou dwellest; in hades Thou hast trampled death; in the depths of the sea, there is Thy hand, O Master...

...O Master! Unto Thee we flee, and falling down before Thee we pray: O Thou Who didst rise from the dead, have mercy upon us!

*Stichera of the Ascension, Tone 6:*
The Lord ascended into the Heavens, that He might send the Comforter unto the world. The Heavens prepared His Throne; the clouds His ascent; the Angels marvel, beholding a man higher than themselves. The Father awaits Him Whom He holds co-eternal in His bosom; and the All-Holy Spirit commands all His Angels: "Lift up your gates, ye princes; clap your hands, all ye nations, for Christ hath ascended whither He was before!"

At Thine Ascension, O Lord, the Cherubim were amazed, beholding Thee, God, ascending upon the clouds, Who sittest upon them; and we glorify Thee, for good is Thy mercy: Glory to Thee!

On the holy mountains, beholding Thine Ascension, O Christ, the Brightness of the Father's glory, we hymn the radiant appearance of Thy countenance; we worship Thy Passion, we honor Thy Resurrection, glorifying Thy glorious Ascension: have mercy upon us!

*Stichera of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Неѿча́емая):*[^792]
Thou wast begotten from the womb before the morning star, without mother from the Father before the ages, even though Arius glorifies Thee as a creature and not God, with audacity foolishly mingling Thee the Creator with created matter, laying up for himself the fuel of eternal fire! But the Council in Nicaea proclaimed Thee, O Lord, the Son of God, co-enthroned with the Father and the Spirit!

[Woodcut engraving depicting the Vision of Saint Peter of Alexandria: the Child Jesus stands upon an altar beneath a ciborium, wearing a torn tunic, while Saint Peter of Alexandria, vested as an archbishop in sakkos, omophorion, and mitre, raises his hands in sorrowful wonder. Inscription above: "Saint Peter of Alexandria beheld Christ in a torn robe, and said unto Him: 'Lord, who hath torn Thy robe?' 'Arius,' He said, 'the divider of the Trinity; receive him not into communion!'" Inscription above the hierarch: "Saint Peter".][^793]

*Troparia:*
"Who hath torn Thy robe, O Savior?" "Arius," Thou didst say, "who severed the equally-honored Principle of the Trinity into divisions: he denied that Thou art One of the Trinity; he also teaches Nestorius not to call her the Mother of God! But the Council in Nicaea confessed Thee, O Lord, the Son of God, co-enthroned with the Father and the Spirit!"

Arius, who hated to see the light, falls into the pit of sin, and his bowels are torn asunder by a divine hook, violently surrendering his substance and soul, becoming another Judas in disposition and manner! But the Council in Nicaea proclaimed Thee, O Lord, the Son of God, co-enthroned with the Father and the Spirit!

Senseless Arius severed the all-pure Monarchy of the Trinity into three unlawful and disparate entities. Therefore the God-bearing Fathers, having assembled eagerly, inflamed with zeal like Elijah the Tishbite, cut down with the spiritual sword the shameful teaching...

...that taught the blasphemer, even as the Spirit declared:[^794]

*Glory... Tone 6:*
Today let us praise the God-bearing Fathers, the mystic trumpets of the Spirit, who sang in the midst of the Church the harmonized tune of theology, proclaiming the changeless Trinity, one in essence and Godhead, who cast down Arius and are champions of the Orthodox, ever praying to the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

*Now and ever... Theotokion, the same Tone:*
Who would not call thee blessed, O all-holy Virgin? *Look to leaf 116.*[^795]

*Then the Entrance. The Prokeimenon of the day.*

*Reading from Genesis (14:14–20):*[^796]
Abram, having heard that Lot his brother's son was taken captive, numbered his own home-born servants, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued after them unto Dan. And he fell upon them by night, he and his servants, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah, which is on the left of Damascus. And he brought back all the cavalry of Sodom, and he brought back Lot his brother's son, and all his goods, and the women, and the people. And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after he returned from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer, and of the kings that were with him, to the valley of Shaveh, which was the king's dale. And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine; and he was the priest of the Most High God. And he blessed Abram, and said: "Blessed be Abram of the Most High God, who created heaven and earth; and blessed be the Most High God, who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hands!"

*Reading from Deuteronomy (1:8–17):*[^797]
In those days, Moses said unto the sons of Israel: "The Lord God saith: Behold, I have delivered the land before your face; go ye in and inherit the land which I sware unto your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give it to them and to their seed after them. And I spake unto you at that time, saying: I cannot bear you alone. The Lord our God hath multiplied you, and behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude. The Lord God of our fathers make you a thousand times so many more as ye are, and bless you, even as He hath spoken unto you! And I took of you wise men, known and prudent, and made them rulers over you, rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, and rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens, and officers to your judges. And I commanded your judges at that time, saying: Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; ye shall judge small and great alike; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's!"

*Reading from Deuteronomy (10:14–21):*[^798]
In those days, Moses said unto the sons of Israel: "Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord thy God, the earth also, with all that therein is. Only the Lord chose your fathers to love them in truth, and chose their seed after them, even you above all nations, this day. Circumcise therefore the hardness of your heart, and be no more stiff-necked. For the Lord our God, He is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, who regards not persons, nor accepts a bribe. He executs the judgment of the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, and loves the stranger, in giving him...

...food and raiment. Love ye therefore the stranger, for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. Thou [O Israel] shalt fear the Lord thy God; Him only shalt thou serve, and to Him shalt thou cleave, and swear by His Name. He is thy praise, and He is thy God, that hath done for thee these great and glorious things, which thine eyes have seen."

*At the Litiya, Stichera of the Saint of the temple. And of the Ascension, idiomelon:*
*Tone 1:*
Ascending into the heavens, whence also Thou didst descend... *Look to leaf 344.*[^799]

*Glory... Of the Fathers, Tone 3:*
Ye were exact guardians of the apostolic traditions, O holy Fathers! For having preached the consubstantial Holy Trinity in an Orthodox manner, ye synodically cast down the blasphemy of Arius; and with him having refuted Macedonius the Spirit-fighter, ye condemned Nestorius, Eutyches, and Dioscorus, Sabellius also, and Severus the headless![^800] Entreat that we may be delivered from their delusion, praying that our life may be kept undefiled in the faith!

*Now and ever... Of the Feast, Tone 5:*
O Lord, while the angels marveled as Thou wast borne aloft, whence Thou hadst never been separated, the hosts of angels and of all the bodiless powers cried aloud with joy unto the celestial hosts: "Lift up your gates, ye princes, and the King of glory shall enter in!" For the Cherubic throne received Thee with Thy flesh; O Lord, glory to Thee!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Resurrection, Tone 6:*
Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, the angels hymn in the heavens; make us also worthy on earth to glorify Thee with a pure heart!

*Other Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́мꙋ є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^801]
*Verse: The Lord is King, He is clothed with majesty!*
Thou hast shattered the gates of brass and crushed the bars of hades, as almighty God, and hast raised up fallen mankind; therefore we also cry aloud: O Thou who art risen from the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, which shall not be shaken.*
Christ, desiring to deliver us from ancient corruption, is nailed to the Cross and laid in the tomb; whom the myrrh-bearing women sought with tears, weeping and saying: "Woe unto us, O Savior of all! How didst Thou desire to dwell in a tomb, O Thou who givest life to all? How wast Thou stolen? How wast Thou transferred? What place hath hidden Thy life-bearing body? But, O Master, even as Thou didst promise us, appear and stay our weeping tears!" And while they wept, an angel cried unto them: "Cease from weeping, say unto the Apostles that the Lord is risen, granting purification and great mercy unto the world!"

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days!*
Thou wast crucified as Thou didst will, O Christ, and by Thy burial Thou didst despoil death, rising on the third day as God with glory, granting unending life and great mercy unto the world!

*Glory... Of the Fathers, Tone 4:*
Today let us who are Orthodox faithfully and piously celebrate the memorial of the assembly of the God-bearing Fathers, gathered from the whole inhabited world in the splendid city of Nicaea; for they piously destroyed the godless decree of fierce Arius and synodically expelled him from the Catholic Church; and clearly taught all to confess the Son of God as consubstantial and co-eternal, existing before the ages, setting this forth explicitly and piously in the Symbol of Faith; therefore we also, following their divine decrees, believing truly, worship the Son with the Father and the all-holy Spirit, in one Godhead, a consubstantial Trinity!

*Now and ever... Of the Feast, the same Tone:*
O Lord, having accomplished the mystery hidden from ages and from generations, as Thou art good, Thou didst come with Thy disciples unto the Mount of Olives, having her that bore Thee, the Creator and Maker of all; for it was fitting that she who suffered maternally more than all at Thy Passion should also enjoy exceeding great joy at the glory of Thy flesh; and partaking thereof at Thine ascension into the heavens, O Master, we glorify Thy great mercies wrought upon us!

*Then: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart... Trisagion: and after Our Father, if there be a Vigil:*
*Troparion of the Fathers twice, and of the Feast once, and blessing of the loaves; and a reading from the Acts of the Holy Apostles. But if not, then Great Vespers concludes according to custom.*

*Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, Tone 6:*
The angelic powers were upon Thy tomb, and the guards became as dead men; and Mary stood at the grave, seeking Thine all-pure body. Thou didst despoil hades, yet wast not tempted by it; Thou didst meet the Virgin, granting life: O Thou who art risen from the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Of the Fathers, Tone 8:*
Most glorious art Thou, O Christ our God, who hast established our fathers as beacons upon the earth, and through them hast guided us all to the true faith: O Most Merciful One, glory to Thee!

*Now and ever... Troparion of the Ascension: Thou hast ascended in glory, O Christ our God... Look to leaf 344.*[^802]

*And the customary dismissal of Great Vespers.*

*Chapter 120. Mark this well:*[^803]
*Be it known that when the Paschal Key is 2, then on May 8 the Commemoration of the Holy Apostle John the Theologian falls on this Seventh Sunday of the Holy Fathers.*

*And his service is sung together with the Sunday service. The service of the Feast of the Ascension is omitted. And there is sung the service of the Resurrection, and of the Theologian, and of the Holy Fathers.*
*On Saturday evening at Small Vespers: At Lord, I have cried, Stichera of the Resurrection for 4. Glory... Of the Apostle, Tone 2: "Son of Thunder..." Now and ever... Theotokion of Tone 1, as is appointed for Small Vespers. At the Aposticha, one sticheron of the Resurrection. Then the Aposticha of the Apostle from Great Vespers, with their verses. Glory... Of the Apostle. Now and ever... Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint. After the Trisagion, Troparion of the Resurrection, and of the Fathers; Glory... Of the Apostle; Now and ever... Of the Feast. Little Litany, and dismissal.*

*At Great Vespers, as customary: At Lord, I have cried, Stichera, 2 from the Oktoechos: of the Resurrection 3, of the Fathers 4, and of the Saint 3. Glory... Of the Fathers; Now and ever... Of the Feast. Entrance; Prokeimenon of the day; Readings of the Fathers and of the Saint. At the Litiya: Stichera of the Saint of the temple, and idiomelon stichera of the Saint; Glory... Of the Fathers; Now and ever... Of the Feast. At the Aposticha: Of the Feast or of the Resurrection; Glory... Of the Saint, or of the Fathers; Now and ever... Of the Feast. At the blessing of loaves, Troparion: "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos" twice, and of the Apostle once. And a reading from the Apocalypse. At "God is the Lord", Troparion of the Resurrection once, and of the Fathers once; Glory... Of the Apostle; Now and ever... Of the Ascension. After the Kathismata, Sessional Hymns of the Resurrection with their Theotokia, and a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel. And the Blameless (Kathisma 17), and the Hypakoe of the Tone, and a reading from the Gospel of Saint John, or the Divine Chrysostom. Polyeleos, and Sessional Hymns of the Saint, all of them; Glory... now and ever... Theotokion of his tone. And a reading: The Life of the Theologian. Anabathmoi and Prokeimenon of the Tone; "Let every breath praise the Lord"; and the Matins Gospel of the Resurrection. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"; Psalm 50; Sticheron of the Resurrection, and the rest. Canons: of the Resurrection with the heirmos for 4, of the Apostle for 4, and of the Fathers for 6. Katavasia of the Feast: "With His divine cloud..." After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Apostle, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the Fathers; Glory... Of the Apostle; Now and ever... Of the Feast; and a reading of the Apostle. After Ode 6, Kontakion of the Fathers and Ikos, and a reading from the Prologue and Synaxarion. Exapostilarion of the Resurrection and of the Fathers; Glory... Of the Apostle; Now and ever... Of the Feast. At the Praises: Stichera of the Resurrection 3, of the Fathers 2, and idiomela of the Apostle 3; Glory... Of the Fathers; Now and ever: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Theotokos..." Great Doxology. Troparion of the Resurrection only. Litanies, instruction, and dismissal. And the customary litany. Glory... now and ever... Gospel Sticheron. And the First Hour, at which Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory... Of the Fathers; Now and ever... Theotokion of the Hour; and at the Second Hour: of the Fathers. At the Third Hour, Troparion of the Resurrection; Glory... Of the Apostle; Now and ever... Theotokion; at the Sixth: of the Apostle. We alternate saying the Fathers and the Apostle. Likewise at the other hours.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone for 4, and of the Fathers, Ode 3 for 4, and of the Apostle, Ode 6 for 4. After the Entrance, Troparion of the Resurrection, and of the Feast, and of the Fathers, and of the Apostle; then Kontakion of the Fathers; Glory... Kontakion of the Apostle; Now and ever... Kontakion of the Ascension. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the Fathers and of the Apostle. Communion verses: "Praise the Lord...", and the other: "Their proclamation hath gone out into all the earth..."*

*This rule is observed when not in a temple dedicated to John the Theologian.*
*The service of Venerable Arsenius is sung whenever the ecclesiarch directs, or at Compline.*[^804]
*Be it also known that when the Paschal Key is 20, then the commemoration of the Holy Emperor Constantine and Helena, or the Third Finding of the Head of John the Baptist falls on this Sunday, and whichever of them it may be, their service is sung together with the Holy Fathers.*[^805]
*We must also know that for the commemoration of the saints who fall on Friday evening onto Saturday, and on the Sunday of Mid-Pentecost, we sing their services at Compline.*

*If there be no Vigil:*
*At the Midnight Office, we sing the Triadicon Canon, the acrostic whereof is: ΤΟΝ ΕΚΤΟΝ ΥΜΝΟΝ ΠΡΟΣΦΕΡΩ ΣΟΙ ΘΕΟΤΗΣ, that is: "A sixth hymn I offer unto Thee, O Godhead." Read in the Oktoechos.*[^806]

## On the Seventh Sunday after Pascha. At Matins.

*At "God is the Lord": Troparion of the Resurrection twice; Glory... Of the Fathers; Now and ever... Of the Ascension.*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 6:*
When the tomb was opened and hades lamented, Mary cried aloud unto the hidden Apostles: "Come forth, ye laborers of the vineyard, proclaim the word of the Resurrection: the Lord is risen, granting great mercy unto the world!"

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
Having called Thy Mother blessed, Thou didst come to Thy Passion by Thine own will, shining forth upon the Cross, desiring to seek out Adam, saying unto the angels: "Rejoice with Me, for the lost coin is found!" O God, who hast wisely ordered all things, glory to Thee!

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*
Lord, Mary Magdalene stood before Thy tomb and wept, crying aloud, taking Thee to be the gardener, saying: "Where hast Thou laid the eternal Life? Where hast Thou hidden Him that sits upon the Cherubic throne? For the guards became as dead through fear: either give me my Lord, or cry out with me: O Thou who wast among the dead and hast raised the dead, glory to Thee!"

*Glory... now and ever... Theotokion:*
O Virgin Theotokos, entreat Thy Son, who of His own will was nailed to the Cross and rose from the dead, Christ our God, that our souls may be saved!

*Then a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel according to John, the beginning whereof is: "After the festival of the most glorious Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, we celebrate the memory of the God-bearing Fathers."*[^807]

*After the Blameless (Kathisma 17): "Blessed art Thou, O Lord...", "The assembly of the angels was amazed..." Hypakoe of the Tone:*
By Thy voluntary and life-giving death, O Christ, having shattered the gates of hades as God, Thou didst open unto us ancient Paradise; and having risen from the dead, Thou hast delivered our life from corruption!

*Songs of Ascents (Anabathmoi), Tone 6, Antiphon 1:*
Unto heaven do I lift up mine eyes, unto Thee, O Word; have mercy on me, that I may live unto Thee!
Have mercy on us who are despised, making us vessels well-pleasing unto Thee, O Word!
Through the Holy Spirit, every saving cause, if He breathe upon anyone according to worthiness, speedily raises him from earthly things, wings him, piercs him, and sets him on high!

*Antiphon 2:*
If the Lord had not been among us, none of us could have stood against the warfare of the enemy; for they that conquer are exalted here.
Let not my soul be caught in their teeth as a bird, O Word! Woe is me! How shall I escape the enemy, being a lover of sin?
Through the Holy Spirit is deification unto all, good will, understanding, peace, and blessing; for He is equally-effective with the Father and the Word!

*Antiphon 3:*
They that trust in the Lord are terrible to enemies and marvelous to all; for they look on high!
The portion of the righteous hath Thee as Helper, O Savior, and doth not stretch out its hands unto iniquities.
The dominion of the Holy Spirit is over all; whom the heavenly armies worship, with every breath below!

*Prokeimenon, Tone 6:*
O Lord, stir up Thy power, and come to save us!
*Verse: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, Thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep!*
*Let every breath praise the Lord.*

*Tenth Resurrection Matins Gospel (John 21:1–14; Pericope 65): "At that time, Jesus showed Himself to His disciples, after that He was risen from the dead..."*[^808]
*Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ..." Psalm 50, and the rest as customary. Canon of the Resurrection with its heirmos for 4, of the Ascension for 4, and of the Fathers for 6.*

*Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6, Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel beheld Pharaoh the pursuer drowned, and cried aloud: Let us sing unto God a song of victory!*[^809]

*Troparia:*
With outstretched palms upon the Cross, O Jesus our God, Thou didst fulfill the Father's good pleasure, O Pious One; therefore we all sing unto Thee a song of victory!

In fear, death approached Thee, the Master of life, as a handmaid when commanded, that through her He might grant unto us endless life and the resurrection!

*Theotokion:*
Having received Thine own Maker, as He Himself willed, incarnate beyond understanding from thy seedless womb, O pure Lady, thou hast truly appeared as Sovereign Mistress over creation!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 1. Heirmos: Unto God the Savior...*[^810]
*Troparion:*
Let all of us people sing unto Christ who ascended with glory upon the shoulders of the Cherubim...

...unto Christ who hath ascended with glory and seated Himself at the right hand of the Father: let us sing a song of victory, for He hath been glorified!

Beholding Christ, the Mediator between God and men, in the flesh on high, the angelic ranks were amazed, and with one accord sang a song of victory, for He hath been glorified!

Unto God who appeared on Mount Sinai and gave the Law to Moses the God-seer, who was taken up in the flesh from the Mount of Olives: unto Him let us all sing, for He hath been glorified!

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Mother of God, unceasingly pray unto God who took flesh from thee and departed not from the bosom of the Father, to save from every distress those whom He created!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, the acrostic whereof is: ΤΟΝ ΠΡΩΤΟΝ ΥΜΝΩ ΣΥΛΛΟΓΟΝ ΤΩΝ ΠΟΙΜΕΝΩΝ, that is: "The first assembly of shepherds I praise." Tone 6, Ode 1. Heirmos: Traversing the deep...*[^811]

*Troparia:*
Praising the all-holy council of the holy Fathers, by their prayers I cry aloud within me a prophetic utterance: I beseech Thee, O Christ, preserve me! *(Twice)*

The God-bearing Fathers, having arisen today like lightning, clearly confessed Thee, O Christ, the only-begotten Son, co-unoriginate and consubstantial with the Father!

*Glory...*
The glorious adorners of Thy bride the Church, O Master, having set forth the golden definition of the holy faith, adorned her therewith as with fair raiment!

*Theotokion:*
Pre-adorned with divine glory, the honored Virgin stands before her Son and God, asking spiritual salvation for us!

*Katavasia: Unto God the Savior, who guided the people through the sea with dry feet and drowned all Pharaoh's army, unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified! Or, as in the Greek usage, Katavasia: "Covered by the divine cloud..."*[^812]

*Ode 3. Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established them upon the rock of Thy confession!*[^813]

*Troparia:*
Beholding God crucified in the flesh, creation dissolved in fear; but was held fast together by the all-governing hand of Him who was crucified for our sake!

Death, destroyed by death, lies wretched and breathless; for unable to endure the divine assault of Life, the strong one is slain, and the Resurrection is granted unto all!

*Theotokion:*
The marvel of thy divine childbearing, O pure Lady, surpasses every order of nature; for beyond nature thou didst conceive God in thy womb, and having given birth, thou remainest ever-virgin!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 3. Heirmos: By the power of the Cross...*[^814]
*Troparia:*
Thou didst ascend unto the Father, O Christ Giver of life, and didst exalt our race, O Lover of mankind, through Thine ineffable lovingkindness!

The angelic ranks, O Savior, beholding human nature ascending together with Thee, were unceasingly amazed and glorified Thee!

The choirs of angels were struck with awe, O Christ, seeing Thee taken up with Thy body, and sang praise unto Thy holy Ascension!

Human nature that had fallen into corruption Thou didst raise up, O Christ, and by Thine ascent didst exalt it, and hast glorified us with Thyself!

*Theotokion:*
Unceasingly pray, O pure Virgin, unto Him that came forth from thy womb, that those who sing of thee as Mother of God may be delivered from the delusion of the devil!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Ode 3. Heirmos: There is none holy as Thou...*
*Troparion:*
Arius the senseless wasted the stream of healing, blaspheming against the divine generation...

...falsely applying creation to the divine nature: and is cut down by the sharp sword of their teachings!

Even as divine Abraham in days of old, all the most honored and clear-voiced ones, having mustered their spiritual host, mightily destroyed Thy furious enemies by Thy power, O Good One!

*Glory...*
The holy hierarchs having assembled as the first synod, piously proclaimed Thee, O Savior, as consubstantial with the unoriginate Father and Maker of all, begotten before all ages!

*Theotokion:*
No earthly word or tongue is able worthily to praise thee, O Virgin; for from thee without seed Christ the Giver of life was well-pleased to take flesh, O all-pure Lady!

*Katavasia: By the power of Thy Cross, O Christ, establish my mind to sing and glorify Thy saving Ascension! Or: "He that burst forth from the womb..."*[^815]

*After Ode 3, Kontakion of the Ascension: Having accomplished the dispensation for us... Look to leaf 347.*[^816]

*Then Sessional Hymn of the Fathers, Tone 4, Podoben: "O unwedded Virgin" (Без̾неве́сная):*[^817]
Today the radiant city of Nicaea summoned to itself three hundred and eighteen chief-priests from all the earth, against Arius who uttered blasphemy and diminished One of the Trinity, the Son and Word of God, very God of very God; and having cast down Arius, they confirmed the Faith!

*Glory... the same.*

*Now and ever... Of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Я҆ви́ся дне́сь):*[^818]
Having ascended again unto Thine own Father, O Maker of all, leave not Thy disciples as orphans, for seeing Thee carried aloft, they cried aloud, O Lover of mankind!

*Ode 4. Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*Christ is my power, God and Lord, the venerable Church piously sings, crying aloud with a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord!*[^819]

*Troparia:*
The tree of true life blossomed forth, O Christ, for the Cross was set up, and being bedewed with blood and water from Thine incorruptible side, budded forth life for us!

No longer doth the serpent falsely suggest deification to me; for Christ, the Divinizer of human nature, hath now made plain the paths of life without hindrance!

*Theotokion:*
Truly ineffable and incomprehensible to those on earth and in heaven are the mysteries of thy divinely-splendid childbearing, O ever-virgin Theotokos!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 4. Heirmos: Habakkuk heard of the power of the Cross...*[^820]
*Troparia:*
Thou didst ascend in glory, O King of angels, having sent us the Comforter from the Father; therefore we cry aloud: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ!

When the Savior ascended unto the Father with the flesh, the angelic armies were amazed at Him and cried: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ!

The angelic powers cried unto the celestial ranks: "Lift up the gates for Christ our King, whom we hymn together with the Father and the Spirit!"

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin gave birth and knew not motherhood, yet is truly a Mother, and remained a Virgin: hymning her, we cry aloud: Rejoice, O Mother of God!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Ode 4. Heirmos: Christ is my power...*
*Troparia:*
Arius, having adulterated the Orthodox Faith with a senseless mind, was cast out from the Church by the decrees of the Fathers, as a gangrenous limb, evil-named!

The choir of the Fathers, leaning upon Thee, O Master, mightily conquered Thine enemies, and taught that the Son is of one essence with the Father and the Spirit!

Thou wast Mediator between God and men, being both God and man, O Christ: therefore knowing Thee as one Son in two natures, the God-wise Fathers proclaimed Thee!

*Theotokion:*
Tasting of the garden showed me dead; but the Tree of Life appearing from thee, O all-pure one, showed me heir of the delight of the resurrection of paradise!

*Katavasia: I have heard the report of the power of Thy Cross, how paradise was opened thereby, and I cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord! Or: "The King of kings..."*[^821]

*Ode 5. Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6. Heirmos: With Thy divine light, O Good One, enlighten, I pray Thee, the souls of those who rise early unto Thee with love, that they may see Thee, O Word of God, the true God, who drawest them out from the darkness of sin!*[^822]

*Troparia:*
Now the Cherubim step back from me, and the flaming sword, O Master, turns its back upon me, having seen Thee, O Word of God, the true God, making a way into Paradise for the thief!

No longer do I fear returning to the earth, O Master Christ; for from the earth Thou hast led me up who was forgotten, by reason of Thy great tender mercy, unto the height of incorruption by Thy Resurrection!

*Theotokion:*
Deliver from storms the souls of those who confess thee, O gracious Lady of the world; for we have gained thee as an invincible protectress, the true Mother of God!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 5. Heirmos: Rising early we cry unto Thee, O Lord...*[^823]
*Troparia:*
Having filled all things with joy, O Merciful One, Thou didst come unto the celestial powers with the flesh!

The angelic powers, beholding Thee carried aloft, cried: "Lift up the gates for our King!"

The Apostles, seeing the Savior lifted up, cried with trembling unto our King: "Glory to Thee!"

*Theotokion:*
We hymn thee as Virgin after childbirth, O Mother of God; for thou didst bear in the flesh the Word of God unto the world!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Ode 5. Heirmos: With Thy divine light, O Good One...*
*Troparia:*
How beautiful truly are the feet of those who now proclaim Thee, O Peace of God and Wisdom surpassing understanding of all angels and men, O Christ, uniting the world with abundance of peace! *(Twice)*

The divine teachers, having come together, proclaimed Thee, O Christ, the Wisdom and Power of the Father, the Hypostatic Word, sealing their teaching with the laws of the all-holy hierarchy!

*Glory...*
Having watered the Orthodox Church with the streams of the pure waters of doctrine, they now enjoy the waters of rest, ever rejoicing therein!

*Theotokion:*
O radiant lampstand, all-pure one, bearing Christ the Sun of righteousness who illuminates all from within thee, O only pure Mother of God, we now call upon thy protection!

*Katavasia: Rising early we cry unto Thee: Lord, save us, for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know no other! Or: "A cleansing from the fire..."*[^824]

*Ode 6. Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, I flee to Thy calm haven and cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!*[^825]

*Troparia:*
Crucified, O Master, Thou didst nail and abolish the curse against us, and pierced in the side with a spear, tearing up the handwriting of Adam, Thou didst set the world free!

Adam was led down, tripped by the deceitful one, into the pit of hades; but being God and merciful by nature, Thou didst descend to seek him, and taking him upon Thy shoulders, didst raise him up!

*Theotokion:*
All-pure Lady who didst give birth to the Helmsman and Lord for mortals: dispel the unstable and fierce tumult of my passions, and grant stillness unto my heart!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 6. Heirmos: The deep encompassed me...*[^826]
*Troparia:*
The Apostles leaped for joy, beholding the Creator carried on high today, and in hope of the Spirit and in awe they cried: Glory to Thine ascent!

Angels stood by, crying unto Thy disciples, O Christ: "In like manner as ye have seen Christ ascending with the flesh, He shall come again, the righteous Judge of all!"

When the heavenly powers beheld Thee, our Savior, taken up to the heights with Thy body, they cried aloud, saying: Great is Thy love for mankind, O Master!

*Theotokion:*
The unburnt bush, the mountain, the living ladder, and the heavenly gate: we worthily glorify thee, O glorious Mary, the boast of the Orthodox!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Ode 6. Heirmos: Beholding the sea of life...*
*Troparia:*
The sower of tares, who was named after madness (Arius), could in no wise hide himself from the inscrutable Providence; for having rivaled Judas, like him he burst asunder, ruptured in his bowels! *(Twice)*

The divine and honored council of the Fathers proclaimed Thee, O Master, as the only-begotten Radiance that shone forth from the essence of the Father, the Son begotten before all ages!

*Glory...*
The belly that poured forth the turbid and undrinkable fountain of heresies of the wicked is torn asunder, according to the word, providentially pierced by the plow of the prayers of the holy hierarchs!

*Theotokion:*
Moses, great among the prophets, prefigured thee, O Mother and Virgin, as the Ark, the Table, the Lampstand, and the Jar, figuratively signifying the incarnation of the Most High from thee!

*Katavasia: The deep encompassed me, the whale became my tomb; but I cried unto Thee, Lover of mankind, and Thy right hand saved me, O Lord! Or: "A cleansing..."*[^827]

*Kontakion of the Fathers, Tone 8, Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Я́кѡ нача́тки):*[^828]
The preaching of the Apostles and the dogmas of the Fathers confirmed the one Faith for the Church; and wearing the garment of truth, woven of theology from on high, she rightly defins and glorifies the great mystery of piety!

*Ikos:*
Let us hear the Church of God crying aloud with an exalted preaching: "He that thirsts, let him come and drink! The cup which I bear is the cup of Wisdom; this drink of truth have I mingled with the Word; I have poured forth no water of gainsaying, but of confession, drinking whereof the present Israel beholds God declaring: Behold, behold, that I Myself am He, and change not; I am God the First, and I am after these things, and besides Me there is none other at all! Therefore they that partake thereof shall be satisfied, and shall praise the great mystery of piety!"

*Synaxarion on the Seventh Sunday, of the Holy Fathers.*[^829]
*Bless, Father, to read.*
*Verses:*
*O chosen assembly of luminaries, I pray you, hasten to assist:*
*Illumine my earthbound thoughts, that they may be light-bearing!*
*Verses:*
*Having called the Son alien to the Father's all-creative essence,*
*Arius was alienated from the glory of God!*

On this same day, the Seventh Sunday after Pascha, we celebrate the First Council in Nicaea of the three hundred and eighteen God-bearing Fathers, for the following cause: Since our Lord Jesus Christ, clothed in the flesh, was truly the Son of God and became man, and as perfect man and God ascended and sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high: this council of holy Fathers so proclaimed Him, and confessed Him consubstantial and co-honored with the Father; and by these words, after the glorious Ascension, they instituted the present feast, setting forth the assembly of so many Fathers who proclaimed Him who ascended in the flesh to be true God, and in the flesh perfect man.

This Council took place in the days of Constantine the Great, in the twentieth year of his reign, after the persecutions had ceased.
