Having first reigned in Rome, he afterward rebuilt Byzantium into Constantinople, named after himself, in the year 5818 from the creation of the world. Then they began to speak against Arius: for this Arius was from Libya, and having come to Alexandria, was ordained deacon by the Hieromartyr Peter of Alexandria; but because he began to utter blasphemies against the Son of God, preaching Him to be created from non-existence and far removed from the Father's divine dignity, and using the titles "Wisdom" and "Word" of God in an improper sense, resembling the wicked Sabellius, who taught a single person and single hypostasis in the Godhead, saying that at one time He was Father, at another Son, and at another Holy Spirit. When Arius uttered these blasphemies, the Great Peter excommunicated him from the priesthood, having seen Christ as an infant upon the holy altar clothed in a torn tunic, who said: "Arius hath torn it!" Achilles, who received the patriarchate of Alexandria after Peter, upon his promise again absolved Arius, and moreover ordained him presbyter and appointed him teacher in Alexandria. But when Achilles died, Alexander became patriarch, who, finding Arius uttering yet worse blasphemies, deposed him by a council in Alexandria; for as Theodoret saith, he taught that the nature of Christ was mutable, and was the first to spew forth the heresy that the Lord assumed mindless and soulless flesh. Arius, having taught many his impiety, wrote to and won over Eusebius of Nicomedia, Paulinus of Tyre, Eusebius of Caesarea, and others, and set himself against Alexander. But Alexander sent...

...sending everywhere an account of his blasphemies and his deposition, and stirred up many. The Church indeed was thrown into confusion, and many desiring to embrace Christian teachings were hindered by the contentious doctrine.

Constantine the Great therefore gathered the holy Fathers in Nicaea from all over the world, providing public carriages and conveyances; and he himself came thither. And when all the Fathers were seated, he sat not upon an imperial throne, but upon a humble chair. And when the charges against Arius were declared, he and all who thought with him were put under anathema; and the Word of God was proclaimed by the holy Fathers to be consubstantial, co-honored, and co-unoriginate with the Father. And they set forth the holy Symbol of Faith, bringing it up to: "And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord...", which the Second Council afterward completed. Furthermore, the First Council confirmed the feast of Pascha, when and how we ought to celebrate it, and not with the Jews, as was formerly the custom. They also set forth twenty canons for ecclesiastical order. And the holy Symbol of Faith Constantine the Great, the equal-to-the-apostles, confirmed last of all in red letters. There were present of these holy Fathers: two hundred and thirty-two hierarchs, and eighty-six priests, deacons, and monks: in all, three hundred and eighteen. The most renowned among them were: Sylvester, Bishop of Rome, and Metrophanes of Constantinople, who being infirm, were present through their locum tenentes; Alexander of Alexandria, with Athanasius the Great, then archdeacon; Eustathius of Antioch, and Macarius of Jerusalem; Hosius, Bishop of Cordoba; Paphnutius the Confessor; Nicholas the Myrrh-streamer, and Spyridon of Trimythous, who having overcome a philosopher there, baptized him, showing him the three-in-one Godhead. In the midst of the Council, two bishop-fathers having passed away unto God, Constantine the Great placed the definitions of the holy Council in their caskets and locked them firmly, and found them also sealed and signed by their hands with ineffable words of God!

The Council being finished, since Constantinople, which was then being built, was completed, Constantine the Great summoned all those holy men; who, having walked throughout the whole city and prayed sufficiently, decreed it to be the Queen of cities, and dedicated it to the Mother of the Word. The Emperor having commanded it, the saints departed each to his own home. But while Constantine the Great had not yet departed unto God, holding the scepter together with his son Constantius: Arius came to the Emperor, saying: "I renounce all things, and wish to be united unto the Church of God!" Having written down his blasphemies, he hung them around his neck, and as though submitting to the Council, striking them with his hand, he said he submitted thereto. And the Emperor commanded the Patriarch of Constantinople to receive Arius into communion. Alexander had then succeeded Metrophanes; knowing the evil character of the man, he did not believe him, and prayed to God to reveal unto him whether it were His will to communicate with Arius. When the time arrived wherein he was to concelebrate with him, his prayer became more fervent, beseeching his death. But Arius, on his way to the church, somewhere near the porphyry pillar of the forum, feeling his bowels burst, went into a public privy, and there ruptured, pouring out all his entrails below, suffering the rupture of Judas, being matched with the betrayer of the Word; and for tearing the Son of God away from the Father's essence, he himself was torn asunder and found dead! And thus the Church of God was delivered from that destruction. By the prayers of the three hundred and eighteen God-bearing Fathers, O Christ our God, have mercy on us! Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^830]

*Ode 7. Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*An angel made the furnace bedewed with moisture for the holy children; but the divine command, burning the Chaldeans, persuaded the tyrant to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*[^831]

*Troparia:*
Lamenting over Thy Passion, the sun clothed itself in darkness, and by day over all the earth the light was darkened, O Master, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

The nethermost regions clothed themselves in light at Thy descent, O Christ, and the forefather Adam, filled with joy, appeared leaping and dancing, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Praising the ruling and all-governing Nature, the thrice-radiant light of the Trinity, the cause of goodness and boundless grace, we cry aloud together: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 7. Heirmos: In the fiery furnace...*[^832]
*Troparia:*
Thou who didst ascend upon the clouds of light and hast saved the world: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Taking upon Thy shoulders our nature that had gone astray, O Savior, Thou didst ascend and come unto God the Father!

...having ascended in the flesh unto the bodiless Father: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Taking our nature slain by sin, Thou didst bring it, O Savior, unto Thine own Father!

*Theotokion:*
Born of a Virgin, O Son, Thou didst make her the Mother of God: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Ode 7. Heirmos: The angel made the furnace bedewed...*
*Troparia:*
Ye conquered Arius, named after frenzy, who raged fiercely and uttered unrighteous words against the Most High, being commanded to cry aloud unto the Son of God: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers! *(Twice)*

Resembling the Sons of Thunder, O marvelous ones, with your fire-breathing lips ye taught all to cry unto the Word, co-unoriginate and co-enthroned with the Father: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Glory...*
Like winged eagles ye came to the aid of the Word, O divinely-blessed ones; for from the ends of the inhabited world the Holy Spirit gathered you to sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
The furnace did not burn the three youths, prefiguring thy childbearing; for the divine fire, not burning thee, dwelt within thee, and enlightened all to cry: Blessed art thou who didst bear God in the flesh!

*Katavasia: He who saved the children that sang praises in the fiery furnace: Blessed is the God of our fathers! Or: "The harmonious pipe of divine wisdom..."*[^833]

*Ode 8. Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the saints, and didst consume the sacrifice of the righteous one with water; for Thou doest all things, O Christ, whatsoever Thou willest: Thee we exalt supremely unto all ages!*[^834]

*Troparia:*
The Jewish people, murderers of the prophets of old, have now committed the murder of God, having lifted Thee upon the Cross, O Word of God: Whom we exalt supremely unto all ages!

Not leaving the heavenly vaults, and descending into hades, Thou didst raise up whole man lying in corruption, O Christ: therefore we hymn Thee unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
From Light Thou didst conceive the Light-giving Word, and didst ineffably give birth to the Super-essential One; for the divine Spirit dwelt within thee, O Virgin: therefore we hymn Thee unto all ages!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 8. Heirmos: Him who was begotten of the Father before the ages...*[^835]
*Troparia:*
Him who descended in two natures, the Giver of life, Christ who ascended into heaven with glory and sits with the Father: ye priests praise, ye people exalt Him supremely unto the ages!

Unto Him who delivered creation from the servitude of idols, and presented it free unto His Father: Thee we hymn, O Savior, and Thee we exalt supremely unto the ages!

Unto Him who by His descent cast down the adversary, and taking along the captive assembly of men, carried them on high: ye priests praise, ye people exalt Him supremely unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast appeared higher than the Cherubim, O pure Theotokos, having borne in thy womb Him who is borne by them, Whom with the bodiless powers mortals glorify unto all ages!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Ode 8. Heirmos: From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew...*
*Troparia:*
Illumined by the rays of Thy Godhead, Thy close shepherds confessed Thee as the Maker of all and Lord of being: Whom we exalt supremely unto all ages!

The choir of shepherds, ever remembered, having gathered together, divinely theologizing for me the uncreated Trinity, teaches all to cry aloud: Thee we exalt supremely unto all ages!

The sacred hierarchs, shepherds worthy of glory, enlighten the Church of Christ, proclaiming pious words everywhere, and supremely exalting Christ unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Mystically in figures the prophets foresaw thee...

...prophets [foresaw thee], who gavest birth unto the Word; for taking flesh from thee, He came forth twofold: Whom we exalt supremely unto all ages!

*Then: We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord...*

*Katavasia: Him who was begotten of the Father before the ages, the Son and God, and in these latter times became incarnate of the Virgin Mother: ye priests praise, ye people exalt Him supremely unto the ages! Or: "He that burst forth from the womb..."*[^836]

*Ode 9. Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 6. Heirmos:*
*It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O most pure one, the incarnate Word was seen by us: Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we call thee blessed.*[^837]

*Troparia:*
Without part in suffering didst Thou remain, O Word of God, though having part in suffering in the flesh; but Thou dost deliver man from passions, having become a passion unto passions, O our Savior; for Thou alone art impassible and almighty!

Having received the corruption of death, Thou didst preserve Thy body untouched by corruption; and Thy life-giving and divine soul, O Master, was not left in hades; but having risen as from sleep, Thou didst raise us up together with Thyself!

*Triadicon:*
God the Father, and the co-unoriginate Son, let all us earthly ones glorify with honorable lips; and the ineffable and most glorious power of the All-Holy Spirit let us revere: for there is one almighty, undivided Trinity!

*Canon of the Ascension, Tone 5, Ode 9. Heirmos: Thee who art beyond mind and word...*[^838]

*Troparia:*
Beholding Thee, the Redeemer of the world, Christ God, divinely taken up on high, the apostles magnified Thee, leaping with fear!

Beholding Thy deified flesh on high, O Christ, the angels said to one another: Truly this is our God!

The ranks of the bodiless powers, beholding Thee, O Christ God, taken up upon a cloud, cried aloud: O King of glory, lift up the gates!

Thee who didst descend even unto the lowest parts of the earth, and didst save man, and by Thine Ascension didst exalt him on high, do we magnify!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O Mother of God, Mother of Christ God! For beholding Him whom thou didst bear being taken up today from earth with the apostles, thou didst magnify Him!

*Canon of the Holy Fathers, Tone 6, Ode 9. Heirmos: It is not possible for men to see God...*

*Troparia:*
The assembly of champions was found gathered by mighty power, the shepherds of the Spirit, theologizing the Word pre-eternal, co-unoriginate and co-enthroned with the Father: Whom now, O sacred ones, with the heavenly hosts, praise ye evermore! *(Twice)*

The pasture of the fierce heresy, as physicians of souls and bodies, ye quenched, having set forth for all the sacred Symbol of faith; which now holding fast, O sacred ministers, we ever glorify your memory! *(Twice)*

*Glory...*
As radiant luminaries, all most pure ones, make my soul shake off the mist, through the prayers of Thy ministers, O Master, who now have proclaimed Thee unoriginate and uncreated, the Creator of all and God, co-unoriginate with the Father!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Resurrection of the dead hath now been granted on account of thine ineffable and unspeakable childbearing, O sovereign Lady, Mother of God; for Life clothed with flesh shone forth from thee upon all, and destroyed the inexorable corruption of death!

*Katavasia: Thee who art beyond mind and word, Mother of God, who in time didst ineffably bear the Timeless One, we believers magnify with songs of praise in oneness of mind. Or: "Thee who art beyond mind and word..."*[^839]

*Holy is the Lord our God (thrice).*

*Resurrectional Exapostilarion (Tenth):*
The Sea of Tiberias with the children of Zebedee, Nathanael with Peter, and two others of old, and Thomas, had them at the fishing: who at Christ's command casting on the right side, drew forth a multitude of fish; Whom Peter having recognized, swam unto Him; to whom He appeared the third time, and showed bread, and fish upon the coals.[^840]

*Glory... of the Holy Fathers.* *Tone 2, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ ᲂу҆слы́шите):*
Celebrating today the memory of the divine Fathers, by their supplications we pray, O all-bountiful Lord: Deliver Thy people from every harm of heresies, and vouchsafe all to glorify the Father, the Word, and the All-Holy Spirit!

*Both now... Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Подо́бенъ):*
While the disciples were gazing upon Thee, Thou didst ascend, O Christ, unto the Father with the apostles...

...unto supremacy: the angels running before cried aloud: Lift up the gates, lift up! The King hath ascended unto primal radiant glory![^841]

*At the Praises: Resurrectional Stichera, 4; and of the Holy Fathers, 4. Tone 6.*

*Resurrectional Stichera:*
Thy Cross, O Lord, is life and protection unto Thy people, and trusting thereon, we sing unto Thee our risen God: Have mercy on us!

Thy burial, O Master, opened paradise unto the human race, and delivered from corruption, we sing unto Thee our risen God: Have mercy on us!

With the Father and the Spirit let us praise Christ, risen from the dead, and let us cry aloud unto Him: Thou art our life and resurrection, have mercy on us!

Having risen from the tomb on the third day, O Christ, as it is written, Thou didst raise up our forefather together with Thyself: therefore the human race glorifies Thee and sings Thy Resurrection!

*Stichera of the Fathers, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ᲂу҆пова́нїе):*[^842]

*Verse: Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and flute [LXX Ps. 150:4].*[^843]
Having gathered together all spiritual skill, and having examined by the divine Spirit the divine and honorable Symbol, the venerable Fathers inscribed it as God-inspired scribes, wherein clearly they teach the Word to be co-unoriginate with Him that begot Him, and truly consubstantial, visibly following the teachings of the apostles, O right glorious, truly God-wise ones!

*Then, uniting both choirs, we sing:*
*Verse: Let every breath praise the Lord [LXX Ps. 150:6].*[^844]
Having received all noetic radiance from the Holy Spirit, the supernatural blessing, with brief words and great understanding they God-inspiredly proclaimed, as heralds of Christ, stewards of evangelical teachings, O blessed ones, and of the pious traditions, having received from on high their revelation clearly, and being illumined, they set forth the faith learned from Him!

*Verse: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy name unto the ages [Daniel 3:26].*[^845]
Having gathered together all pastoral experience, and being moved with most righteous wrath according to their skill, they vengefully drove away the grievous and destructive wolves, casting them out by the sling of the Spirit from the fullness of the Church, fallen as unto death, and having been incurably diseased, O divine shepherds, and as true servants of Christ and most sacred initiates of the divine preaching!

*Verse: Gather unto Him His venerable ones, who have established His covenant upon sacrifices [LXX Ps. 49:5].*[^846]
*And we sing the Sticheron:* "Having gathered together all spiritual skill..."

*Glory... Tone 8:*
The choir of the Holy Fathers, having gathered from the ends of the inhabited world, proclaimed one essence and nature of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and clearly handed down the mystery of theology to the Church: whom praising in faith let us bless, saying: O divine army, God-proclaiming weapons of the Lord's host, all-radiant stars of the noetic firmament, unshakable pillars of Sion, fragrant flowers of paradise, all-golden mouths of the Word, boast of Nicaea, ornament of the whole world: pray ye earnestly for our souls!

*Both now...: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Mother of God..."* *Great Doxology.* *Troparion: Resurrectional only.* *Litanies and Dismissal.* *And the Departure [into the narthex].*

*Glory... Both now...: Tenth Gospel Sticheron, Tone 6:*[^847]
After the descent into hades and the resurrection from the dead, the disciples, sorrowing as was fitting over Thy departure, O Christ, turned to labor, and again the boat and net, and fishing was nowhere; but Thou, O Savior, having appeared as Master of all, dost command the net to be cast on the right side, and the word was immediately accomplished, and there was a great multitude of fishes; and a strange supper was prepared on earth, of which Thy disciples then having partaken, vouchsafe us also now mentally to be filled, O Lord who lovest mankind!

*Then: Catechesis of Saint Theodore the Studite, and the First Hour, and the Final Dismissal.*[^848]

*At the Liturgy:* *Resurrectional Beatitudes, Tone 6, on 6; and from the Canon of the Holy Fathers, Ode 6, on 4. Instead of the Prokeimenon, the Hymn of the Fathers, Tone 7: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers...*

Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, and praised and glorified is Thy name unto the ages! *Verse: For Thou art righteous in all that Thou hast done for us [Daniel 3:26–27].* *Epistle: Acts of the Apostles, Pericope 44 (Acts 20:16–18, 28–36).*[^849] *Alleluia, Tone 4: The God of gods, the Lord, hath spoken, and called the earth...* *Verse: Gather unto Him His venerable ones [LXX Ps. 49:1, 5].*[^850] *Gospel: from John, Pericope 56 (John 17:1–13).*[^851] *Communion Verse: Praise the Lord from the heavens [LXX Ps. 148:1].*[^852] *Another: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance [LXX Ps. 111:6].*[^853]

## Seventh Sunday after Pascha: Vespers

*At "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 stichoi: of the Holy Fathers, 3; and for the Menaion, 3.*

*Stichera of the Fathers, Tone 6, Podoben: "Unoriginate" (Ненача́емаѧ):*[^854]
From the womb Thou wast born before the morning star, from the Father without mother before the ages, even though Arius glorifies Thee as a creature and not God, with audacity! foolishly confusing Thee, the Creator, with material creatures, hiding for himself fuel for the eternal fire; but the Council in Nicaea proclaimed Thee the Son of God, O Lord, co-enthroned with the Father and the Spirit!

Who rent Thy garment, O Savior? Arius, Thou didst say: who severed the Trinity, the equal-in-honor Principle, into divisions: he denied Thee to be One of the Trinity; he also teaches not to call the Theotokos Mother of God.[^855] But the Council in Nicaea confessed Thee to be the Son of God, O Lord, co-enthroned with the Father and the Spirit!

Arius falls into the pit of sin, having hated to see the light, and by the divine hook he is burst asunder inwardly, violently surrendering his whole being and soul, having become another Judas in disposition and manner! But the Council in Nicaea proclaimed Thee the Son of God, O Lord, co-enthroned with the Father and the Spirit!

Senseless Arius severed the All-Holy Trinity, the single Sovereignty, into three unlawful and unequal essences. Therefore the God-bearing Fathers, having eagerly come together, inflamed with zeal like Elijah the Tishbite, with the spiritual sword cut down the blasphemer accoutred in shame, even as the Spirit spoke!

*Glory... Tone 6:*
Today let us praise the mystic trumpets of the Spirit, the God-bearing Fathers, who sang in the midst of the Church a harmonious melody of theology: one immutable Trinity, essence and Godhead; the overthrowers of Arius and champions of the Orthodox, who ever pray unto the Lord that our souls may be saved!

*Both now... Same Tone:*
On the holy mountains, beholding Thine Ascension, O Christ, the radiance of the Father's glory, we hymn the light-bearing form of Thy countenance, we worship Thy sufferings, we honor the Resurrection, glorifying the glorious Ascension: Have mercy on us!

*Prokeimenon of the day.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ᲂу҆пова́нїе):*
"Having gathered together all spiritual skill...", with 4 verses, written today at the Praises (see fol. 367)[^856].

*Glory... Tone 3:*
Faithful guardians of the apostolic traditions were ye, O holy Fathers: for having orthodoxly proclaimed the consubstantiality of the Holy Trinity, ye synodically cast down the blasphemy of Arius; with him also having refuted Macedonius the fighter against the Spirit, ye condemned Nestorius, Eutyches, and Dioscorus, Sabellius and Severus the headless:[^857] from whose deception ask that we be delivered, praying that our unblemished life be preserved in the faith!

*Both now...:*
"God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet [LXX Ps. 46:6],[^858] to lift up the fallen image of Adam, and to send the Holy Spirit the Comforter, to sanctify our souls!"

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." Trisagion Prayers, and after "Our Father": Troparion of the Holy Fathers. Glory... Both now... of the Feast.*

*And the service of the Holy Fathers is concluded. The glory of the Ascension is chanted during the present week until Friday, which is its Apodosis; and we omit the Octoechos.*[^859]

## Monday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Matins

*At "God is the Lord": Troparion of the Feast (thrice).*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*
From on high unto earth didst Thou descend, O my Christ, and immediately from earth didst Thou ascend on high unto Thy Father...

...while the disciples were gazing upon Thy departure: with them therefore celebrating, we sing Thy saving Ascension! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^860]
Seated upon the heavenly clouds, having left peace unto those on earth, Thou didst ascend and sit at the right hand of the Father, as being consubstantial with Him and the Spirit; for even though Thou didst appear in the flesh, yet Thou didst remain unchangeable: therefore Thou awaitest the end of the dispensation, when Thou shalt come to judge all things! O righteous Lord, spare our souls, granting remission of transgressions, as a merciful God, unto Thy servants! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast, with Heirmos, on 8; and in the Menaion, on 4. Exapostilarion of the Feast.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆́гг҃льскїя си́лы):*[^861]
Having assumed me entirely, O Christ, ineffably whole, apart from sin, Thou didst unite me unto the divine nature, suffering neither confusion, nor alteration, nor division: glory to Thy fearful descent, and to Thy sufferings, and Resurrection, and Ascension, whereby our nature that had fallen of old hath been renewed!

"Why do ye gaze into heaven, and fearfully behold the Invisible?" Thine angels, O Savior, cried aloud unto Thy disciples: "He who ascends with glory, in like manner shall come, bearing flesh, to judge all breathing with righteous scales, being God and man!"

With lamentation and joy, the company of Thy disciples, standing together on the Mount of Olives, beholding Thy venerable Ascension, O sheep of God, cried aloud: "O Master, leave not Thy servants orphans, but send the divine Spirit unto our souls, enlightening Thy servants!"

*Glory... Both now... Tone 7:*
Thou didst come unto the Mount of Olives, O Thou who hast mercy on the human race, and a cloud received Thee from the eyes of Thy disciples, who trembled indeed at the sight, but rejoiced at the expectation of the Holy Spirit: confirming them wherewith, O Savior, have mercy on us!

*At the Beatitudes, the Triodion, Tone 1.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos: Thy victorious right hand...*[^862]
*Troparia:*
Thine all-glorious descent upon earth, which the angels understood not then, they now recognize as Thou ascendest into the heavens, saying: Who is this King of glory?

Having willingly endured the Crucifixion, O Christ, Thou didst rise on the third day; then Thou didst ascend unto the heavens while the disciples beheld Thee, and marveled beyond measure at Thy power!

Placing Thine ascension upon clouds, by Thy sovereign will incomprehensibly, from the Mount of Olives Thou hast now flown up on high, borne by a cloud!

*Theotokion:*
Truly hast thou surpassed the ranks of heavenly angels, O pure one, having in the flesh given birth unto the Word of the Father: Whom now pray thou earnestly, O all-immaculate one, that we be delivered from irrational deeds!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Him who in the unoriginate light of the Father...*[^863]
*Troparia:*
Unto Him who ascended in glory unto the unoriginate radiant Father, and sent down the Holy Spirit unto the apostles: praise, bless, and exalt Him supremely unto the ages!

Sing and make melody unto the Lord, shout with fear, ye earthly creatures; for He hath ascended in glory today, uniting you with the heavenly hosts unto all ages!

"Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye thus looking up on high in fear?" the bodiless ones said unto the disciples: "In like manner as ye see Him, again shall Christ come in glory!"

*Theotokion:*
Having without tillage brought forth the heavenly Ear of grain that nourishes the ends of the earth by divine power, fill my earthen soul that hungers for Him!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: The image of thy pure childbearing...*[^864]

*Troparia:*
Passion, and Crucifixion, and death didst Thou endure for us, O sinless One, and having risen in God-befitting manner, Thou didst ascend unto Thine unoriginate Father and Word: therefore we worship Thee, incomprehensible Godhead!

Moses calls in the Spirit that the angelic hosts be strengthened, as the King of all ascends bodily from earth unto the heavenly kingdoms, and sets fallen nature upon the Father's throne!

*Glory...*
"Lift up the noetic gates!" David cried prophetically in the Spirit: the Only-begotten Son of God received the nations upon His shoulders, and ascends in the flesh unto the Father, Whom He left not in His descent!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Sweetness and desire of all, thy Son is God and Lord, O most pure and chaste one: Whom pray thou earnestly with the high and bodiless hosts, that we be delivered from the soul-corrupting bitterness of sins!

## Monday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Vespers

*On the same Monday, in the evening, as usual. At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*[^865]
Having accomplished the dispensation for all, O Savior, Thou didst come unto the Mount of Olives, O Christ, whence Thou wast taken up before Thy disciples, carried into heaven with glory: therefore, wondering at the mystery, the higher ranks cried unto the lower orders: Lift up the gates, and He shall enter whence He went forth, the King and God of all, as He willed, having wondrously wrought salvation for the world!

The choir of disciples, as they beheld Thee taken up, said: O Master, how dost Thou now leave Thy friends? And whither goest Thou, who holdest all things in Thy hand? We, having left all, have followed Thee as God, rejoicing, having strong hope in Thee to exist: leave us not orphans, as Thou didst promise, O merciful Savior, send the Comforter, the Savior of our souls!

Bestowing a perfect blessing upon Thy friends, O Master, Thou didst mystically teach them: "Behold, O friends, I go unto the Father, to send you the Spirit, another Comforter; lay aside sorrow; I will not leave the sheep whom I gathered, I will not leave those whom I loved, rather, clothed with divine power from heaven, go ye," saying, "and preach among all nations the good tidings of salvation!"

*Glory... Both now... Tone 5:*
"Come, ye faithful, let us praise the Ascension..." (see fol. 344)[^866].

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тридне́венъ въскре́слъ є҆сѝ):*[^867]
For the sake of Thine ultimate compassion, O Christ, Thou wast born of the Virgin in the flesh, and willingly didst endure the Crucifixion; having risen from the tomb on the third day, Thou didst raise us up and enliven us!

*Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with a voice of rejoicing [LXX Ps. 46:2].*[^868]
While Thy divine disciples visibly beheld Thee, O Christ, Thou didst ascend from earth unto the heavenly heights, and unto them didst promise to send Thy Spirit, confirming and enlightening us!

*Verse: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet [LXX Ps. 46:6].*[^869]
The multitude of angels marveled at Thy strange and fearful ascension, O Jesus, King of all, and they cried unto the heavenly gates to be lifted up, unto the highest powers now!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*
Thou hast ascended in glory into the heavens, O Thou who fillest all things with Thy Godhead, and didst sit at the right hand of the Father, being from the beginning God the Word: therefore the heavenly hosts, beholding, cried fearfully unto the apostles: "Why stand ye looking into heaven? Behold, He whom ye have seen, the same shall come again...

...with glory to judge all the earth, and to reward each according to his works!" Unto Whom let us cry aloud: O incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee! *Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." and the Dismissal.*

## Tuesday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Matins

*At "God is the Lord": Troparion of the Feast (thrice).*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени зна́менанꙋ):*[^870]
While the angels were marveling at the strange ascent, and the disciples were awestruck at the fearful lifting up, Thou didst ascend with the flesh, O Christ, and the gates were lifted up for Thee, O Savior: therefore the heavenly hosts wondered, crying aloud: Glory to Thy fearful descent, glory to Thine Ascension, glory to Thy dispensation, O Thou who alone lovest mankind! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*[^871]
The pre-eternal and unoriginate Word, having taken human nature, having deified it mystically, today ascended: the angels running before showed unto the apostles that He was borne into heaven with great glory: worshiping Whom, they said: Glory to God who hath ascended! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Psalm 50. Canon of the Feast, on 8; and in the Menaion, on 4. Exapostilarion of the Feast.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^872]
With the disciples of the Word, let us believers run with virtues unto the mountain, that we may be vouchsafed to see the glory of Christ!

*Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with a voice of rejoicing [LXX Ps. 46:2].*[^873]
The contrivances of the Manichees have been visibly put to shame; for what their minds could not conceive, Christ hath openly shown: the Ascension with the flesh!

*Verse: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet [LXX Ps. 46:6].*[^874]
Blessed are they who have tuned themselves with the lute of virtue; for by deeds Christ's Ascension fulfills the words of all prophecy!

Today in the heavens the high powers, beholding our nature, marveled at the strange manner of the ascent: they were perplexed, saying one to another: "Who is this that is come?" Beholding their Master, they commanded the gates to be lifted up for Him: with them also let us unceasingly praise Him who with the flesh comes again thence, as God to judge all and the whole world! *Glory... Both now... Tone 5:*

*At the Beatitudes, the Triodion, Tone 2.*
*Ode 2. Heirmos: See, see that I am God...*[^875]
*Troparia:*
Abiding with the disciples during forty days after the divine rising from the tomb, O Savior, promising to send them the divine Spirit, in such manner Thou didst ascend in glory, carried strangely upon the shoulders of the Cherubim!

"Lift up the gates, understand the marvelous works!" the high noetic powers cried aloud: "The King of glories comes now into His rest, having deified earthly men through His abundant compassion and unceasing mercy!"

Thou who makest darkness Thy hiding-place, for the bodiless nature, God who walkest upon the wings of the winds, clothed from the Virgin as with a bright cloud, by a bright cloud didst ascend from earth on high, while the disciples beheld the glorious Ascension!

*Theotokion:*
Untilled earth, who didst sprout the Nourisher of all, who opens His hand and by divine strength fills every living creature with favor: strengthen with the Bread of life hearts enfeebled by the surfeit of our evil transgressions!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Refusing to worship the golden image...*[^876]
*Troparia:*
Having assumed Adam's nature and deified it, the Word ascended unto His Father, the Primal Origin of light, while all the bodiless ranks marveled and cried aloud: Praise the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto the ages!

Elijah, prefiguring Thy fearful Ascension, O Life-giver, was shown as an armed warrior by the divine Spirit, and was carried on high from earth, singing unto the Master: Let all creation praise the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto the ages!

Praise God, shout, ye nations, and clap your hands, sing in unison: with glory Christ ascended whence He came to us, to save those who cry aloud: Praise and exalt Him supremely unto the ages!

*Triadicon:*
Glorify all the Father, and the co-unoriginate Son, and the Spirit, the uncreated Trinity: united in nature, yet singing Them divided in Persons, let all common creation praise the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee as is meet...*[^877]

*Troparia:*
"Who is this that now ascends with glory upon the clouds?" the highest ranks said, crying aloud unto them: "Lift up the noetic gates! He is the only God who hath united earthly things with heaven; unto Him let us bring majesty and glory with fear!"

"Behold," Thou didst say, O Word, unto the disciples sorrowing over Thy departure: "tarry, waiting in faith, until the divine Comforter from on high comes unto you, the unforgotten fountain of all gifts: He shall teach you all things, as He is all-good!"

*Glory...*
Beholding Adam's fallen nature wonderfully set on high upon the Father's throne, and ever worshiped by angels and archangels, and by thrones, virtues, and dominions: glory be to our only God who hath so willed!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Fair in beauty did the fair Maiden bear Thee; Whom beholding, having neither form nor comeliness when Thou didst suffer, O Savior, weeping she said: "I marvel at Thine incomprehensible humility, O my Son, whereby Thou savest humbled human nature!"

## Tuesday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Vespers

*On the same Tuesday, in the evening, as usual. Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "As noble among the martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^878]
While Thy divine disciples were gazing, Thou didst ascend unto the heavenly heights, and didst sit at the right hand of the Father, O co-eternal Son, inseparable from Him; and as Thou didst say, Thou didst send the Comforter, making heavenly those on earth, wise and God-proclaiming, Thy sacred disciples!

Thou becamest incarnate because of Thine ineffable goodness, O Jesus, and willingly didst endure Crucifixion and death; and immediately having risen on the third day from the dead, after forty days Thou didst ascend whence Thou didst first descend, having humbled earthly things, and bringing all unto the Father!

When the wise apostles beheld Thee taken up upon the clouds, O Lord, weeping and filled with compunction, they cried with tears: Leave us not orphans, whom in compassion Thou hast loved, but send down upon us, as Thou didst promise, O all-bountiful One, Thine All-Holy Spirit, enlightening our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 4:*[^879]
When Thou wast taken up in glory, O Christ God, while the disciples were gazing, the clouds received Thee with gladness, the gates were lifted up as they beheld Thee, the angels rejoiced with gladness, and the highest powers called out, saying: "Lift up your gates, and the King of glory shall enter!" And the disciples, marveling, said: "Depart not from us, O Good Shepherd, but send unto us Thine All-Holy Spirit, guiding, and enlightening, and confirming our souls!"

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́снымъ чи́номъ):*[^880]
Thou hast confirmed human nature through Thyself, having made all things new, and didst ascend in the flesh, and didst sit on high, O Word of God, at the right hand of the Father: therefore we await Thee to come again as Judge of all, believers and unbelievers!

*Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with a voice of rejoicing [LXX Ps. 46:2].*[^881]
The angels cried aloud unto Christ's apostles: "Ye men, why gaze ye, as Christ the Life-giver ascends on high? He shall come to judge all, being God over all, and rendering unto all according to the worthiness of their deeds!"

*Verse: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet [LXX Ps. 46:6].*[^882]
Having assumed flesh, Thou didst deify it, O Savior who lovest mankind, and didst vouchsafe it immortal and divine glory in Thy fearful and terrible Ascension: O longsuffering One, illumine our hearts with Thy light, even of us who sing unto Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 5:*
"O Lord, as Thou wast taken up..." (see fol. 344)[^883].

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." and the Dismissal.*

## Wednesday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Matins

*At "God is the Lord": Troparion of the Feast (thrice).*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate with the Father" (Собезнача́льномꙋ Сло́вꙋ):*[^884]
From on high from heaven unto those on earth, and lying below in the prison of hades, Thou didst raise up Adam's image together with Thyself, O God, and by Thine Ascension, O Christ, having led him into the heavens, Thou didst make him co-enthroned upon Thy Father's throne, as Thou art merciful and lovest mankind! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́инственно):*[^885]
Having ascended the Mount of Olives, O merciful God, whence Thou didst ascend into the heavens: for a bright cloud from earth took Thee, while Thy disciples beheld the fearful wonder, and the bodiless ones in the heavens cried aloud with fear: "Lift up the gates for the highest hosts!" With them all creation praises Thee, the eternal King and God! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast, and in the Menaion.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^886]
A new and marvelous wonder: for human nature hath ascended into heaven, united unto God the Word, the Ruler of all!

*Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with a voice of rejoicing [LXX Ps. 46:2].*[^887]
The radiant and most bright day of the eternal divine ascent into heaven hath shone forth, enlightening all things!

*Verse: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet [LXX Ps. 46:6].*[^888]
Even as Thou didst send Thy Comforter Spirit from on high unto the disciples, so send down Thy grace upon Thy people, O Christ Savior!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 5:*
"Come, ye faithful, let us praise the Ascension..." (see fol. 344)[^889].

*At the Beatitudes, the Triodion, Tone 3.*
*Ode 3. Heirmos: Thou art the confirmation of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord...*[^890]
*Troparia:*
Human nature, condemned and corrupted by transgression, Thou hast raised up, O Master, higher than the angels, as Thou art compassionate!

Thou hast ascended into the heavens with glory, while the bodiless ones sing unto Thee, O Lord, as Creator of all and our God!

Having ascended into the heavens, O all-good Master, Thou didst send the true Comforter Spirit unto Thy disciples!

*Theotokion:*
Incarnate from thee, O pure one, came forth the Word, righting the fall of the first-fashioned through the compassion of His mercies!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: In the unquenchable fire...*[^891]

Having accomplished by almighty power the dispensation for us, O God, Thou didst ascend while Thy disciples gazed, and cried unto Thee with fear: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^892]

"Ye men of Galilee, truly why look ye thus, as He ascends close unto heaven?" the angels said: "even as ye see Him, so again shall He come to judge all creation: Whom we exalt supremely unto the ages!"

"The upright Spirit, the divine Spirit, the Spirit existing indivisibly with Thee, as Thou didst promise, send unto us, O Word of God, carried upon the clouds of glory!" the divine apostles cried: "that we may sing and exalt Thee supremely unto the ages!"

*Theotokion:*
From thee the Wisdom of God built for Himself a temple, and became incarnate by ineffable descent, O Maiden who knewest not wedlock; for thou alone among all generations wast chosen to be the dwelling-place of Christ God!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: A new and divine marvel...*[^893]

*Troparia:*
Ascending with glory amid shouting, as the prophet spoke of old: "The Lord and God hath gone up! Sing unto Him, ye nations, sing with faith, and praise Him with trembling, for He hath wrought unsearchable and ineffable things!"

Unto the sorrowing disciples Thou didst say: "I will not be parted from you forever, even though I go unto the Father who sent Me; go ye, teach all the world to know Me as the true God, who have done the most glorious things which ye see and have heard!"

*Glory...*
Having spoken thus unto all, O Christ, immediately a cloud of light took Thee, and while all beheld, Thou didst ascend from earth; and having ascended, Thou abidest with God above all principality and power: therefore we glorify Thy much-hymned power!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Truly hast thou appeared as the receptacle of Light, for from thee God became ineffably incarnate without change, having exalted Adam's nature upon the Cross, and having become the first-born from the dead; and remaining God in the highest, together with the Father and the divine Spirit He is glorified!

## Wednesday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Vespers

*On the same Wednesday, in the evening, as usual. At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^894]
Thou didst suffer as man, being impassible in Thy Godhead, and having risen on the third day, Thou didst despoil death, and having raised up all who had decayed through transgression, Thou didst ascend unto the Father, having promised to send the Comforter unto Thy sacred apostles, O almighty Jesus, Savior of our souls!

"Why stand ye looking into heaven?" the angels, visibly appearing as young men, said unto the initiates of the Word: "This same Jesus whom ye see a bright cloud taking up, shall come in like manner as ye have seen Him, to judge the world, as it is written; go ye therefore and accomplish all that hath been spoken!"

After Thy rising from the tomb, ineffably risen, O almighty Lord, having taken those whom Thou didst love, Thou didst lead them out as far as Bethany, O Word, and coming unto the Mount of Olives, having blessed them, Thou didst ascend while the angels submitted unto Thee, O all-good Jesus, Savior of our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 1:*
"Thine angels, O Lord, said unto the apostles..." (see fol. 348)[^895].

*Then, Stichera in the Menaion.*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^896]
"Leave not orphans those whom I have gathered," the Lord said unto His friends, "but I will send you the All-Holy Spirit!"

*Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with a voice of rejoicing [LXX Ps. 46:2].*[^897]
The angels cried aloud unto the apostles: "Ye men of Galilee, in like manner as ye have seen Him, so shall He come again!"

*Verse: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet [LXX Ps. 46:6].*[^898]
Thy disciples, O Word, came down with joy from the Mount of Olives, glorifying and praising Thy divine Ascension!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 4:*
"Ascending into the heavens whence also Thou didst descend..." (see fol. 344)[^899].

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace, O Master..." and the Dismissal.*

## Thursday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Matins

*At "God is the Lord": Troparion of the Feast (thrice).*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "When the stone had been sealed" (Ка́мени зна́менанꙋ):*[^900]
Hades having been despoiled by Thee, O Life-giver, and the world having been enlightened by Thy Resurrection, Thou didst ascend in glory, O Savior, holding all things in Thy hand: therefore with the angels we glorify Thee, O almighty Lord: Glory to Thine Ascension, O Christ, glory to Thy kingdom, glory to Thy compassion, O Thou who alone lovest mankind! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1:*
Thou camest in the flesh from heaven, O Word, upon earth, that Thou mightest raise up all with Thyself: Thou didst descend incorporeal upon earth, and didst enter with the flesh, O Christ: therefore the heavenly hosts cried aloud, shouting: Glory to Thy descent, O Christ, glory to Thine Ascension, glory to Thy dispensation, O Thou who alone lovest mankind! *Verse and Both now... the same. Canon of the Feast, on 6; and in the Menaion...*

*At the Aposticha: Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^901]
Thou hast accomplished, O Good One, the Father's good pleasure, uniting the things on high with those below, and didst ascend in glory unto the foremost ranks!

*Verse: Clap your hands, all ye nations; shout unto God with a voice of rejoicing [LXX Ps. 46:2].*[^902]
A bright cloud received Thee on high, and the angels served Thy divine Ascension with fear and trembling!

*Verse: God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet [LXX Ps. 46:6].*[^903]
Beholding Thee carried upon a cloud, with the apostles the Mother of God sings God-befitting praise unto Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 7:*
"Thou didst come unto the Mount of Olives..." (see today)[^904]. *Then: "It is good to give thanks unto the Lord..." The First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*At the Beatitudes, the Triodion, Tone 4.*
*Ode 4. Heirmos: He that sits in glory upon the throne...*[^905]
*Troparia:*
Inaccessible by nature, becoming accessible unto me, clothed with my nature, Thou didst enlighten all my being, and by Thine Ascension didst lead it up, far above every principality and power!

Elijah the charioteer passed into hearing, prefiguring of old Thy divine Ascension, O Word of God: for as upon a chariot, O Savior, carried by a cloud, Thou didst reach the Father's bosom!

While the disciples were terrified at the fearful taking up and marveled, the divine angels proclaimed: "Ye men of Galilee, as ye see, so again shall Jesus come to judge all!"

*Theotokion:*
Having renewed crushed human nature, O most pure one, which had bowed down to corruption, having incarnated God and given birth beyond nature, O unwedded Maiden, unto Him we cry: Glory to Thy power, O Lord! *Ode 8. Heirmos: The children walking...*

*Troparia:*
Walking upon the wings of the winds, borne upon a cloud, He is now received up into the heavens where He was before; He sends the Comforter unto the disciples, as they praise and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Having willingly endured the Crucifixion and Burial, Thou didst rise on the third day, O almighty One, and appearing unto those that love Thee during forty days, Thou didst make them glad; then having blessed them, Thou didst ascend unto Thy Father with glory!

Beyond human nature and beyond word, O God-loving disciples, the Word, having ascended, sends unto you, as He promised, the vision of the All-Holy and Co-enthroned Spirit, as ye sing: "Praise the Lord and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!"

*Theotokion:*
O shut Gate of God, through which the Most High alone passed, guide me unto the divine paths, and open unto me the doors of grace; for unto thee do I flee, O Virgin, the only protectress of mankind!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: A stone cut without hands...*[^906]

*Troparia:*
"Until ye be clothed with power from on high," Thou didst say unto the disciples, "tarry ye gathered together; for behold, I am taken up, and I will send you the Comforter Who is co-enthroned with the Father!"

Come mystically, having all ascended to the height of contemplation, let us behold with spiritual eyes Him Who ascended and sits at the right hand of the Father, as the co-enthroned and co-eternal Word!

*Glory...*
The Sun, shining forth beautifully from the tomb, by grace, like radiant beams unto all the inhabited earth, sent you forth, O apostles, enlightening it and driving away the gloom!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Spare me, O Christ, when Thou comest with glory to judge the world, dispelling the gloom of my passions by the prayers of her that bore Thee, and make me an inheritor of Thy Heavenly Kingdom!

## On the Same Thursday Evening: Vespers

*The regular Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried": Stichera of the Feast, without the Old Testament Readings and the Entrance. Likewise on Friday at Matins:*[^907] *The entire service of the Feast unchanged, as indicated for the Feast itself, except the Polyeleos and the Gospel, and we do not sing "More honorable than the Cherubim." And thus is the Apodosis of the Feast of the Ascension of Christ celebrated. And the service of the saint of the day is sung at Compline (see fol. 354)[^908].*

## On Friday of the Seventh Week after Pascha: Liturgy

*At the Beatitudes, the Triodion, Tone 6.*

*Ode 5. Heirmos: Rising early unto Thee...*[^909]

*Troparia:*
Having overthrown the dominion of death by divine power, Thou didst rise on the third day, O my Christ, and didst ascend with glory unto the heavenly places, while Thy disciples sang praises unto Thee as God and Lover of mankind!

"Leave us not orphans, O Bountiful One, but as Thou didst promise, send Thine All-Holy Spirit!" Thy disciples cried aloud unto the Redeemer, as they beheld Thee, O Lover of mankind, ascending from the earth.

Behold, the Spirit is about to descend upon the earth in tongues of fire, so that He may visibly manifest as fiery the clay-fashioned human tongues of the disciples, proclaiming His God-befitting coming!

Clothed in human nature, having renewed the corrupted, O Word, for the sake of boundless compassion, Thou hast given us a strong wall and protection forever, beholding Thee as God and Man!

*Theotokion:*

*Ode 8. Heirmos: According to the Father's law...*[^910]
Having united the separated by Thy tender mercy, O Word all-good, striking down the adversary by the suffering of Thy flesh, Thou didst ascend in glory unto the Father Whom Thou didst never leave, while the disciples watched: therefore with them we bless and supremely exalt Thee unto the ages!

Having had mercy, O Savior, upon those whom Thou didst love, rescuing them from the malicious slander of the enemy, Thou didst ascend from the Mount of Olives, O Master, while Thy disciples looked on and marveled how a cloud received Thee in the flesh, like a Cherubic throne: therefore with them we bless and supremely exalt Thee unto the ages!

"I will not leave you orphans, O blessed sons and heirs of My Kingdom, but I will send from on high the Comforter, teaching you mystically, beyond comprehension and mind, and showing the participation of fire unto mortal beings," Thy disciples cry aloud unto Thee, O Bountiful One: therefore with them we praise and supremely exalt Thee unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Beyond the laws of nature, O Virgin, having given birth unto the Lawgiver, Who put on the renewal of the law and bestowed the brightness of grace: therefore, O pure one, free me who am now sorely overcome by the law of sin, that I may sing: "Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!"

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Every tongue is at a loss...*[^911]

*Troparia:*
Having had mercy on cast-off and afflicted human nature, O Thou Who alone art merciful and loving of mankind in grace, Thou didst take upon Thyself human flesh, and by Thy mighty suffering as Savior didst ascend, O Christ, on high unto the Father, having filled all things with glory!

"Why are ye grieving? Why do ye marvel?" the angels cried aloud unto the apostles, standing with them upon the mountain: "This Jesus Whom ye see ascended, so shall He come again in great glory to judge the inhabited world and to give unto each according to his desert!"

*Glory...*
O Thou Who didst give good humility unto Thy sacred disciples through Thy Holy Spirit, as a bountiful Benefactor, preserve them unharmed from the evil one, that having done Thy will, O Christ, we may all be accounted worthy of Thy Kingdom together!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
A receptacle of the Light that enlightened all creation hast thou been shown to be, O alone most pure and all-immaculate Mary, Mother of God: therefore I pray thee, enlighten my passion-tossed soul darkened by the pleasures of this life, that I may walk by day in divine paths!

---

# PART V: GREAT FEAST OF HOLY PENTECOST, KNEELING PRAYERS, SUNDAY OF ALL SAINTS, AND REAR FLYLEAVES

## Memorial Saturday of the Seventh Week after Pascha (Saturday of Souls)[^912]

*On which we make commemoration of all the departed from the ages, our Orthodox fathers and brethren, and all who have fallen asleep in the faith of Christ.*

*On Friday evening, at Vespers: We set 6 Stichera. Stichera for the Martyrs, Tone 6:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, not having denied Thee, nor departed from Thy commandments: by their prayers have mercy on us!

The passion-bearing martyrs and citizens of heaven, who suffered on earth, endured many torments, and received the perfect crown in heaven: let them pray for our souls!

Having suffered for Thy sake, O Christ, they endured many torments: by their prayers and intercessions, O Lord, preserve us all!

*Other Stichera for the Departed, Tone 8, Podoben: "In Eden of old" (И҆́же въ є҆де́мѣ):*[^913]
Today, O faithful, making commemoration of all the dead from the ages who lived piously in the faith: let us hymn the Savior and Lord, earnestly beseeching that in the hour of judgment they may give a good defense unto Him, our very God Who judges all the earth, that having obtained a place at His right hand in joy, in the portion of the Righteous and in the radiant lot of the Saints, they may be accounted worthy of His heavenly Kingdom!

O Savior, Who by Thy blood hast redeemed mankind, and by Thy death hast delivered us from bitter death, and by Thy Resurrection hast granted us life everlasting: give rest, O Lord, unto all that have fallen asleep in piety, whether in deserts, or in cities, or in the sea, or on land, or in any place: emperors, priests, high priests, monks, and laymen, in every age of the whole human race; and account them worthy of Thy Heavenly Kingdom!

By Thy Resurrection from the dead, O Christ, death no longer holds dominion over those that have died in piety: therefore we earnestly pray, give rest unto Thy servants in Thy courts and in the bosom of Abraham, from Adam even unto this day, who have served Thee purely: our fathers and brethren, friends together and kinsmen, every person who in this life has served faithfully and has passed away unto Thee in divers manners and forms, O God; and account them worthy to obtain Thy Heavenly Kingdom!

*Glory... Tone 8:*
I weep and lament when I contemplate death, and behold our beauty created according to the image of God lying in the graves, formless, inglorious, having no shape! O wonder! What is this mystery that has befallen us? How have we been surrendered unto corruption? How have we been yoked unto death? Truly by the command of God, as it is written, Who grants rest unto the departed!

*Both now... Theotokion, Same Tone [Tone 8]:*
"Who will not call thee blessed, O all-pure Virgin..." (see in the Fourth Saturday, fol. 196)[^914].

*Then, instead of the Prokeimenon, we sing Alleluia, Tone 8.*
*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord [LXX Ps. 64:5].*[^915]
*Verse: And their soul shall dwell among good things [LXX Ps. 24:13].*[^916]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Martyrs, Tone 6:*
The army of the holy martyrs became an invincible weapon: for seeing death lying before them, and looking beyond unto the life to come, they were strengthened by Thine hope: by their prayers, have mercy on us!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord [LXX Ps. 64:5].*
Thy creative command was my origin and substance: for wishing to fashion a living being out of the invisible and the visible nature, Thou didst form my body from the earth, and gavest me a soul by Thy divine and life-creating breathing: therefore, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servants in the land of the living, and in the tabernacles of the righteous!

*Verse: And their soul shall dwell among good things [LXX Ps. 24:13].*
The tasting of the tree of old in Eden became grief unto Adam, when the serpent vomited forth his poison: for through it entered universal death, devouring man. But the Master having come overthrew the serpent, and granted us rest: let us therefore cry aloud unto Him: Spare, O Savior, and give rest with Thine elect unto those whom Thou hast taken!

*Glory... Tone 6:*
Like a blossom that withers, and like a shadow that passes away, every man is dissolved; but again at the sounding trumpet, all the dead, as in an earthquake, shall rise up to meet Thee, O Christ God: then, O Master, do Thou rank in the tabernacles of Thy Saints those whom Thou hast translated from us, mercifully overlooking their transgressions!

*Both now... Theotokion, Same Tone [Tone 6]:*
All my hope do I place in thee, O Mother of God: preserve me under thy protection!

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace, O Master..." Troparion, Tone 8:*
O Thou Who by the depths of Thy wisdom in love for mankind dost govern all things, and dispensest what is profitable unto all, O only Creator: give rest, O Lord, unto the souls of Thy servants; for they have placed their hope in Thee, our Maker and Fashioner and God! *Glory... (the end of the Troparion).*

*Both now... Theotokion:*
In thee we have a wall and a haven, and an acceptable intercessor before the God Whom thou didst bear, O unwedded Mother of God, salvation of the faithful!

*And the remaining order of the Vigil: that is, the entire service for the departed, from beginning unto end, which is performed in the evening and in the morning:*

*and observe strictly as it was ordained for Meatfare Saturday (see the Lenten Triodion, fol. 37 through 51)[^917]. And concerning the Canon at Panikhidas: see Marko, Chapter 141; and in the manuscript: After the dismissal in church, we do the customary service in the narthex, at the Great Panikhida for the departed. And we sing the Canon for the dead of the current Tone of the Octoechos. But if the commemoration of one of the Great Saints falls on this day, then the service of the Saturday is sung in the crypt-chapel of rest; and in church the service of the Menaion is sung, that is, of the celebrated Saint, and of the patron of the temple—these two canons. For the rest, see above on folio 55[^918].*

## On the Seventh Saturday after Pascha: Matins

*After the Six Psalms, Alleluia in Tone 8, and its verses. Troparion: "O Thou Who by the depths of Thy wisdom..." (twice). Glory... Both now... Theotokion: "In thee we have a wall and a haven..."*

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:*
By the resistance of their passion-bearing contest, the wounds of the tormentors were turned unto torments for the tormentors, and like a pillar of angelic faces holding the honors of victory, they extinguished the boasts of the tormentors and tyrants, and overthrew Belial by confessing Christ: O Lord Who didst strengthen them, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel [LXX Ps. 67:36].*[^919]
Having endured the contest of suffering, the holy ones, receiving the honors of victory from Thee, brought to nought the schemings of the lawless and received unfading crowns: for their sake, O God, save our souls!

*Verse: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them [LXX Ps. 33:18].*[^920]
Thou hast shown the memory of Thy saints, O Lord, like the paradise of Eden: for in it all creation rejoices; grant us therefore by their prayers peace and great mercy!

*Glory... Sessional Hymn for the Dead:*
Truly all things are vanity, and life is but a shadow and a dream; for in vain does every mortal disquiet himself, as the Scripture says: when we have gained the world, then we take up our dwelling in the grave, where emperors and beggars are together! Therefore, O Christ God, give rest unto the departed, as Lover of mankind!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Calling Thy Mother blessed, Thou didst come unto voluntary Passion, and wast lifted up upon the Cross, seeking to search out Adam, saying unto the angels: "Rejoice with Me, for the lost drachma is found!" O God Who hast ordered all things wisely, glory to Thee!

*The Homily of John Chrysostom is read: Consolation concerning the Departed, and Instruction concerning Thanksgiving and Praise of God in Afflictions and in Immoderate Weeping. Its incipit: "God created the first man with all creation..."*[^921]

*Then after the Amomos [Psalm 118]: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, teach me Thy statutes." "The choir of saints has found the fountain of life..." and all the Troparia in order. And then, Sessional Hymn for the Dead, Tone 5:*
Give rest, O our Savior, with the righteous unto Thy servants, and settle them in Thy courts, as it is written: overlooking as good their transgressions, voluntary and involuntary, known and unknown, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
O Christ God, Who didst shine forth unto the world from the Virgin, and through her hast shown us to be sons of light, have mercy on us!

*Then the Reading from the same homily. Psalm 50 [LXX Ps. 50]. Then we sing the Stichology... Canon to the Saint of the Temple with its Heirmos on 6; and the present Canon on 8, the composition of our venerable father Sir Theodore the Studite, Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos: Let us send up a song, ye people, unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory and crying: Let us sing unto Thee, the only Master!*[^922]
*Refrain: Give rest, O Lord, to the souls of Thy departed servants.*

*Troparia:*
Let us all pray unto Christ, making commemoration today of the dead from the ages, that He may deliver from eternal fire those who have fallen asleep in faith and in the hope of everlasting life!

In the depth of Thy judgments, O Christ, Thou hast all-wisely foreordained for each the end of life, the place and manner: therefore, those whom the grave has covered in every land, save at the judgment, O Thou Who didst descend!

O Thou Who gavest the boundaries of our life, do Thou, O Lord, show those who have departed from the night of this life to be sons of the never-setting Day: Orthodox priests, emperors, and all people!

Those whom the water covered, and war mowed down, an earthquake encompassed, and murderers slew, and fire burned up: rank the faithful, O merciful One, in the portion of the Righteous!

Overlooking all our debts in the flesh, O our Savior, of every age of the whole human race, set them uncondemned before Thy judgment seat, as they make answer unto Thee, the Creator!

*Glory... Triadicon:*
I hymn the three Persons of one Essence above all things that exist: the unbegotten Father, the begotten Son, and the Holy Spirit: one unoriginate Kingdom, Dominion, and Godhead!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Truly thou hast been shown to be a heaven upon earth, greater than the heaven on high, O all-immaculate Virgin: for from thee the Sun shone forth upon the world, purifying it with righteousness!

*Katavasia: "Let us send up a song..."*

*Ode 2. With this Heirmos on 8. If in the Psalter we do not sing this ode, we say the rest. Heirmos: See, see that I am your God, born before the ages of the Father, and in these latter days incarnate without man of the Virgin, and having destroyed the sin of our forefather Adam, as Lover of mankind!*[^923]

*Troparia:*
"See, see that I am your God," Who by righteous judgment of old set the boundaries of life, receiving into incorruption from corruption all who have fallen asleep in the hope of everlasting resurrection!

O Lord, Who from the four corners of the earth receivest those who have fallen asleep in faith: in the sea, or on land, or in rivers, springs, or lakes, or in pits, or those who have become food for beasts, birds, and reptiles: give rest unto all!

In Thine hand, O Lord, Thou hast fore-judged all things, dissolved into four elements: at Thy Coming, having gathered them, raise them all up, forgiving their transgressions done in ignorance and in knowledge!

O fearful second Coming of Thine, O Lord! For when Thou comest as lightning upon earth, Thou shalt raise up all Thy creation to judge: account those who then lived in faith in Thee, who went out to meet Thee, worthy to be with Thee!

*Glory... Triadicon:*
All-perfect, supersubstantial, unoriginate Trinity: unbegotten Father, and only-begotten Son, Spirit proceeding from the Father and made manifest through the Son: one Essence and Nature, Lordship and Kingdom, save us all!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
O ineffable wonder of thy childbearing, O Virgin Mother! How dost thou give birth and yet remain pure? How dost thou bear a child and knowest not man? O wonders, as He knows, Who was born of thee beyond nature in new splendor, God the Word!

*Katavasia: "See, see..."*

*Ode 3. Heirmos: O Word of God, Who with Thine hand didst establish the heavens in the light of Thy true knowledge: establish also the hearts of us that place our hope in Thee!*[^924]

*Troparia:*
Account those who have completed the course of life in pious glory worthy, O God, to be clothed with the crown of the righteous, and to enjoy heavenly blessings!

Those suddenly snatched away, consumed by lightning, frozen by frost, and struck by any wound: give rest, O God, when Thou shalt try all things with fire!

Those who have sailed over the ever-troubled sea of this life, O Christ, account worthy to run unto the incorruptible haven of Thy life, those whose lives were steered in Orthodoxy!

Those whom every creature of the sea, and birds of the air, received as food, O Christ: by Thy judgments raise them up, O God, in the last day with glory!

*Glory... Triadicon:*
Intellectually joining the divine Unity in three Persons simply, together co-eternal and unmingled: for like the speed of lightning, so the Fashioner is seen in Unity!

*Theotokion:*
Thy wonder is incomprehensible: for without man thou givest birth, and keepest thy virginity pure after bearing. Therefore the host of angels and the race of mankind hymn thee unto the ages!

*Katavasia: "O Word of God, Who with Thine hand..." Kontakion of the Temple.*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*[^925]
O Thou Who upon the Cross didst endure the Cross and death, and didst put to death the dominion of Hades, and didst raise the dead: give rest, O Savior, unto the departed, as the God Who loves mankind; and at Thy fearful and Dread Coming, O Life-giver, as Thou possessest a multitude of mercy, account them worthy of Thy Kingdom! *Glory... the same.*

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Show thy speedy protection, help, and mercy upon thy servants, and calm the waves of vain thoughts, O pure one, and raise up my fallen soul, O Mother of God; for I know, yea, I know, O Virgin, that thou canst do whatsoever thou desirest!

*And the Reading.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos: Looking from the mountain overshadowed, O Word, the Prophet foresaw in divine vision that from the alone Mother of God Thou wouldst become incarnate, and with trembling he glorified Thy power!*[^926]

*Troparia:*
Fathers and forefathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers, from the first even unto the last who died in the lawful covenant and in the right faith: remember them all, O our Savior!

Those who left this life in faith in the mountains, on the path, in desolate places and in deserts—monks and laymen, youths and elders: settle them with the saints, O Christ!

Those who passed away unexpectedly from sorrow and joy, who suffered in prosperity or in adversity: give rest unto them all, O Savior of us all!

Those whom the sword slew, and a horse dashed down, whom hail, snow, and torrential rain overwhelmed, whom a falling brick choked, or earth buried: O Christ our Savior, give them rest!

*Triadicon:*
Wondrously as one and three-radiant, in each Person indivisibly: for the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are worshipped as one God!

*Theotokion:*
Direct us by thy prayers, steering those assailed by the tempest of sin into saving havens, O Mother of God, delivering us from every distress!

*Ode 5. Heirmos: Early in the morning my spirit seeks Thee, O God, for Thy commandments are light at Thy Coming: in them therefore enlighten our mind, O Master, and guide us upon the paths of life!*[^927]

*Troparia:*
Making commemoration today of each of the dead who have lived piously from the ages, O Lord, we earnestly cry unto Thee: Give rest unto all with Thy saints!

Deliver from eternal torment, O Bountiful One, those whom Thou hast received of every generation and race, among emperors and princes, or those who have lived monastic lives in Orthodoxy!

Knowing what is profitable for all whom Thou hast fashioned, O Lord, those whom Thou hast permitted to die unexpectedly by sudden falls: deliver our God from every torment!

From the fire that ever burns, and from dark gloom, from the gnashing of teeth, and the worm that torments without end, and from every punishment: deliver all who have died in faith, O our Savior!

*Glory... Triadicon:*
Co-enthroned, unoriginate Unity, unique division, possessing one nature in three Persons, united in one will for the keeping of the commandments!

*Theotokion:*
More honorable than the fiery-visaged Seraphim hast thou been shown to be, O pure one, having borne the inaccessible Jesus the Savior, Who by incarnation deified the commingling of earthborn mortals!

*Ode 6. Heirmos: Held fast by many transgressions and falling down before Thy compassions, receive me as the Prophet, O Lord, and save me, O Lover of mankind!*[^928]

*Troparia:*
Having loosed the pains of death by Thy suffering, O Prince of Life, our God: give rest unto Thy servants who have fallen asleep from the ages!

By Thine ineffable judgments, those whom magical potions, poisons, and sudden stranglings have slain: give rest with the saints, O Lord!

When Thou shalt judge all things, as they stand naked and uncovered before Thy face: then, O Bountiful One, spare those who have served Thee faithfully, O God!

When Thine Archangel shall sound the last trumpet for the resurrection of life of all: then, O Christ, give rest unto Thy servants!

Those whom Thou hast received in faith from the ages, O God, account worthy of the whole mortal race to glorify Thee unto the ages with those that glorify Thee!

*Glory... Triadicon:*
O Godhead in Trinity, co-enthroned: Father, Son, with the Holy Spirit: Thou art my God, holding all things in Thy sovereign power!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
O Forefather Jesse, leap for joy! From thy root has sprung the flower of life, Christ God, saving the world from the pure Maiden!

*Kontakion, Tone 8. Automelon:*[^929]
Settle in the tabernacles of the elect those who have been translated from among us from temporal things, and give rest with the righteous, O immortal Savior! For if as mortals they have sinned upon earth, yet do Thou, as the sinless Lord, forgive them their voluntary and involuntary transgressions, through the mediation of the Mother of God who bore Thee, that with one accord we may cry aloud over them: Alleluia!

*Ikos:*
Thou alone art immortal, Who didst fashion and make man; for we mortals were formed from the earth, and unto the same earth shall we return, as Thou didst command, Who didst fashion me and say unto me: "Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return," whither all we mortals go, making our funeral weeping a song: Alleluia!

*Ode 7. Heirmos: In the beginning Who didst lay the foundations of the earth, and didst establish the heavens by Thy word: blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers!*[^930]

*Troparia:*
Making commemoration of those who have departed from the ages in piety, we cry aloud: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers!

Those who have died suddenly in piety, fallen from every precipice, from tree, iron, or any stone: give rest, O God, unto those who have fallen asleep in faith!

At Thy fearful Coming, O Bountiful One, set at the right hand of Thy sheep those who in this life served Thee in Orthodoxy, O Christ, and have passed away unto Thee!

Rank Thy servants in the choir of Thine elect, O Christ, to cry aloud unto Thee: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers!

O bountiful Savior, Who from the dust of the earth didst fashion flesh and vivify it with the spirit: give rest, O God, in ageless life unto those whom Thou hast taken!

*Glory... Triadicon:*
As by three suns let the Godhead of the one Light in three Hypostases be hymned: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit: one nature, but three Persons!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
With one accord we sing unto thee the song of David, calling thee the Mountain of God, O Virgin, in which the Word dwelt in the flesh, deifying us spiritually within Himself!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Him Who was glorified on the holy mountain, and in the bush revealed the mystery of the Ever-Virgin by fire unto Moses: praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all the ages!*[^931]

*Troparia:*
Having shattered first the shadow of death, shining forth like the Sun from the tomb: make all who have died in faith sons of Thy resurrection, O Lord of glory, unto the ages!

O Witness of secret and hidden things, when Thou shalt reveal the works of darkness and expose our hearts: enter not into judgment with all who have fallen asleep in faith!

When Thou shalt sit upon the Throne, and command Thine elect to appear for judgment from the ends of the earth: then spare all, O Christ, as Thou art merciful!

Unto those who died suddenly by accident, from violent death and swift torrent, suffocation, strangling, and the stomping of horses, O Lord of glory: grant relief unto the ages unto those who have fallen asleep in faith!

*Bless the Father and the Son... Triadicon:*
I hymn Thee as Unity in essence, and I honor Thee as three Persons: Father, Son, and All-Holy Spirit; the unoriginate dominion of Thy Kingdom I glorify unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
A stream of living water and a sealed fountain hast thou been shown to be, O Virgin Mother of God: for having given birth unto the Lord without man, thou waterest the faithful with the water of immortality unto all the ages!

*We praise, we bless... Heirmos: "Him Who was glorified on the holy mountain..."*

*Ode 9. Heirmos: The childbearing of the Ever-Virgin, manifested of old on the mountain unto the Lawgiver by fire and the bush, for the salvation of us the faithful, we magnify with unceasing hymns!*[^932]

*Troparia:*
Where the dwelling of those that rejoice is, of Thy saints, O Lord: account worthy all who have fallen asleep from the ages in faith and in hope to rejoice!

Those who died by God's rebuke, by deadly thunders of all kinds poured out from heaven, swallowed by the gaping earth, or engulfed by the sea: give rest, O Christ, unto all the faithful!

From poisonous bites of serpents, from swallowing by beasts, from trampling by horses, and from strangling and hanging by one's neighbor: give rest unto those who in faith have served Thee!

Every age: the elder and the infant, the youth and the child, nursing babes, male and female: give rest, O God, unto the faithful whom Thou hast received!

Those who have died in faith from the ages and generation of generations, each by name: account them worthy to stand uncondemned before Thee, O Christ, at Thy Coming!

*Glory...*
O God one in Trinity, glory to Thee unceasingly: for though each is God, yet the Father, the Son, and the Spirit are one in essence by three-radiant properties!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Thy childbearing is beyond comprehension: for thou didst bear Him Who was before, and ineffably feddest with milk the Nourisher of the world, and heldest Him Who holds all things, Christ our only Redeemer, O all-immaculate one!

*Then: "It is truly meet..."*

*Exapostilarion, Tone 3, Podoben: "He that adorned the heavens with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣ́здами):*[^933]
Making commemoration of all the departed in Christ, let us, the faithful, remember also that final day, ever beseeching Christ on our own behalf and for them!

*Glory... Another Exapostilarion for the Dead:*
O Thou Who rulest over the living and the dead as God: give rest unto Thy servants, settle Thine elect; for though they sinned, O Word, yet they departed not from Thee!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Sweetness of angels, joy of the sorrowing, protectress of Christians, O Virgin Mother of the Lord: having interceded for us, deliver us from eternal torment!

*At the Praises, we set 4 Stichera, Tone 8, Podoben: "In Eden of old" (И҆́же въ є҆де́мѣ):*[^934]
