O Savior, Who by Thine own hand didst fashion Adam and set the bounds between incorruption and mortality, and by grace didst exchange corruption for life, restoring him unto the first life: do Thou Thyself, O Master, give rest with the righteous in the choir of Thine elect unto Thy servants whom Thou hast translated from us, and having inscribed their names in the Book of Life, raise them up at the voice of the archangel, at the sound of the trumpet, and account them worthy of Thy Heavenly Kingdom! *(Twice).*

O Savior, Who by Thy blood hast redeemed mankind, and by Thy death hast delivered us from bitter death, and by Thy Resurrection hast granted us life everlasting: give rest, O Lord, unto all that have fallen asleep in piety, whether in deserts, or in cities, or in the sea, or on land, or in any place: emperors, priests, hierarchs, monks, and laymen, in every age of the whole human race; and account them worthy of Thy Heavenly Kingdom!

Christ, having risen, loosed the bonds of Adam the first-formed, and destroyed the might of Hades: be of good cheer, all ye dead! Death is put to death, and Hades is led captive with it, and Christ is King, Who was crucified and is risen! He has bestowed upon us incorruption of the flesh; He raises us up, and grants us resurrection, and will account all worthy of that glorious joy who with faith and love have warmly trusted in Him!

*Glory... Tone 6:*
The tasting of the tree of old in Eden became grief unto Adam, when the serpent vomited forth his poison: for through it entered universal death, devouring man. But the Master having come overthrew the serpent, and granted us resurrection: let us therefore cry aloud unto Him: Spare, O Savior, and give rest with the saints unto those whom Thou hast taken, as Lover of mankind!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
By the prayers of her that bore Thee, O Christ, of Thy martyrs and apostles, prophets, hierarchs, venerable and righteous ones, and all the saints: give rest unto Thy departed servants!

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos: Stichera by Theophanes, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ᲊпова́нїе):*[^935]
Possessing incomprehensible tender mercy toward us, and an inexhaustible wellspring of divine goodness, O greatly merciful One: settle in the land of the living those who have passed away unto Thee, O Master! In beloved and longed-for dwellings, granting an inheritance that abides forever! For Thou didst shed Thy blood for all, O Christ, and didst redeem the world with a life-bearing price!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord [LXX Ps. 64:5].*
Having willingly endured life-creating death, Thou didst pour forth life and gavest everlasting sweetness unto the faithful, and divine loving-kindness, O Master, Who alone art all-bountiful and sinless: therein we pray Thee, rank those who have fallen asleep in the hope of the resurrection, granting remission of sins, that Thy Name may be praised above all things, O Christ, and being saved we may glorify Thy love for mankind!

*Verse: And their soul shall dwell among good things [LXX Ps. 24:13].*
Ruling over the living by Thy divine authority, and exercising mastery over the dead, we pray Thee with all our soul, O Christ: do Thou Thyself, O Lover of mankind, give rest unto Thy faithful servants who have departed unto Thee, the only Benefactor, with Thine elect, in places of refreshment, in the splendors of the saints! For Thou art the Desirer of mercy, and savest as God those whom Thou didst create according to Thine image, O Thou Who alone art abundant in mercy!

*Glory... Tone 6:*
Thy creative command was my origin and substance: for wishing to fashion a living being out of the invisible and visible nature, Thou didst form my body from the earth and gavest me a soul by Thy divine and life-creating breathing: therefore, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servants in the land of the living, in the tabernacles of the righteous!

*Both now... Theotokion, Same Tone [Tone 6]:*
Thou art our God, Who in wisdom createst and accomplishest all things: Thou didst send prophets, O Christ, to foretell Thy Coming, and apostles to proclaim Thy marvelous works! And the former indeed foretold Thy Coming, while the latter enlightened the nations through Baptism; and the martyrs suffering received what they longed for; and the choir of both prays unto Thee, together with her that bore Thee: give rest, as God, unto the souls whom Thou hast received, and account us worthy of Thy Kingdom, O our Redeemer and God, Who didst endure the Cross for our condemned works!

*Then: "It is good to give thanks unto the Lord..." The Trisagion. Then the Troparion: "O Thou Who by the depths of Thy wisdom..." Glory... Both now... "In thee we have a wall and a haven..." (see fol. 379)[^936]. And the customary Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the Canon, Ode 3 and Ode 6. Prokeimenon, Tone 6: Marvelous is God in His saints, the God of Israel [LXX Ps. 67:36]. Verse: In the congregations bless ye God, the Lord from the springs of Israel [LXX Ps. 67:27]. Another for the Departed: Their soul shall dwell among good things [LXX Ps. 24:13]. The Epistle, in Acts, Pericope 51 [Acts 28:1–31]; and another, Pericope 163 [1 Thess. 4:13–17]. Alleluia, Tone 6: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them [LXX Ps. 33:18]. Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord [LXX Ps. 64:5]. The Gospel from John, Pericope 67 [John 21:15–25]; and another, Pericope 21 [John 5:24–30]. Communion Hymn: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous [LXX Ps. 32:1]; and another: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken, O Lord [LXX Ps. 64:5]. Alleluia (thrice).*

# PART V: GREAT FEAST OF HOLY PENTECOST AND ALL SAINTS[^937]

## The Holy and Glorious Sunday of Pentecost

*On Saturday evening, at Little Vespers:*

*The Priest having given the blessing, we say: "O Heavenly King..." and the rest.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 4, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чино́въ):*[^938]
Now the nations are renewed to proclaim the marvelous works of God in strange tongues and with a vision of fire, for the assurance of all that dwell upon earth, to report openly now as a sign unto the nations: true salvation is come! *(Twice).*

The power from on high which Thou didst promise to send unto Thy disciples, O Christ, having accomplished it, Thou dost send Thy Holy Spirit, showing us that Thou art the Truth, and that those who hope in Thee, O Good One, shall truly never be put to shame!

Having fulfilled the promise of Thine own Comforter, Thou hast sent Him unto the world as in fiery tongues, to consume with divine fire the sins of all, and to grant unto us pure communion with Him, as we faithfully love Him!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 7:*
Having the Comforter Christ God before the Father, now that another Comforter is come upon earth unto us this day, let us worship with faith the Holy Spirit!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*[^939]
Enlightened in mind with the God-originating radiance, Thy disciples, O Word, essentially received the Holy Spirit!

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me [LXX Ps. 50:12].*[^940]

Tongues of fire from on high appeared upon the apostles, enlightening, yet not consuming them!

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me [LXX Ps. 50:13].*
That the fearful wonder might strike terror into the race of unbelievers, with other, strange tongues they proclaimed divine things!

*Glory... Both now... Same Tone [Tone 2] and Podoben:*
Having come from on high unto us, O Comforter, even as formerly unto the apostles, who preach Thee as God unto the Father and the Savior!

*Then: "Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..." The Trisagion. And after "Our Father..." Troparion: "Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God..." The Little Litany. And the Dismissal.*

*Mark's Chapter 103:*[^941] *If there should fall the feast of any saint having a vigil on the Sunday of Pentecost: if it is his temple, we sing his service, as for the Theologian with the Ascension (see fol. 343).*[^942]

*At Great Vespers:*

*After the customary Psalm [Ps. 103]. The entire Kathisma: "Blessed is the man..." [LXX Ps. 1:1],*[^943] *in which we sing nothing.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 Stichera, and sing Idiomel Stichera, Tone 1:*
We celebrate Pentecost, and the coming of the Spirit, and the appointed fulfillment of the promise, and the completion of hope, and the mystery, how great and honorable it is! Therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O Maker of all, Lord, glory to Thee! *(Twice).*

In foreign tongues Thou hast renewed Thy disciples, O Christ, that through them they might proclaim Thee, the immortal Word and God, Who grantest great mercy unto our souls!

The Holy Spirit provides all things: He pours forth prophecy; He consecrates priests; He taught wisdom to the unlearned; He revealed fishermen as theologians; He gathers together the entire concourse of the Church! O Comforter, consubstantial and co-enthroned with the Father and the Son: glory to Thee!

*Other Stichera, Tone 2:*
We have seen the true Light, and we have received the heavenly Spirit; we have found the true faith, worshipping the undivided Trinity: for the same has saved us![^944]

In the prophets Thou didst announce unto us the way of salvation, and in the apostles the grace of Thy Spirit shone forth, O our Savior: Thou art the first God, and Thou art after these, and unto ages Thou art our God! *(Twice).*

In Thy courts we sing of Thee, the Savior of the world, and bending our knees, we worship Thine unconquerable power: at evening, and at morning, and at midday, and at every season we bless Thee, O Lord!

In Thy courts, O Lord, we the faithful, having bent the knees of souls and bodies, hymn Thee, the unoriginate Father, and the co-unoriginate Son, and the co-everlasting and all-holy Spirit, Who enlightens and sanctifies our souls!

The consubstantial Trinity we praise in song: Father and Son, with the Holy Spirit; for thus all the prophets proclaimed, and the apostles with the martyrs!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8. Composition of Leo the Emperor:*[^945]
Come, O ye peoples, let us worship the tri-hypostatic Godhead: the Son in the Father with the Holy Spirit! For the Father timelessly begat the Son, co-everlasting and co-enthroned; and the Holy Spirit was in the Father, glorified with the Son: one power, one essence, one Godhead! Worshipping Whom, we all say: Holy God, Who didst create all things through the Son, by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit! Holy Mighty, through Whom we have known the Father, and the Holy Spirit came into the world! Holy Immortal, Comforter Spirit, Who proceedest from the Father and restest in the Son: Holy Trinity, glory to Thee!

*Then the Entrance. "O Gladsome Light..." The Prokeimenon of the day: "The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty..." [LXX Ps. 92:1].*

*The Readings. The First Reading [Numbers 11:16–17, 24–29]:*[^946]
The Lord said unto Moses: Gather unto Me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou thyself knowest to be the elders of the people, and their scribes; and thou shalt bring them unto the tabernacle of witness, and they shall stand there with thee. And I will come down and speak there with thee, and I will take of the Spirit that is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, and thou shalt not bear them thyself alone. And Moses gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle. And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto Moses, and took of the Spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy men, the elders; and as the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied in the camp, and ceased not. And there remained two men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad, and the Spirit rested upon them; and these were of them that were written, but they came not unto the tabernacle; and they prophesied in the camp. And a young man ran and told Moses, and said: Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp! And Joshua the son of Nun, who stood before Moses, his chosen one, answered and said: My lord Moses, forbid them! And Moses said unto him: Art thou envious for my sake? And who would grant that all the Lord's people were prophets, when the Lord shall put His Spirit upon them?

*The Reading of the Prophecy of Joel [Joel 2:23–32]:*[^947]
Thus saith the Lord: Ye children of Zion, rejoice, and be glad in the Lord your God: for He hath given you food unto righteousness, and He will rain down upon you the early and the latter rain, as before. And the threshing floors shall be full of wheat, and the presses shall overflow with wine and oil. And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpillar, and the palmerworm, My great army which I sent among you. And ye shall eat in plenty, and be satisfied, and praise the Name of the Lord your God, Who hath dealt marvelously with you: and My people shall never be put to shame. And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and there is none else: and My people shall never be put to shame. And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions. And on My bondmen and on My bondwomen in those days will I pour out of My Spirit, and they shall prophesy. And I will show wonders in the heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and notable day of the Lord come. And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on My Name shall be saved.

*The Reading of the Prophecy of Ezekiel [Ezekiel 36:24–28]:*[^948]
Thus saith the Lord: I will take you from among the nations, and gather you out of all foreign countries, and will bring you into your own land. And I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols will I cleanse you. And a new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. And I will put My Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in My statutes, and ye shall keep My judgments and do them. And ye shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and ye shall be My people, and I will be your God.

*At the Litiya, Stichera. Written at the Praises:*[^949]
Marvelous things have all the nations seen this day...

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*
When Thou didst send down Thy Spirit, O Lord, upon the sitting apostles, then the children of the Hebrews beholding were struck with terror at the wonder! For they heard them speaking in other, strange tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance; for being unlettered they were made wise, and catching the nations into faith, they spoke divine words! Therefore we also cry aloud unto Thee: Who didst appear on earth to save us, O Lord, glory to Thee!

*At the Aposticha, Idiomel Stichera, Tone 6:*
The nations, not understanding the power of the all-holy Spirit which came upon Thine apostles, O Lord, deemed the change of tongues to be drunkenness; but we, having been established by them, unceasingly say thus: Take not Thy Holy Spirit from us, we pray Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me [LXX Ps. 50:12].*[^950]
O Lord, the descent of the Holy Spirit, having filled Thine apostles, disposed them to speak in other tongues; therefore that marvelous wonder was deemed drunkenness by the unbelieving, but unto the faithful it was the mediator of salvation: of whose illumination account us also worthy, we pray Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me [LXX Ps. 50:13].*[^951]
O Heavenly King, Comforter, Spirit of truth, Who art everywhere and fillest all things, Treasury of good things and Giver of life: come and abide in us, and cleanse us from every impurity, and save our souls, O Good One!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*
Languages were once confounded because of the audacity of the tower-building; but now languages have been made wise because of the glory of the knowledge of God! There He condemned the impious for their transgression; here Christ has enlightened the fishermen by the Spirit! Then muteness was wrought for punishment; now harmony is renewed unto the salvation of our souls!

*Then: "Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart in peace..." Troparion, Tone 8:*[^952]
Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God, Who hast revealed the fishermen to be all-wise, having sent down upon them the Holy Spirit, and through them didst catch the universe: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee! *(Thrice).*

*The Blessing of the loaves. And the reading in the Homilies on the Acts of the Holy Apostles.*

*On the Same Sunday, at Matins. At "God is the Lord..."*
*The Troparion of the Feast (thrice). After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*[^953]
The midpoint of the feast, O ye faithful, and the final feast let us celebrate radiantly: this is Pentecost, the fulfillment of the promise and of the foretelling! For on this day the Comforter's fire came down upon earth as in the form of tongues, and enlightened the disciples, and revealed them as initiates of heavenly mysteries! The Comforter's Light is come and has enlightened the world! *Glory... and now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*[^954]
The wellspring of the Spirit having come upon earth, dividing mentally into fiery rivers, bedewed the apostles, enlightening them; and it became unto them a bedewing cloud, an enlightening fire, and raining down a flame, through which we have received grace by fire and water: the Comforter's Light is come, and has enlightened the world! *Glory... and now... the same.*

*And the reading in the Commentary of John: Homily 50. After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was mystically commanded" (Повелѣ́нное та́инственно):*[^955]
The lovers of Zion were filled with joy, and they who before were fearful received a sign: for the Holy Spirit this day came down from on high upon the house of the disciples, and each spoke differently unto the people! For the tongues were divided, being visible as fire; and it consumed them not, but rather bedewed them! *Glory... and now... the same.*

*And the reading in the Theologian, whereof the beginning is: "To philosophize briefly concerning the feast."*

*Gradual: 1st Antiphon of Tone 4: "From my youth..." Prokeimenon, Tone 4: "Thy good Spirit shall lead me in the land of uprightness [LXX Ps. 142:10].*[^956] *Verse: Hear my prayer, O Lord, give ear unto my supplication [LXX Ps. 142:1]. Let every breath praise the Lord. The Gospel from John, Pericope 65 [John 20:19–23]:*[^957] *On the same day at evening... End: whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained. "Having seen the Resurrection of Christ..." is not said. The kissing of the Gospel according to custom. Psalm 50. Then: Glory... Through the prayers of the holy apostles... Both now... Through the prayers of the all-pure Theotokos... Sticheron, Tone 6: "O Heavenly King..."*

*Canons of the Feast: two Canons. The Heirmoi of both Canons twice, the Troparia on 12; and after each Ode, one Choir sings the 1st Heirmos, and the other Choir the 2nd Heirmos.*

*Canon 1, Composition of Lord Cosmas the Monk,*[^958] *bearing the acrostic: PENTECOSTEN HEORTAZOMEN, which is: "Let us celebrate Pentecost." Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:*
He who overwhelmed Pharaoh and his chariots in the sea, shattering wars with a high arm: let us sing unto Him, for He is glorified!

*Troparion:*
In deed, as of old Thou didst promise unto the disciples, Thou hast sent the Comforter Spirit, O Christ, and hast made light to dawn upon the world, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
That which was proclaimed of old in the Law and the Prophets is fulfilled: for the grace of the divine Spirit has this day been poured out upon all the faithful!

*Another Canon, Iambic, Composition of Lord John of Damascus,*[^959] *Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Covered by divine darkness, the slow of tongue proclaimed the God-written Law; for having shaken off the mire from the eye of the mind, he beholds Him Who is, and is instructed in the knowledge of the Spirit, honoring Him with divine songs!

*Troparion:*
The pure and venerable lips said: There shall be no separation for you, O friends! For I, sitting upon the Father's throne, will pour forth the Spirit, to cause ungrudging grace to shine upon those who desire it!

*Troparion:*
Having passed the boundary, the most true Word quietly completes the heart: for having finished the work, Christ gladdened His friends, granting the Spirit with a rushing breath and fiery tongues, as He promised!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^960]
Thou saidst unto the disciples, O Christ: Tarry ye in Jerusalem, until ye be clothed with power from on high; and I will send another Paraclete like unto Myself, My Spirit and the Father's, wherein ye shall be established!

*Troparion:*
The power of the divine Spirit having come, united in one concord the voices that of old were wickedly divided, divinely instructing the faithful in the knowledge of the Trinity, wherein we are established!

*Another Heirmos [Second Canon]:*
Prayer of the prophetess Hannah of old loosed the bonds of a childless womb and the reproach of barrenness, bearing a contrite spirit unto the Mighty One and God of knowledge![^961]

*Troparion:*
Incomprehensible is the most divine Being: for making unlettered fishermen into eloquent orators, He bridles the mouths of the wise with the Word, and from deep night rescues countless peoples by the radiance of the Spirit!

*Troparion:*
Proceeding from the unbegotten Light was the all-powerful shining Light: Who now through the Son reveals the Father's authority, a kindred illumination, a fiery voice in Zion unto the nations!

*Hypakoe, Tone 8:*[^962]
The midpoint of the feast and the final feast, O ye faithful, let us celebrate radiantly: this is Pentecost, the fulfillment of the promise and of the ancient law! For on this day the Comforter's fire came down upon earth as in a vision of tongues, and enlightened the disciples, and revealed them as initiates of heavenly mysteries! The Comforter's Light is come and has enlightened the world! *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^963]
Perceiving Thy final coming, O Christ, the prophet cried aloud: I have heard Thy power, O Lord, that Thou art come to save all Thine anointed ones!

*Troparion:*
He Who spake in the prophets, and was proclaimed of old in the Law unto the imperfect: God the true Comforter, is this day made known unto the ministers and witnesses of the Word!

*Troparion:*
Bearing the token of Divinity, the Spirit was divided unto the apostles in fire, and appeared in strange tongues, as the divine Power of the Father coming forth, sovereign in authority!

*Another Heirmos [Second Canon]:*[^964]
O King of kings, only Word proceeding from the only unoriginate Father: as Benefactor Thou hast truly sent unto the apostles Thy Spirit of equal might, as they sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having mingled the divine bath of regeneration with the Word for composite human nature, Thou pourest forth a stream upon me from Thy non-corrupt pierced side, O Word of God, sealing it with the warmth of the Spirit!

*Troparion:*
All knees bend unto the Comforter, and unto the Son of the Father, and unto the kindred Father: for in three Persons they behold an essence truly intangible, timeless, one; for the light of the Spirit's grace has shone forth!

*Troparion:*
Let all be filled with the most divine Spirit, as many as are ministers of the tri-hypostatic Essence: for Christ accomplishes above nature as Benefactor, and forms anew unto salvation, manifesting the grace of the Spirit!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^965]
Conceived in the womb of the prophets through fear of Thee, O Lord, and brought forth upon earth, the Spirit of salvation creates clean hearts in the apostles, and in the faithful is renewed upright; for Thy commandments are light and peace!

*Troparion:*
This power that is come this day: the good Spirit, the Spirit of the wisdom of God, the Spirit proceeding from the Father and revealed unto us the faithful through the Son, is the Bestower in Whom the holiness of nature is planted and beheld!

*Another Heirmos [Second Canon]:*[^966]
Receive the fire-breathing dew of the Spirit as redemption and cleansing from sins, O radiant children of the Church! For now from Zion the Law has gone forth, the fiery grace of the Spirit in tongues!

*Troparion:*
Even as He willed sovereignly, the unmastered Spirit descends from the Father, making the apostles wise in tongues, sealing the life-bearing Word, conformable unto the Father, whereof the Savior spake!

*Troparion:*
That He might heal the thoughts of sins, God the unoriginate Word prepared the apostolic company as a most pure house, wherein now the consubstantial and essential Spirit comes to dwell!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^967]
Swimming in the tempest of worldly cares, and sinking with my fellow-sailors under sins, and cast out unto the soul-destroying beast: like Jonah, O Christ, I cry unto Thee: Lead me up from the death-bearing deep!

Thou didst richly pour out of Thy Spirit upon all flesh, as Thou saidst, and all things were filled with Thy knowledge, O Lord: for from the Father the Son was incorruptibly begotten, and the undivided Spirit proceeded!

*Another Heirmos [Second Canon]:*[^968]
O Master Christ, Thou hast caused cleansing and salvation to dawn unto us from the Virgin, that like as from the belly of the sea beast Thou didst snatch the prophet Jonah, Thou mightest deliver Adam who had fallen with his whole race!

*Troparion:*
Do Thou, O Almighty One, renew within our inward parts the true and upright Spirit proceeding from the Father, which we have received together: Who consumed the defilement of hostile matter, and is the Cleanser of filth from our thoughts!

*Troparion:*
Unto the apostles who longed for their inheritance, and unto the dwellers in Zion who awaited Thy coming, the Spirit makes known the kindred Word of the Father, swiftly showing the harsh insolence of heathen flatteries, and establishing them in fire-breathing power!

*Kontakion, Tone 8:*[^969]
When the Most High came down and confused the tongues, He divided the nations; but when He distributed the tongues of fire, He called all to unity: and with one voice we glorify the all-holy Spirit!

*Ikos:*
Grant swift and steadfast consolation unto Thy servants, O Jesus, when our spirits grow despondent! Depart not from our souls in afflictions, be not far from our thoughts in tribulations, but ever anticipate us! Draw near unto us, draw near, Thou Who art everywhere present: and even as Thou wast ever with Thine apostles, so also unite Thyself unto those that love Thee, O Bountiful One, that united unto Thee we may hymn and glorify Thine all-holy Spirit!

*Prologue.*

*Synaxarion for the Sunday of Pentecost:*[^970]

*Verse: By a rushing breath Christ imparts the Spirit;*  
*By a flame and fiery tongues He distributes Him.*  
*Verse: The Holy Spirit appeared in these seven great days;*  
*And was richly given unto the fishermen disciples.*  

On this day, the eighth Sunday after Pascha, we celebrate the Holy Pentecost. This feast also we have received from the Hebrew books; for they celebrate Pentecost among them, honoring the number seven, because fifty days after Passover having passed, they received the Law. So also we, celebrating fifty days after Pascha, receive the all-holy Spirit, Who lays down the law and guides into all truth, and commands what is well-pleasing unto God.

Be it known that among the Hebrews there were three feasts: Passover, Pentecost, and Tabernacles (that is, the honoring of booths). Passover indeed they kept in remembrance of the passage through the Red Sea; for *Pascha* is interpreted *Passage*. Such a feast was a type of our passage from the darkness of sin back unto Paradise, and our restoration. And Pentecost they celebrated in remembrance of their affliction in the wilderness, and how through many sorrows they were brought into the Promised Land; for then they enjoyed the fruit of wheat and wine: and this feast showed our affliction from unbelief and our entrance into the Church, for then we also partake of the Master's Body and Blood. Some indeed say that for this cause Pentecost was celebrated among the Hebrews; but others say it was because of the fifty days wherein Moses, having fasted, received the God-written Law, together commemorating the sacrifice of the calf and other things which Moses did upon going up and coming down the mountain. Unto others it was thought that Pentecost was devised among the Hebrews for the honor of the number seven, as was said; for that number, being multiplied by itself, makes fifty, wanting one day. And the honor of the sevenfold number among the Hebrews is not only in days, but also reaches unto years, whereof is the Jubilee, which they celebrate, interpreted *Remission*; for this happens in the forty-ninth year, when they leave the land unsown, and grant rest unto animals, and command purchased slaves to go free. And the third feast, Tabernacles (that is, the honoring of booths), was celebrated after the gathering of fruits, which is five months after the feast of Passover: this was celebrated in memory of the day wherein Moses first pitched the booth seen on Mount Sinai, prepared by the cloud, and fashioned by Bezaleel. And making booths, they kept this feast, abiding in the fields, thanking God as they gathered the fruits of their labors.

David also seems to have written concerning the winepresses in the Psalms: and that feast was a type of our resurrection from the dead, when our bodily tabernacles having been dissolved and fashioned anew, we shall receive the fruits of our labors, celebrating in everlasting tabernacles! And it is meet to know that on that day when Pentecost was fulfilled, the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples: and the holy Fathers themselves determined to separate the feasts, because of the majesty of the all-holy and life-creating Spirit, seeing that He is One of the holy and life-originating Trinity; therefore we also shall declare on the morrow how the Holy Spirit came. Through the prayers of the holy apostles, O Christ God, have mercy upon us, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^971]
Cast into the fiery furnace, the venerable youths turned the flame into dew, singing thus in praise: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
While the apostles proclaimed the divine wonders, the operation of the Spirit was deemed drunkenness by the unbelieving, through Whom the Trinity is made known, the one God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Orthodoxly we theologize the undivided Essence: God the unoriginate Father, and the Word and Spirit of the same authority, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another Heirmos [Second Canon]:*[^972]
The harmonious melody of musical instruments sounded to honor the lifeless golden image; but the light-bearing grace of the Comforter inspires us to cry: O only Trinity, equal in might and unoriginate, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
The foolish voice did not understand the prophetic speech, declaring to be wine-wrought drunkenness what they heard as strange speech from the apostles; but we the pious divinely cry aloud unto Thee: O Benefactor of all, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
The divine Joel thundered forth the divine teaching of the vision of the supreme Godhead, saying of the Word: I will pour out My Spirit upon those who cry: O brightly shining threefold Light of nature, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
The third hour divided the grace in appearance, that we might honor the three hypostases in simplicity of authority: but now on this one day of the Lord, blessed is the Son, the Father, and the Spirit!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^973]
The bush that shared communion with God without being burned in Sinai showed God unto Moses slow of tongue and halting in speech; and the zeal of God showed forth the three youths unconsumed by fire as singers: Praise the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Troparion:*
At the life-bearing, rushing, sonorous breath of the mighty Spirit from on high, the wonders of God were proclaimed in fiery tongues unto the fishermen: Praise the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Troparion:*
Ascending as unto the untouchable mountain, not fearing the terrible fire, come and let us stand upon Mount Zion, in the city of the living God, rejoicing now with the Spirit-bearing disciples: Praise the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

*Another Heirmos [Second Canon]:*[^974]
The thrice-radiant image of the Godhead looses bonds and refreshes the flame: the youths sing praise, and all created nature blesses the only Savior and Creator as Benefactor!

*Troparion:*
The Spirit brings to remembrance the words of Christ that nourish mankind, which He heard of the Father and spake unto the apostles, comforting them with a blessed, rich vision in fiery tongues; and ordered creation sings praise unto Thee!

*Troparion:*
Savingly sovereign alone, being Light self-bestowing and the Giver of light, Thou art come filling the apostles, O honorable Head of Thy servants, and bestowing the Spirit Who satisfies!

*Troparion:*
The Spirit-filled lips of the prophet sang of Thy bodily coming with the King, and the Spirit proceeding from the Father's bosom, uncreated, creative, co-enthroned with Thee, honored by the faithful of one doctrine!

*"More honorable than the Cherubim..." is not sung. Ode 9. Heirmos: Not having known corruption...*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^975]
Not having known corruption through experience of birth, yet lending flesh unto the all-wise Word: O unwedded Mother, Virgin Theotokos, receptacle of the Uncontainable, dwelling-place of Thine illimitable Maker, Thee do we magnify!

*Troparion:*
Carried rejoicing on the burning fiery chariot of old, the fire-breathing zealot prefigured the breath from on high that has now shone forth upon the apostles: enlightened by Whom, they proclaimed the Trinity unto all!

*Troparion:*
Contrary to the law of nature, a strange thing was heard from the disciples: for when one voice spake by the grace of the Spirit, peoples, tribes, and nations heard in different ways the marvelous works of God, being instructed in the knowledge of the Trinity!

*Another Heirmos [Second Canon]:*[^976]
Rejoice, O Queen, glory of mothers and virgins! For every eloquent and God-inspired mouth cannot oratorically hymn Thee worthily: every mind is confounded in comprehending Thy childbearing; therefore with one voice we glorify Thee!

*Troparion:*
It was meet to praise the naturally life-bearing Maiden: for she alone concealed within her womb the Word, Who heals the diseased nature of mankind; Who now sitting at the right hand of the Father's realm, has sent forth the grace of the Spirit!

*Troparion:*
As many as have been breathed upon by the God-flowing grace, shining, sparkling, changed with a strange and most comely change, having recognized the indivisible wisdom of equal power, we glorify the thrice-radiant Essence!

*Then the Katavasia: both Heirmoi together.*

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "He that adorned the heavens with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣ́здами):*[^977]
O all-holy Spirit, proceeding from the Father, and through the Son having come unto the unlettered disciples: save and have mercy upon all who have known Thee as God! *(Twice).*

*Glory... Both now... Another Exapostilarion:*
Light is the Father, Light is the Word, Light is also the Holy Spirit: Who was sent unto the apostles in fiery tongues, and through Whom the whole world is enlightened to worship the Holy Trinity!

*At the Praises, we set 6 Stichera, and sing Idiomel Stichera, Tone 4:*[^978]
Marvelous things have all the nations seen this day in the city of David, when the Holy Spirit descended in fiery tongues, as Luke the God-proclaimer wrote: for he said: When Christ's disciples were gathered together, there came a sound as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting; and they all began to speak in strange tongues, with strange teachings, and strange commandments of the Holy Trinity! *(Twice).*

The Holy Spirit ever was, and is, and shall be: having neither beginning nor ending, but ever joined and numbered with the Father and the Son: Life, and Life-creator; Light, and Giver of light; essentially Good, and Wellspring of goodness: through Whom the Father is known, and the Son is glorified, and by all is recognized: one power, one union, one worship of the Holy Trinity! *(Twice).*

The Holy Spirit is Light and Life, a living, noetic Fountain: Spirit of wisdom, Spirit of understanding; Good, Upright, Noetic, ruling, cleansing offenses; God and deifying; Fire proceeding from the Father, speaking, operating, distributing gifts: through Whom all the prophets and divine apostles were crowned with the martyrs: a strange hearing, a strange sight, fire divided for the imparting of gifts!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 6:*
O Heavenly King, Comforter, Spirit of truth, Who art everywhere present and fillest all things: Treasury of good things and Giver of life: come and abide in us, and cleanse us from every impurity, and save our souls, O Good One!

*Then the Great Doxology. Troparion. Litany. And the Dismissal thus:*
Thou Who in the appearance of fiery tongues didst send down Thine all-holy Spirit upon Thy holy disciples and apostles: Christ our true God, through the prayers of His all-pure Mother, of the holy, glorious, and all-praised apostles, and of all the saints, will have mercy upon us and save us, as He is good and the Lover of mankind! *Then the First Hour. And the Catechesis of St. Theodore the Studite. And the final Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy. First Antiphon [LXX Psalm 18]:*[^979]
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands [LXX Ps. 18:2].*  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Verse: Day unto day pours forth speech, and night unto night proclaims knowledge [LXX Ps. 18:3].*  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Verse: There are no speeches nor words, in which their voices are not heard [LXX Ps. 18:4].*  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Verse: Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world [LXX Ps. 18:5].*  
*Refrain:* Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!  
*Glory... Both now...*  
Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us!

*Second Antiphon [LXX Psalm 19]:*  
*Verse: The Lord hear thee in the day of affliction, the Name of the God of Jacob protect thee [LXX Ps. 19:2].*  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Good Comforter, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia! *(Thrice).*  
*Verse: Send thee help from the sanctuary, and support thee out of Zion [LXX Ps. 19:3].*  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Good Comforter...  
*Verse: The Lord grant Thee according to Thy heart, and fulfill all Thy counsel [LXX Ps. 19:5].*  
*Refrain:* Save us, O Good Comforter...  
*Glory... Both now...*  
*Only-begotten Son... (sung quietly).*

*Third Antiphon [LXX Psalm 20]:*  
*Verse: The King shall rejoice in Thy strength, O Lord, and in Thy salvation shall He greatly exult [LXX Ps. 20:2].*  
*Troparion, Tone 8:* Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God...  
*Verse: Thou hast given Him the desire of His heart, and hast not withheld from Him the request of His lips [LXX Ps. 20:3].*  
*Troparion:* Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God...  
*Verse: For Thou hast anticipated Him with blessings of goodness, Thou hast set upon His head a crown of precious stone [LXX Ps. 20:4].*  
*Troparion:* Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God...

*Then the Entrance. The Priest, or the Deacon if there be one: "Wisdom! Stand upright!" And we sing the verse from Psalm 20: "Be Thou exalted, O Lord, in Thy strength; we will sing and praise Thy mighty acts!" [LXX Ps. 20:14]. Troparion: "Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God..." Glory... Both now... Kontakion: "When the Most High came down..."*

*Take note that what is here indicated we also perform on other feasts wherein we sing Antiphons. Instead of the Trisagion, we sing: "As many as have been baptized into Christ..." [Gal. 3:27]:*[^980]  
*Tone 1: As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia (thrice). And the fourth time: Glory... Both now... Have put on Christ. Alleluia. And again the whole: As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia.*

*Prokeimenon, Psalm 18, Verse 4, Tone 8: Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world [LXX Ps. 18:5].*[^981] *Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands [LXX Ps. 18:2].*

*The Epistle, in Acts, Pericope 3 [Acts 2:1–11]:*[^982] *In those days, when the day of Pentecost was fully come...*

*Alleluia, Psalm 32, Verse 6, Tone 1: By the Word of the Lord were the heavens established, and all the host of them by the Spirit of His mouth [LXX Ps. 32:6].*[^983] *Verse 13 of the same Psalm: The Lord looked down from heaven, He beheld all the sons of men [LXX Ps. 32:13].*

*The Gospel from John, Chapter 7, Pericope 27 [John 7:37–52; 8:12]:*[^984] *In the last day, that great day of the feast...*

*Communion Hymn, Psalm 142, Verse 10: Thy good Spirit shall lead me in the land of uprightness [LXX Ps. 142:10].*[^985] *Another from Psalm 50, Verse 13, Tone 8: Take not Thy Holy Spirit from us, we pray Thee, O Lover of mankind! Alleluia.*

*On Sunday of Pentecost, in the Evening. The klepalo is sounded quickly for the sake of the service of the Kneeling:*[^986]

*The Priest having given the blessing, we say: "O Heavenly King..." The Trisagion; and after "Our Father...", "Lord, have mercy" (12 times). Glory... Both now... "O come, let us worship..." (thrice). Then the Psalm: "Bless the Lord, O my soul..." [Ps. 103]. We sing: Glory... Both now... Alleluia (thrice). Then the Great Litany:*

**Deacon:** In peace let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the peace from above and the salvation of our souls, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the peace of the whole world, the good estate of the holy churches of God, and the union of all, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For this holy house, and for them that with faith, reverence, and the fear of God enter therein, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For our most holy Archbishop, the Ecumenical Patriarch *(Name)*; for our honorable presbyterate, the diaconate in Christ, for all the clergy and the people, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For our Great King *(Name)*, and our pious sovereigns, princes, and lords, for all their palace and armed forces, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That He may aid them and subdue under their feet every enemy and adversary, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the deliverance of our fathers and brethren held captive, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For this city, and for every city, village, and countryside, and monastery, and for the faithful that dwell therein, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For seasonable weather, abundance of the fruits of the earth, and peaceful times, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For them that travel by sea, by land, the sick, the suffering, the imprisoned, and for their salvation, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the people here present, who await the grace of the Holy Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For them that bow their hearts and their knees before the Lord, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That He may be bountiful unto all of us, souls and bodies, who righteously with faith and reverence are gathered together in this all-pure temple: let us pray unto the Lord.[^987]
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That we may be accounted worthy of healing and the incorrupt grace of the Holy Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That we may be a temple and dwelling place of the Holy and Life-creating Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That God may preserve us unceasingly to abound in the Holy Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That we may find grace and mercy of the All-Holy Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the manifestation, that we may be partakers of the Holy Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the reception unto remission of sins, and knowledge of spiritual grace, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That we may not be alien unto the Holy Spirit in the fearful and righteous tribunal of Christ, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the granting of rich mercy, bounties, and the grace of the Holy Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That in the Holy Spirit all bonds of the enemy may be loosed for us, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For the salvation from on high of us who bow our hearts with faith and bend our knees on this fiftieth day, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That the Lord our God may hear us sinners, and send down upon us the Holy Spirit, and cleanse us, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That we may ever worship with soul and body, and sing unto the Holy and Consubstantial Trinity in unity, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That the Lord God may be well-pleased toward us who have bent our knees, and send down upon us His Holy Spirit, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That our genuflections and prayers may be acceptable before Him as the odor of spiritual incense, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** That we may be priests of the divine illumination of the true and life-creating Trinity, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** For our deliverance from all tribulation, wrath, and necessity, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** Help us, save us, have mercy upon us, and protect us, O God, by Thy grace.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy.  
**Deacon:** Commemorating our all-holy, pure, most blessed and glorious Lady, the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary, with all the saints, let us commend ourselves and one another, and all our life unto Christ our God.  
**Choir:** To Thee, O Lord.  

*Then the Priest exclaims:*  
**Priest:** For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.  
**Choir:** Amen.  

*See below concerning the Finding of the Precious Head of the Prophet Isaiah (see fol. 315).*[^988]  

*Then at "Lord, I have cried," we set 6 Stichera, and sing Idiomel Stichera, Tone 4: "Marvelous things have all the nations seen this day..." (repeating them). Glory... Both now... Tone 6: "O Heavenly King..." (written above at the Praises, see fol. 394).*  

*The Entrance with the censer. "O Gladsome Light..." The Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*[^989]  
*Who is so great a God as our God? Thou art the God Who doest wonders!*  
*Verse 1: Thou hast declared Thy power among the peoples.*  
*Verse 2: And I said: Now have I begun; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High.*  
*Verse 3: I remembered the works of the Lord.*  
*And again: Who is so great a God as our God?...*  

*Then the Priest or the Deacon exclaims:*  
**Deacon:** Again and again, bending the knees, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy *(thrice).*  

*And with all of us bending our knees upon the ground, and having our heads uncovered and bowed down, the Superior or the Priest reads these Prayers from the sanctuary with a loud voice in the hearing of all, in a compunctionate voice, and not hurriedly:*  

*THE FIRST PRAYER:*[^990]  
**Priest:** O Lord, pure, undefiled, without beginning, invisible, incomprehensible, unsearchable, unchanging, unsurpassed, immeasurable, long-suffering Lord, Who alone hast immortality, dwelling in light unapproachable: Who madest heaven and earth and the sea and all that in them is; Who grantest unto all their petitions before they ask: we ask Thee and pray Thee, O Master, Lover of mankind, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and of Mary the Ever-Virgin and all-glorious Theotokos: Who first indeed taught by words, and afterward showed by deeds, when He endured the saving Passion, giving unto us, Thy humble, sinful, and unworthy servants, an example to offer supplications unto Thee, in the bending of the neck and knees, for our sins and for the ignorances of the people: do Thou Thyself, O greatly merciful Lover of mankind, give ear unto us in whatsoever day we call upon Thee, and especially on this fiftieth day, whereon after the Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ into heaven, and His sitting at the right hand of Thee, God and Father, He sent down the All-Holy Spirit upon His holy disciples and apostles, Who also sat upon each one of them:

and they were all filled with His inexhaustible grace, and began to speak in other tongues Thy marvelous works, and prophesied:[^991] now therefore give ear unto us who pray unto Thee, and remember us, humble and condemned, and turn back the captivity of our souls, having Thy mercy interceding for us: receive us who fall down before Thee, and cry: We have sinned! Unto Thee were we cast from the womb, from the belly of our mother Thou art our God. But because our days have vanished in vanity, we are stripped of Thy help, and deprived of all defense: but trusting in Thy compassions, we cry: Remember not the sins of our youth and our ignorances, and cleanse us from our secret faults; look upon our lowliness, and cast us not off in the time of old age; when our strength fails, forsake us not: before we return unto the earth, make us worthy to return unto Thee, and attend unto us with favor and grace; measure our iniquities with Thy compassions, set the abyss of Thy bounties against the multitude of our sins. Look down from the height of Thy sanctuary, O Lord, upon Thy people who stand before Thee, awaiting the rich mercy that is from Thee: visit us with Thy goodness; remember us in Thy compassions; deliver us from the oppression of the devil; establish our life with Thy holy and sacred laws; commit Thy people unto a faithful guardian angel; gather us all into Thy Kingdom; grant mercy unto those who hope in Thee; forgive them and us our offenses; purify us for the operation of Thy Holy Spirit; destroy the snares of the enemy that are set against us!

*He also appends this prayer:*[^992]  
Blessed art Thou, O Lord Almighty, Master and God, Who hast enlightened the day with the light of the sun, and illumined the night with rays of fire; Who hast granted us to pass through the length of the day, and to draw near unto the beginnings of the night: give ear unto our supplications and those of all Thy people; and having forgiven us all our voluntary and involuntary sins, receive our evening supplications, and send down the multitude of Thy mercy and Thy compassions upon Thine inheritance; defend us with Thy holy angels; arm us with the armor of Thy righteousness; nail us unto Thy truth; guard us with Thy power; deliver us from every adversity, and from every assault of the adversary: and grant unto us the present evening with the coming night, perfect, holy, peaceful, sinless, free from scandal, and without fantasy, and all the days of our life: through the prayers of the holy Theotokos, and of all the saints who from the ages have been well-pleasing unto Thee!

*Then the Deacon says:*  
**Deacon:** Help us, save us, have mercy upon us, raise us up, and protect us, O God, by Thy grace.  
Commemorating our all-holy, pure, most blessed Lady...  
*Then the Priest gives the Exclamation:*  
**Priest:** For Thine it is to have mercy and to save us, Christ our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.  
**Choir:** Amen.  
*After this the Deacon says:*  
**Deacon:** Let us all say with our whole soul, and with our whole mind let us say:  
*And the rest of the customary Litany.*  
*The Priest gives the Exclamation:*  
**Priest:** For a merciful and man-befriending God art Thou, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.  
**Choir:** Amen.  
*Then the Deacon:*  
**Deacon:** Again and again, bending our knees, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy *(thrice).*  
*Then the Priest reads:*  
*THE SECOND PRAYER, with a loud voice:*[^993]  
**Priest:** O Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who hast given Thy peace unto men, and the gift of the All-Holy Spirit, while still present with us in this life, ever granting unto the faithful an indefeasible inheritance:

and Who didst most manifestly send down this grace unto Thy disciples and apostles this day, and didst establish their lips with fiery tongues:[^994] through whom the whole human race having received the knowledge of God in our own tongues into the hearing of the ear, we have been enlightened with the light of the Spirit, and delivered from delusion as from darkness; and by the distribution of visible fiery tongues and by a supernatural operation, we were taught faith in Thee, and were enlightened to bless Thee, with the Father and with the Holy Spirit, in one Godhead, and power, and dominion: Thou therefore, O Effulgence of the Father, the unchanging and immutable Image of His essence and nature, O Fountain of wisdom and grace: open also the lips of me, a sinner, and teach me how it is meet, and for what things it is necessary to pray: for Thou art He Who knowest the great multitude of my sins, but Thy compassion shall overcome their countless number: for behold, I stand before Thee in fear, having cast the despair of my soul into the depth of Thy mercy: govern my life, Thou Who guidest all creation with a word by the ineffable power of wisdom, O quiet Haven of those caught in storm: and show me the way wherein I should walk. Grant the Spirit of Thy wisdom unto my thoughts; bestow the Spirit of understanding upon my foolishness; overshadow my deeds with the Spirit of Thy fear; and renew an upright Spirit in mine inward parts; and with a governing Spirit establish the slip of my thoughts: that being guided every day toward what is profitable by Thy good Spirit, I may be made worthy to do Thy commandments, and ever to remember Thy glorious coming, and the searching scrutiny of the deeds wrought by us: and suffer me not to be deceived by the corruptible allurements of this world, but strengthen me to desire the attainment of the treasures to come. For Thou hast said, O Master: Whatsoever anyone asks in Thy Name, he receives without hindrance from Thy co-eternal God and Father. Therefore also unto me, a sinner, at the coming of Thy Holy Spirit, do Thou grant Thy grace: whatsoever I have asked, render unto me for salvation! Yea, O Lord, Giver of every good endowment, and rich Giver of good things, for Thou art He Who grantest superabundantly beyond what we ask. Thou art He Who forgivest and hast compassion, having without sin become a Partaker of our flesh; and bowing down in loving compassion unto those who bend their knees unto Thee, having become the cleansing of our sins: grant therefore unto Thy people Thy compassions; give ear unto us from Thy holy heaven; sanctify them by the power of Thy saving right hand; cover them with the shadow of Thy wings; despise not the works of Thy hands: against Thee alone have we sinned, but Thee alone do we serve; we know not how to worship a strange god, nor to stretch out our hands, O Master, unto an alien god: forgive us our offenses, and receiving our kneeling supplications, extend unto all of us the hand of help; receive the prayer of all as acceptable incense,[^995] taken up before Thy most good Kingdom!

*He also appends this prayer:*

O Lord, Lord, Who hast delivered us from every arrow that flies by day, deliver us also from every thing that walks in darkness;[^996] receive the evening sacrifice, the lifting up of our hands; vouchsafe us also to pass through the course of the night blamelessly, untempted of evils; and deliver us from every disturbance and fear that comes unto us from the devil: grant compunction unto our souls, and care unto our thoughts concerning the trial of Thy fearful and righteous judgment: nail our flesh with Thy fear, and mortify our members that are upon the earth, that even in the quiet of sleep we may be enlightened by the vision of Thy judgments. Remove from us every unseemly fantasy and harmful lust. And raise us up at the time of prayer, established in faith, and advancing in Thy commandments!

*Then the Deacon says:*  
**Deacon:** Help us, save us, have mercy upon us, raise us up, and protect us, O God, by Thy grace.  
Commemorating our all-holy, pure, most blessed Lady...  
*The Priest gives the Exclamation:*  
**Priest:** Through the good will and grace of Thine Only-begotten Son, with Whom Thou art blessed, together with Thine All-Holy, Good, and Life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.  
**Choir:** Amen.  
*Then:*  
*Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin...*  
*And after this the Deacon says:*  
**Deacon:** Again and again, bending our knees, let us pray unto the Lord.  
**Choir:** Lord, have mercy *(thrice).*  
*Then the Priest reads:*  
*THE THIRD PRAYER:*[^997]  
**Priest:** O ever-flowing, living, and illuminating Fountain, O creative Power co-eternal with the Father, Who hast most excellently fulfilled the whole dispensation for the salvation of mankind, O Christ our God: Who didst shatter the unbreakable bonds of death and the bolts of Hades, and didst trample down the host of evil spirits; Who offeredst Thyself as a blameless sacrifice for us, and gavest Thy most pure Body as an offering untouched and impassable unto any sin; and through this fearful and ineffable sacred rite didst grant us eternal life: Who descendedst into Hades, and didst shatter the eternal bars, and showedst an ascent unto those who sat below; and didst ensnare the primevally evil and abyssal serpent with God-wise allure, and boundest him with chains of darkness in Tartarus, and in unquenchable fire and outer darkness, shutting him in by Thine immeasurable might: O greatly renowned Wisdom of the Father, Who didst appear as a great Helper unto the afflicted, and didst enlighten those that sit in darkness and the shadow of death: Thou, Lord of eternal glory, and beloved Son of the most high Father, eternal Light from eternal Light, Sun of righteousness: give ear unto us who pray unto Thee, and give rest unto the souls of Thy servants, our fathers and brethren who have fallen asleep before us, and our other kinsmen according to the flesh, and all who are of the household of faith, for whom also we now make remembrance: for in Thee is the dominion over all, and in Thy hand Thou holdest all the ends of the earth! O Master Almighty, God of our fathers and Lord of mercy, Creator of the mortal and immortal race, and of all nature, both compounded and again dissolved; of life and of ending, of our sojourning here and of our translation thither: Who measurest the years for the living, and assignest the times of death; Who bringest down into Hades and leadest up; Who bindest in weakness, and settest free in power; Who orderest the present things profitably, and directest the things to come unto salvation:

Who cheerest with the hope of resurrection those who are wounded with the sting of death! Thou Thyself, Master of all, God our Savior, the Hope of all the ends of the earth, and of those far off upon the sea: Who also on this final, great, and saving day of the Feast didst show forth unto us the mystery of the Holy, Consubstantial, Co-eternal, Undivided, and Unconfused Trinity; and didst pour out the descent and coming of Thy Holy and Life-creating Spirit in the appearance of fiery tongues upon Thy holy apostles, appointing them as proclaimers of the pious faith, and showing them to be confessors and heralds of true theology: and Who on this all-perfect and saving Feast hast deigned to receive propitiatory supplications for those held in Hades, granting great hopes of relief and comfort to be sent down from Thee for those held in afflictions: give ear unto us, Thy humble servants who pray unto Thee! And give rest unto the souls of Thy servants who have fallen asleep before us, in a place of light, in a place of verdure, in a place of refreshment, whence all sickness, sorrow, and sighing have fled away; and establish their spirits in the habitations of the righteous, and vouchsafe them peace and relief:[^998] for the dead shall not praise Thee, O Lord, nor shall those who are in Hades dare to offer confession unto Thee; but we the living bless Thee and pray Thee, and offer unto Thee propitiatory prayers and sacrifices for their souls!

*He also appends this prayer:*[^999]  
O God, great and eternal, holy and Lover of mankind, Who hast counted us worthy to stand at this hour before Thine unapproachable glory, for the singing and praise of Thy marvelous works: be merciful unto us, Thine unworthy servants, and grant grace that with a contrite heart and without haughtiness we may offer unto Thee the thrice-holy doxology, and thanksgiving for Thy great gifts, which Thou hast wrought for us and dost work at all times! Remember, O Lord, our weakness, and destroy us not with our iniquities, but show great mercy in our lowliness: that having escaped the darkness of sin, we may walk in the day of righteousness, and having put on the armor of light, we may remain unassailed by any snare of the evil one, and with boldness may glorify in all things Thee, the only true God and Lover of mankind! For Thine in truth is the great and mighty mystery, O Master of all and Creator: the temporal dissolution of Thy creatures, and their subsequent reassembly and eternal rest! Unto Thee do we give thanks in all things: for our entry into this world, and for our departure, which by Thy unfailing promise pre-pledge unto us the hope of resurrection and incorruptible life, which may we attain in the future at Thy second coming! For Thou art both the Author of our resurrection, and the living, unfeigned, and man-befriending Judge of those who have lived, the Master and Lord of retribution, Who didst intimately partake of our flesh and blood, through extreme mercy and condescension, and didst willingly submit Thyself unto temptation to the sharing of our blameless passions, receiving the compassion of bounties; and wherein Thou Thyself hast suffered being tempted, Thou hast become a self-pledged Helper unto us who are tempted: therefore also Thou hast raised us up into Thy dispassion: receive therefore, O Master, our prayers and supplications, and give rest unto each one's father, and mother, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and kinsmen, and all the souls that have fallen asleep before us: in the hope of resurrection and eternal life, write their spirits and names in the book of life, in the bosoms of Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the land of the living, in the Kingdom of heaven, in the paradise of delight, through Thy radiant angels, leading all into Thy holy habitations, raising up also our bodies in the day which Thou hast appointed, according to Thy holy and unfailing promises! There is no death, O Lord, for Thy servants when we depart from the body and come unto Thee our God, but a translation from things most sorrowful unto things most blessed and joyful, and rest and joy: and if we have sinned in anything against Thee, be merciful unto us and unto them: for none is pure from stain before Thee, even though his life be but one day, save Thou alone, our Lord Jesus Christ, Who didst appear sinless upon the earth: through Whom we all hope to obtain mercy and the remission of sins: therefore unto us and unto them, as Thou art good and the Lover of mankind, remit, pardon, and forgive our offenses, voluntary and involuntary,

those in knowledge and those in ignorance, manifest and unmanifest, those in deed, those in thought, those in words, and those in all our walkings and movements: and unto those who have departed grant freedom and relief; and bless us who are here present, granting a good and peaceful end unto us and unto all Thy people, and opening unto us the bowels of mercy and love of mankind at Thy fearful and dread coming, and make us worthy of Thy Kingdom!

*In the Greek collections the Prayers conclude immediately thus:*[^1000]  
*For Thou art the rest of our souls and bodies, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.*  
*And thou, if thou wilt conclude without offense.*  
*In some books, however, the final Prayer at Vespers is appended by the Priest.*  
*The customary prayer is said: "O Lord, great and most high..." written in the Sluzhebnik at Vespers, and it is possible for thee to append it. However, let it be according to discretion whether this or another applies. But if anyone does not wish to follow the Greek books, let him read the following Prayer, not concluding the aforesaid: which is not found in the Greek collection.*

*The Prayer appended after these prayers, addressed specifically unto the Holy Spirit, the composition of the Most Holy Patriarch of Constantinople, Kyr Philotheus:*[^1001]  
O Heavenly King, Comforter, Master, co-unoriginate and co-eternal, sharing the same fountain and equal in honor, O Spirit with the Father and the Son, true Spirit, existing, good, holy, ruling, and life-creating, proceeding ineffably from the Father, and resting indivisibly upon the Son, Receptive of adoption and deification of noetic and rational nature, Treasury of present and future good things: upright Spirit, good Spirit, of the Father's essence, and from all His divine and unoriginate lips, ineffably proceeding:[^1002] hypostatic Breath, and Wisdom and Power: Spirit of God and from God, Spirit of the Father and from the Father, Spirit of the Son, Spirit of Christ: the former because of the one essence whence is the procession, the latter again because of the one and indivisible essence, and the speaking and manifestation from thence: Thou therefore, O good Master, one God of the Trinity, true God from true God: Who together with the Father and with the Son didst create the rational and sensory creation, and dost sustain and preserve it by ineffable wisdom and power, and at all times through the design of ineffable providence, providentially preserving and confirming it beyond comprehension: O unoriginate, invisible, incomprehensible, unsearchable, unfathomable, ineffable, innumerable, infinitely powerful, Almighty Lord: Who formerly didst diversely operate and speak in the fathers and the prophets, and didst show forth the mystery of the Holy Trinity, and didst conceal the ineffable bodily dispensation of the Only-begotten Son and God; and afterward, upon His bodily ascension into heaven and His session, and on this great and perfect saving Pentecostal Feast, for the sake of Thy natural gifts and grace, didst enlighten the world as with the substantial appearance of fiery tongues, and didst sit upon the holy apostles and disciples, and by Thy divine power didst clothe them, and didst fill them with supernatural and ineffable grace, according to the unfailing promise of Christ: through whom all human nature having received the word of faith, we were taught true knowledge of God and grace, and being enlightened by Thy ineffable power and operation,

hast taught us to worship the one God in three Persons alone. Thou Thyself, O Master, the Illumination of the Father, the living and unchanging Image of the Father, together with the Son the immutable Image and the seal of their essence and nature, and the Fountain of sanctification, immortality, and life, in the future unchanging and unending age, the crown and ultimate reception of the saints, wherein is the Cause and Fountain of the Godhead, the one unbegotten and unoriginate Father and God, with the Only-begotten Son and God, the bestowal of all things, unforgotten and ineffable, operating beyond nature in the present and future life: receive the supplication of me, a sinner and unworthy, and Who alone knowest the multitude of all my sins: have mercy upon me according to Thy great mercy, and according to the multitude of Thy compassions cleanse mine iniquities; and wash away thoroughly the mire of my sins, and cleanse the besetting foulness of the passions of my soul: O only pure and undefiled One, and Cleanser of every foulness of stench and passion: cleanse me from my secret faults, O Lord, and deliver Thy servant from those that are foreign; remember not the sins of my youth, and of mine ignorance, and of the wretchedness of mine old age: enlighten my darkened noetic eyes, and rekindle the extinguished lamp of grace; teach my mind by what manner and operation it may know that the Holy Spirit is truly in rational nature! Grant me a word of good cheer, and power, and height, and strength, and strength, that pure and outstretched prayers may ever be offered for Thy people, and for Thy universal Church and flock: which by Thy power and operation, redeemed by the blood of the Only-begotten Son and God, Thou hast divinely established and composed: confirm it upon the rock of the confession of the Godhead, unyielding and unshakable, mightier than the gates of Hades, more powerful and higher than countless heresies, untouched and uninjured in eternal operations and strength, filled in every way with Thy strength and grace! Receive, O King, their genuflections and groanings, their common, united, and outstretched prayers, and their diligent supplications, in faith and hope, that they may look steadfastly unto Thee alone night and day, and gaze upon none other save Thee, our God and Master, and expect salvation from Thee alone; and forgiving them and us every offense, voluntary and involuntary: as Thou art a God most good and almighty, turn away present evils, and make us worthy of eternal blessings: by the mercy and love of mankind of God the Father, and of the Holy Son, and of Thee, the All-Holy and Co-honored Spirit, the one tri-hypostatic Godhead, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Then the Deacon says:*  
**Deacon:** Help us, save us, have mercy upon us, raise us up, and protect us, O God, by Thy grace.  
Commemorating our all-holy, pure...  
*The Priest gives the Exclamation:*  
**Priest:** For Thou art the rest of our souls and bodies, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.  
**Choir:** Amen.  
*After this:*  
**Deacon:** Let us complete our evening prayer unto the Lord... *And the rest.*  
Commemorating our all-holy, pure...  
*The Priest gives the Exclamation:*  
**Priest:** For Thou art a good God and the Lover of mankind...  
**Priest:** Peace be unto all.  
**Deacon:** Bow your heads unto the Lord.  
*The Priest reads the customary secret Prayer, which is: "O Lord our God, Who didst bow the heavens..."*  
*Then the Exclamation:*  
**Priest:** Blessed and glorified be the majesty of Thy Kingdom: of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.  
**Choir:** Amen.  
*And immediately they divest, and in the midst of the church we sing:*

*At the Aposticha, Idiomel Stichera, Tone 3:*[^1003]  
Now for a sign unto all have the tongues visibly appeared: for the Jews, from whom Christ came according to the flesh, having been sick with unbelief, fell away from the grace of God; and we who are from the Gentiles have been accounted worthy of the divine light, being established by the words of the disciples, who proclaim the glory of God, the Benefactor of all. With these, bending our hearts with our knees, in faith let us worship the Holy Spirit, Who is proclaimed as the Savior of our souls!

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me [LXX Ps. 50:12].*[^1004]  
Now the Comforter Spirit has been poured out upon all flesh: for beginning from the choirs of the apostles, from them the grace has been extended unto the faithful by participation; and He confirms His sovereign coming in the form of fire, distributing tongues unto the disciples for the hymning and glory of God: therefore, enlightened noetically in our hearts, and established in faith, let us pray unto the Holy Spirit, that our souls may be saved!

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me [LXX Ps. 50:13].*[^1005]  
Now are the apostles of Christ clothed with power from on high: for the Comforter renews them, being renewed in them by a mystical renewal of understanding; who proclaiming in strange and lofty voices, honor the eternal nature and the simple tri-hypostatic Godhead of God, the Benefactor of all: therefore, enlightened by their teachings, let us worship the Father with the Son and the Spirit, praying that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*  
*Come, O ye peoples, let us worship the tri-hypostatic Godhead... (see fol. 387).*

*Come, O ye peoples, let us worship the tri-hypostatic Godhead... (see fol. 387).*  
*Then: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart... The Trisagion. And after the Our Father, the Troparion of the Feast: Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God... And the Dismissal: see in the Sluzhebnik.*

*Note: It is meet to know that this week of Holy Pentecost is free from fasting on Wednesday and Friday.[^1006] For monks: milk, cheese, eggs, fish, wine, and oil. For laymen: meat. The Mid-Hours of the Hours are also omitted, and the Canon of the Theotokos sung at Compline is suspended.*

*Chapter 116. When the Paschal Key is 'N', then May 25 is the Third Finding of the Precious Head of the Holy Forerunner John.[^1007] At this Feast and others: We sing his office together with that of the Holy Spirit. At Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," we set 8 Stichera: Feast 4, and Forerunner 4. Glory... Forerunner. Both now... Feast. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the Feast. Readings of the Forerunner, 3. Then the Prayers. And after this the Litanies. If there is a Litiya, we sing Glory... Forerunner. Both now... Feast. At the Aposticha: Stichera of the Holy Spirit. Glory... Forerunner. Both now... Feast. After the Trisagion: Troparion of the Forerunner. Glory... Both now... Feast. And the Dismissal. At Matins, we sing the entire office as for the Theologian, with Mid-Pentecost. Likewise also at the Divine Liturgy: written at the Feast of Mid-Pentecost (see fol. 276).*

*Note: The office of the saint of the day is sung wherever and whenever the Ecclesiarch decides.*

*ON THE SAME PENTECOST SUNDAY. AT COMPLINE.*  
*We sing the Canon to the Holy Spirit. The composition of Theophanes. Tone 4.*[^1008]  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*[^1009]  
Israel, having escaped the slavery of the people, traversed the impassable sea as dry land; and beholding the enemy drowned, sings a hymn unto God the Benefactor, Who works wonders with a high arm, for He has been glorified!

*Troparion:*  
O divine Holy Spirit, Who distributest endowments unto all, and workest all things by Thy will: breathe into me Thy light-bearing endowment, that I may glorify Thee, joined with the Father and the Son!

*Troparion:*  
O Comforter, Who gavest grace unto the heavenly powers of Thy thrice-holy inspiration: cleanse also the vessel of my mind, and show it to be filled with Thy sanctification!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
O Fountain of life, Who art found to be a stream of divine grace, O Holy Spirit of God: having quickened my mortified mind, raise it up by Thine operation to sing of Thy goodness!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Thou wast indeed the temple of God by the descent of the Spirit, by Whose creative power He granted strength unto Thy childbearing, O full of grace. Rejoice, O thou who gavest birth in the flesh unto the unoriginate Word!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*[^1010]  
Unto the Son begotten incorruptibly of the Father before the ages, and in these latter times incarnate of the Virgin without seed, unto Christ God let us cry aloud: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Having by nature the fountain power of will, creating as God for the heavenly and supramundane hosts, the Holy Spirit unceasingly teaches them to cry: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Troparion:*  
With unceasing praises, the God-proclaimed apostles magnifying the grace of the Spirit like a storm, harmoniously with the bodiless choirs glorify Him, crying: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
The one Goodness and Godhead, one Power, one Beginning, and one Kingdom of the Holy Trinity let us hymn with holy voice, crying: Holy art Thou, O Lord!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
O chariot-bearing and radiant Habitation, all-pure One, thou wast higher than the Cherubim, having borne God upon thine arms: therefore with one voice we hymn thee, O pure One: Rejoice, all-blessed Maiden!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*[^1011]  
A rod from the root of Jesse, and a blossom from it, O Christ, Thou hast budded forth from the Virgin; from the mountain overshadowed and densely forested Thou art come, incarnate from an unwedded Mother, O immaterial God: glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Great endowments has the All-Holy Spirit poured out upon the apostles: coming as divine, as good, as fulfilling the masteries, as deifying, as sanctifying, as the creative, sovereign, and self-governing Lord of all!

*Troparion:*  
Sitting upon the Father's throne, O Christ, Thou hast sent down the Comforter unto Thy disciples, as Thou didst promise, O Savior: sending Him as God Who comes, not as alien, but as the Creator of all, proceeding from the Father!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*
