The depths of the future did the All-Holy Spirit teach through the tongues of the prophets of old: and through the tongues of the all-wise apostles He proclaims with the sound of a rushing mighty wind the marvelous works of God, now sacredly abiding with them!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
We call thee the Gate of the noetic Light, O Mother of God, through which Christ entered unto us, fair in the divine beauty of Godhead in the flesh; covered with that garment, He Who was invisible as God has now become visible like unto us!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*[^1012]  
Being the God of peace and the Father of bounties, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy great counsel, granting peace: therefore, guided unto the light of the knowledge of God, watching early out of the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*  
O Spirit of wisdom, and fear of God, and truth, and light, and understanding, Who grantest peace: come and dwell within us, that being illuminated by Thy commandment, and watching early out of the night, we may glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*  
Upholding all things, and being Lord over all, Who preservest creation from falling: grant us holiness and illumination, that being satisfied with Thy bestowal of light, watching early out of the night, we may glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
Of old He Who inscribed the Law for Moses clearly sets forth the commandments of the New Testament and the law of grace, having written them upon the hearts of the apostles: the divine Comforter, having come as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Thou hast annulled the curse of Eve, the mother of all, by thy childbearing, O Virgin, having shone forth Christ as a blessing unto the world: therefore rejoicing with lips and disposition, confessing thee truly as the Theotokos, we bless thee!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^1013]  
The sea monster spewed out Jonah unharmed from its belly as an infant, just as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth preserving her incorrupt: for He Who suffered no corruption Himself preserved her who bare Him uninjured!

*Troparion:*  
Fulfilling the promise unto Thy disciples, O Christ, Thou didst send them the Spirit, granting the single operation of great wonders, and pouring forth gifts in fiery-form tongues, that the flocks of the Gentiles might be filled with the knowledge of Thee!

*Troparion:*  
Come unto us, O Holy Spirit, making Thy partakers partakers of holiness, and of never-setting light, and of divine life, and of most fragrant distribution: for Thou art the River of Godhead, proceeding from the Father through the Son!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
Save, O Comforter, those who faithfully hymn Thy divine coming, Who proceedest through the Son; and cleanse us from every defilement, as Thou art compassionate, and show us worthy of Thine illumination, making us spotless mirrors by Thy most God-beholding light!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
The abyss of prophecies mystically taught concerning thee, foreseeing the mystery of the ineffable and divine incarnation of God the Word, proclaimed thee as Virgin Mother: for thou hast revealed the truest and ancient Light!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*[^1014]  
The Children nurtured in piety, disregarding the ungodly command, feared not the threat of fire; but standing in the midst of the flame, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
Now is the fulfillment of Christ's promise accomplished:

for the division of tongues declared unto the disciples the coming of the Spirit, radiating from the one transcendent Godhead of the Trinity!

*Troparion:*  
Of old the senseless agreement of tongues was divided, but now they are manifestly gathered into one composition, through the wonder-working and divine Spirit Himself, One of the transcendent Trinity!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
At the breath of the Holy Spirit carried from on high, the apostles of Christ proclaimed with marvelous voice the mighty works of God, singing in harmony: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
The three Children in the furnace prefigured the image of thy childbearing: for as they remained unconsumed by the fire, so wast thou preserved pure, having received in thy womb the unendurable Fire, the blessed God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^1015]  
The prefigured image of a supernatural wonder: for the furnace burned not the youths whom it received. So neither did the Fire of the Godhead burn the Virgin's womb into which it entered: therefore let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:*  
O Holy Spirit, proceeding from the Father, granting holiness unto all who believe in Thee, for Thou art holy and the Bestower of holiness unto men: therefore singing, we cry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:*  
Thou grantest the gift of grace as Benefactor unto those who hymn Thee, O Comforter, for Thou art the Giver of good things and an ocean of grace: therefore praising Thee, we sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
True and life-creating is the Spirit, self-moved, self-governing, distributing the distribution of gifts as He wills, sovereign, self-commanding, unoriginate: Whom we now worship and sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Who marvels not at the exceeding multitude of Thy compassions, O unoriginate Word? For for our sake, being rich, Thou didst become poor, and didst dwell in the womb of the holy Virgin: therefore singing, we cry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*[^1016]  
Rejoice, virgin glory! Rejoice, all-pure Mother: whom all creation magnifies with divine hymns!

*Troparion:*  
Behold, Thou hast sent down unto us another Comforter, O Thine Only-begotten Word, co-enthroned with Thy Father!

*Troparion:*  
Save from temptations, O Comforter, those who confess Thee as co-enthroned, and who glorify Thine eternal being!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
Come unto us, O Comforter, satisfying us with Thy comfort, as we theologically praise Thine ineffable glory!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
O all-immaculate Bride of God, deliver from temptations by thy prayers those who worthily honor thee!

## ON MONDAY OF THE HOLY SPIRIT[^1017]

*AT THE MIDNIGHT OFFICE:*  
*After "I believe in one God...": After the first Trisagion, we say the Troparion of the Feast. After the second Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Feast. Hypakoe: 12 times. And the Dismissal. The prayers for the departed are not said.*

*AT MATINS:*  
*At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, thrice.*  
*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*[^1018]  
We sing and hymn, glorify and honor, together with the Father and the Son, the All-Holy Spirit, in one Godhead, divided by personal property: for thus did the apostles of Christ ...the apostles, to teach others and together to preach unto all the world. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́йно):*  
After Thy Resurrection from the tomb, O Christ, and Thy divine Ascension unto heavenly heights, Thou didst show Thy glory from on high unto the beholders of God, renewing an upright Spirit in the apostles: whence, as a musical instrument, with a divine lute, they clearly proclaimed unto all the mystery of Thy dispensation and providence, O Savior. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Then, both Canons of the Feast: of Tone 7, with Heirmos, to 8; and of Tone 4, with Heirmos, to 6. Katavasia: Covered by the divine... both choirs together. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast. After Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast.*

*Synaxarion on Monday after Pentecost, of the Holy Spirit:*[^1019]

*Verses:*  
*{ For every breath praises Christ;*  
*{ The Spirit, by Whom every hostile spirit is expelled.*  

On this day, Monday of Pentecost, we celebrate the All-Holy, Life-Creating, and All-Powerful Spirit Himself, one of the Trinity, God, equal in honor, consubstantial, and equal in glory with the Father and the Son. For on this fiftieth day He descended substantially upon the holy Apostles, having appeared in the form of fiery tongues, and sat upon each one of them in the Upper Room where they were abiding. And out of reverence unto the All-Holy Spirit, the holy and divine Fathers, having well ordered all things, divided the feast and decreed that this day also should be celebrated as Pentecost: for the Savior, before His holy Passion, promised the coming of the Comforter, saying:[^1020] *It is expedient for you that I go away; for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come.* And again: *When He, the Spirit of truth, is come, He will teach you and guide you into all truth.* And again: *I will pray the Father, and He will send you another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, Who proceeds from the Father.* And after the Passion again, when He was ascending into the heavens, He said: *Tarry ye in Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high.*

He sends Him, when the days of Pentecost were being fulfilled, as they were abiding together. At the third hour of the day in the Upper Room, suddenly there was a sound from heaven as of thunder, so that the multitude of the inhabited earth ran together; and the Holy Spirit appeared in the likeness of fiery tongues upon each one of them, not only unto the Twelve, but also unto the Seventy; and they spoke in strange tongues, that is to say, each apostle spoke the tongues of all tribes—not that the apostle spoke his own tongue and the foreigner understood, but the apostle heard and spoke the tongue of each nation. And some among the gathered peoples thought they were drunk; for each did not comprehend how an apostle spoke especially unto all, and they thought this was drunkenness. But others wondered, saying: *What does this mean?* For these were gathered from all the earth because of the feast: Parthians, Medes, and Elamites, who had a short time before been taken captive by Antiochus.

Ten days after the Ascension having passed, the All-Holy Spirit comes, and not immediately then after the Ascension, in order that He might make the disciples who awaited Him even more fervent.[^1021] Some also say this: that on each day, each one of the nine angelic ranks bowed down before the coming of that deified Flesh: nine days therefore having been fulfilled, on the tenth day the Comforter came. We are transformed by sleep; and fifty days after Pascha He comes in commemoration of the Old Law: for when Israel crossed the Red Sea, fifty days having passed, they received the Ten Commandments. Behold also the signs: there a Mountain, here an Upper Room; there fire, and here fiery tongues; and instead of thunder and darkness, an exceedingly violent wind. And in the appearance of tongues the Holy Spirit descended, showing that He hath a kindred nature with the living Word; or also because the apostles were about to teach and bring the nations into the tongues; and in fiery tongues, because God is a consuming fire, and for the sake of purification; and divided, because of the gifts that were to be distributed. And as He once divided and confused into many the single tongue of those of old, so now also in those who knew one tongue He divided it into many, that He might gather together from all nations those who had been dispersed unto the ends of the inhabited earth. And it takes place at the Feast, that, a greater multitude of people being gathered, the report of the wonder might go forth through all the inhabited earth, so that even those who happened to be at Pascha and had seen the miracles wrought by Christ might now again be filled with wonder. On the fiftieth day it was fitting...

...it was fitting that in the very time when of old the Law was given, in that same time also the grace of the Holy Spirit should be poured out: as Christ also did, when at the legal Passover He accomplished His own Passover, the true Passover.

And the Holy Spirit sat not upon the mouths, but upon the heads of the apostles, embracing that which is divine, and the highest part of the body, the mind itself, from which also the tongue hath its power of speech; or as a certain image, the Spirit uttering a sound by tongues, as if to ordain the apostles to be teachers of the whole world under heaven: for ordination (that is, cheirotonia) takes place upon the heads. The sound and the fire occurred because these took place also at Sinai: that the same Spirit might be shown to be both then and now, enacting the Law and ordering all things. And the multitude of the people was troubled by the rushing sound of the wind, because they thought it was the end of the world, as Christ foreshowed unto the Judeans concerning their destruction. And He said "as of fire," lest anyone should think anything bodily concerning the Holy Spirit: for they accused the apostles of drunkenness; but Peter, standing up and speaking forth in the midst of the people, refuted them, showing that what was said by them was not adhering to the truth: and he brought forward the prophecy of Joel as witness, and brought from among them unto divine knowledge about three thousand souls.

And the Holy Spirit is called Comforter because He is able to comfort and give rest unto us: for instead of Christ we have received Him, and in Him we have Christ: for He also intercedes for us with unutterable groanings unto God, as our Lover of mankind and Advocate, as is Christ also: for He too is a Comforter. On this account the Holy Spirit is called "another Comforter": for the Apostle says: *We have an Advocate [Comforter], Jesus, with God.* And "another" was said on account of consubstantiality: for to say "another and another" (*allos kai allos*) is of identical substance and nature, whereas "another and another [thing]" (*heteron kai heteron*) we know is said of different natures. This Holy Spirit is consubstantial with the Father and the Son in all things; therefore together with Them He creates all things, and that very resurrection which is to be, and whatsoever He wills He does: He sanctifies, He divides, He fashions anew, He sends forth, He makes wise, He anoints the Prophets; and to speak simply, in all things He is self-governing, all-powerful, good, upright, sovereign: by Him all things receive life and motion, whatsoever is partaker of holiness and of any life: simply, He hath all things that the Father and the Son have, except unbegottenness and begottenness, proceeding from the Father alone.

The Holy Spirit having been poured out upon all flesh, the whole world was filled with all manner of graces; and thereby all nations were guided unto divine knowledge, and every disease and every plague was driven away. And thrice by Christ was the Holy Spirit given unto the disciples: before the Passion obscurely; after the Resurrection by breathing, more effectually; and now He hath sent Him down substantially: or rather, He Himself descended, perfectly enlightening and sanctifying them, and through them bringing the ends of the inhabited earth unto God. By the visitation of His holy coming, through the prayers of the holy Apostles, O Christ our God, have mercy on us, both now and ever and unto ages of ages. Amen.

*After Ode 9, the Exapostilarion of the Feast, thrice.*

*At the Praises, we set 4 verses, and sing Stichera Idiomela, Tone 2:*  
We have seen the true Light, and we have received the heavenly Spirit; we have found the true faith, worshipping the undivided Trinity: for She hath saved us.

*Sticheron:*  
In the Prophets Thou didst announce unto us the way of salvation, and in the Apostles hath shone forth, O our Savior, the grace of Thy Spirit: Thou art God first, and Thou art the same hereafter, and unto the ages Thou art our God.

*Sticheron:*  
In Thy courts I sing Thee, the Savior of the world, and bending the knees I worship Thine invincible Power: evening and morning and at midday, and at every time I bless Thee, O Lord.

*Sticheron:*  
In Thy courts, O Lord, the faithful bending the knees of souls and bodies, we hymn Thee, the All-Holy Father, and the co-unoriginate Son, and the co-eternal and All-Holy Spirit, Who enlightens and sanctifies our souls.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*  
Once the tongues were confounded... (see fol. 384)[^1022]

*Then, the Great Doxology. Troparion of the Feast. Litany, and Dismissal. And the First Hour.*

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Feast, Odes 3 and 6.*[^1023] *Introit: Be Thou exalted, O Lord, in Thy strength; we will sing and praise Thy mighty acts. Troparion: Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God... Glory... Both now... Kontakion: When the Most High came down... Trisagion. Prokimenon, Tone 6: Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance. Verse: Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry, O my God. Epistle to the Ephesians, pericope 229 [Eph. 5:8b–19].*

...*Brethren, walk as children of light... Alleluia, Tone 2: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy. Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me. Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 75 [Matt. 18:10–20]: The Lord said: Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones... Communion Verse: Thy good Spirit shall lead me in the land of uprightness.*

*It is fitting to know that throughout this entire week, at Vespers, the Stichera of the Feast are sung first at "Lord, I have cried"; then 3 from the Menaion for the saint of the day; Glory... Both now... the Idiomelon of the Feast; at the Aposticha, the Stichera of the Feast with their own verses. For the Oktoechos (that is, the Eight Tones) is not sung. At Matins, we sing the Canon, alternating both authors to 6, and repeating the Heirmoi, so that there may be 8 in all; and for the saint of the day to 4, until Friday. On Friday at Vespers there is the usual order of the Feast; likewise at Matins on Saturday, and the Apodosis of the Feast takes place, as thou shalt see in order.*

*On the same Monday, in the evening, at "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses, and sing 3 of the Feast, and 3 from the Menaion.*

*Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
Marvelously powerful, co-enthroned, co-directed, and co-unoriginate with the Father and the Word is the Holy Spirit, Creator and co-eternal, All-Good, All-Ruling: having nourished the disciples of the Word, He made them wise in tongues and in diverse voices to proclaim the mighty acts of God and the doctrine of the Trinity.

*Sticheron:*  
Those obscured by the drunkenness of lack of understanding, the manifold gathering of nations, seeing the disciples of God speaking high things in the Spirit, called them drunkards in diverse tongues, while they themselves were engulfed in the drunkenness of deceit: but having recognized Thee through them, O God-loving Savior, we are saved.

*Sticheron:*  
O ever-flowing Fountain, ceaselessly pouring forth the ineffable river of grace, ever welling up with living water, equally overflowing and gushing out: by its outpourings water my soul, delivering me from the furnace of passions, and from the flame of cruel burning, and from fiery torment!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 4:*  
We celebrate Pentecost... (at the Litiya, fol. 386)[^1024]

*Then, "O Gladsome Light," and the rest.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*  
Thou grantest from on high unto Thy people, O King of all, remission of sins, having shown us to be temples for the All-Holy Spirit.

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
A rushing sound from heaven, as if borne along by a violent wind, plainly entered the house where the disciples were.

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
In deed unto the disciples, as Thou didst promise, O Word, Thou hast sent Thy divine and Holy Spirit, and hast illumined them.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 4:*  
The Holy Spirit provides all things... (search before, fol. 387)[^1025]

*Then, "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart," the Troparion of the Feast, and the Dismissal.*

## ON TUESDAY AFTER PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*  
Ordering, hymning together, glorifying together, and honoring together the Holy Spirit with the Father and the Son, in one Godhead, distinguishing by hypostatic properties: for thus did He clothe Christ's apostles today, to preach throughout all the world in surpassing wisdom. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́ро предвари́):*  
As Thou didst promise sovereignly, distributing unto Christ's apostles, Thou didst unite into one harmony of faith in the uncreated Trinity, by different tongues...

...the division of tongues: but [show] Thy magnificent deeds in us, O good Lover of mankind, we pray Thee. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast: Tone 7, to 6, and Heirmos twice, so that there may be 8 in all; and of the Menaion for the Saint, to 4. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast, twice.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тридне́вно воскре́слъ е҆сѝ):*  
The Holy Spirit, Light proceeding from Light, came upon earth in fiery tongues, to consume sins, for those who worship in faith the Tri-hypostatic Godhead.

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
Renew in us, O God, the All-Holy Spirit, Whom of old having sent unto Thy disciples, Thou didst strengthen them, O Compassionate One, to fulfill Thy saving purposes in the world.

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
Unto the All-Holy Spirit, faithfully theologizing, let us cry aloud: Depart not from us, O Good Comforter, Who bestowest cleansing upon all and enlightenest those who hymn Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 4:*  
Renewing with foreign tongues... (at the Litiya, fol. 386)[^1026]

*Then, the First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On the same Tuesday, at the Beatitudes, Refrains:*  
*Tone 2, Ode 2 Heirmos: True is God...*  
*Troparion:*  
O upright Spirit, guide onto the upright paths those who theologize Thee!

*Troparion:*  
O Comforter Who hast come from the heavens, save those who sing unto Thee!

*Troparion:*  
O Life life-creating, and Light existing, O Comforter, save those who sing unto Thee!

*Troparion:*  
God, true Son and Benefactor, O Comforter, save those who sing unto Thee!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Thou hast given birth, O Virgin Mother, unto true God for our salvation: Him do thou entreat for us all!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: In the furnace of fire...*  
*Troparion:*  
Unto the all-wise disciples gathered in the Upper Room, tongues were suddenly seen being divided, as if fiery, and the sound of a violent wind was heard, as they exalted Christ above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:*  
Christ the Comforter hath graciously sent down unto us the good Comforter, the Spirit Who spoke in the Prophets, and speaking in fiery tongues of the divinely-eloquent and all-wise apostles!

*Troparion:*  
The Fountain of gifts, the Bestower of good things, the Spirit Comforter having come unto Christ's disciples and anticipating, renewed them, having caused the light of piety to shine forth through them!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Unto Him Who rests indivisibly together in the bosom of the Father, having taken up His dwelling in thy mortal womb, O honored Virgin Bride of God, we sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: He Who from God is God the Word...*  
*Troparion:*  
He Who enlightens the angelic choirs and pilots the heavenly ranks as good: He hath now come down from heaven, and having made the all-wise apostles exceedingly wise with divine radiances, hath sent them unto the inhabited earth!

*Troparion:*  
The Holy Spirit openly distributes the wealth of the Godhead, abiding and unexhausted, unto the apostles in fiery tongues: and He hath made them more intense than flame, consuming the foul mire of idols!

*Glory... Troparion:*  
O Spirit of truth and understanding, O Spirit of wisdom, and might, and light, proceeding from the Father, and for the Son's sake richly given unto creation: save us who worship Thy dominion in faith!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
O all-blessed Virgin, all my hope fervently...

...I place upon thee: save me, O Mother of Life, and vouchsafe me, O pure one, to be filled with the eternal food, that in faith and love in songs I may magnify thee.

*On Tuesday evening, at "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses: 3 of the Feast, and 3 from the Menaion.*

*Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*  
The Holy Spirit, distributing gifts, came upon earth, not as of old in the shadow of the Law shining forth in the Prophets, but substantially now hath been granted unto us through the mediation of Christ: let us purify our hearts with virtues and receive His coming, being mystically enlightened.

*Sticheron:*  
Take not Thy Holy Spirit from us, O Lover of mankind, but grant grace unto those who have lived worthily, in soul and heart, that we may fittingly accommodate His joint refuge, to be temples and dwellings for the Comforter, O Jesus our God, Savior of our souls.

*Sticheron:*  
Unto the Holy Spirit Who enlightens all things, let us devoutly sing, and in faith let us cry: Having come into the world by the good pleasure of the Father, depart not from us, and in the presence of Thy Godhead, make us abodes of Thine ineffable grace, and sanctify all who faithfully sing unto Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 6:*  
The nations, not understanding, O Lord, the power of the All-Holy Spirit... (fol. 384)[^1027]

*Then, "O Gladsome Light of the holy glory."*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́снымъ чинѡ́мъ):*  
How fearful, how contrary to nature, that fiery tongues of the rational heaven should proclaim unto the nations the glory of God, Who adorned the heavens with fire, and illumined the sensible world, together with the Son and the Spirit!

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
Unto Christ's disciples gathered in Sion, as the promise was made, the Holy Spirit came upon them in the appearance of fire, and showed them to be inspired with fire, radiating the teachings of the Trinity in the mystical proclamation.

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
The sacred disciples, forged like iron swords, the Holy Spirit having come made complete: therefore they cleansed the earth for God the Creator, having hewn down the unhallowed, so that the weapons of the evil one vanished, and salvation came unto our souls.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 6:*  
O Lord, the descent of the Holy Spirit upon Thine apostles... (see fol. 384)[^1028]

*Then, "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart," the Troparion of the Feast, and the Dismissal.*

## ON WEDNESDAY AFTER PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*  
The spiritual grace having come from poor fishermen, hath enlightened Thine apostles, O Christ, as all-wise princes: through whose teachings we also ever celebrate the bright feast of Pentecost, hymning Thee together with the Father and the divine Spirit. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Guiding unto wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости наста́вниче):*  
The All-Holy Spirit having now descended upon the apostles in the appearance of fire, filled the gatherings of nations with wonder: for as they spoke in fiery tongues, O Lover of mankind, each heard his own language; and the wonder seemed unto the unbelievers as drunkenness, but unto the faithful truly salvation was recognized...

...was recognized: therefore we glorify Thy dominion, O Christ God, asking remission of sins to be sent richly upon Thy servants. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast, and of the Menaion. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*  
Having come from on high unto us, O Comforter, as formerly unto the apostles, sanctify and save those who proclaim Thee as God.

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
Suddenly from heaven, the Power of the divine Comforter showed all the apostles to be all-wise fishers of God.

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
Illumined by the divine-originating radiance, having enlightened their mind, Thy most sacred disciples, O Word, received the Holy Spirit.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 6:*  
O Heavenly King, O Comforter... (fol. 384)[^1029]

*Then, the First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On the same Wednesday, at the Beatitudes, Refrains:*  
*Tone 3, Ode 3 Heirmos: O Firm Foundation...*  
*Troparion:*  
He Who established the heavenly hosts, the Comforter Spirit, today hath shown the apostles to be heavens.

*Troparion:*  
Worshipping the Spirit, consubstantial, equal in power, co-enthroned, and of like form with the Father and the Word, devoutly we magnify Him.

*Troparion:*  
The undefiled, purifying, all-pure Spirit Comforter let us theologize, Who rules over all creation.

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Thou hast been an honored Temple, Ark, and Candlestick, an abode: having shone forth Christ, the unwaning Light unto those in darkness.

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Unto the incomprehensible fire...*  
*Troparion:*  
Unto the one indivisible Essence in three Persons we bow down, the One Sovereignty and Kingdom, wisely singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Having known the Life-Originating and divine Spirit, the Perfecter in the Trinity, with notable songs of praise gloriously we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
O noetic Spirit, O divine Spirit, compassionate toward all, richly distributing operations of gifts unto those singing in faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
The Beauty of Jacob, thee most divinely-comely, O all-pure Mother of God, He Who is fairer than all, God the Word chose, Whom we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: In the shadow of the Law...*  
*Troparion:*  
The many-eyed and divinely-moved Spirit, beloved of God, Who of old in the Prophets foreshowed the present enlightenment and all-rich outpouring of the gifts of grace, distributed unto the disciples and witnesses of the Word.

*Troparion:*  
The divine-originating, inviolable Spirit let us doxologize, Who welling forth unto all and working the divine gifts, the other Comforter Spirit, proceeding from the unoriginate Father, and comprehended together with the co-unoriginate Son.

*Glory... Troparion:*  
Praise the beneficent and rich Spirit, Who enlightens and illumines all with light of understanding: His all-powerful, confessing dominion, ranked together with the Father, and glorified together with the Son, we glorify!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
The shadow of the Law hath passed away, and enlightenment hath shone forth unto those sitting in darkness, from thee, O Virgin, having become incarnate through exceeding compassion, He Who was begotten of the unoriginate Father before all ages, consubstantial with Him Who begat Him.

*On the same Wednesday, in the evening, at "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses: 3 of the Feast, and 3 from the Menaion.*

*Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*  
Behold, the day of joy and gladness! From on high the Holy Spirit appeared today unto the sacred disciples in the appearance of fire from the Father, and enlightened all: He showed the fishermen to be wise teachers, as the divinely-eloquent Luke wrote, filling all things with a rushing wind: therefore, marveling in faith, let us praise the great mercy of Christ our God, and His marvelous descent!

*Sticheron:*  
We celebrate Holy Pentecost, and the power of the Spirit, and the true joy, the fulfillment of divine hope, and the mystery that hath appeared unto us from of old: therefore also we cry aloud unto Thee: O Maker of all, take not Thy Spirit from us, O Word, but send Him from heaven, O Savior: through the prayers of the holy, all-praised, and venerable Apostles, grant peace unto our souls, we pray Thee!

*Sticheron:*  
The animate heavens declare today the magnificent deeds of the Savior, and they went forth into the world clearly to proclaim the teaching of divine power, and they enlightened all creation by their teachings, to sing of the undivided, one Trinity, in three Persons unconfused: therefore in faith we celebrate the coming of the Holy Spirit, which hath appeared from on high and enlightens the ends of the earth.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 7:*  
Having Christ God as Comforter with the Father, unto the other Comforter, Who hath come unto us upon earth today, the Holy Spirit, in faith let us bow down!

*Then, "O Gladsome Light."*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехва́льніи мꙋ́ченицы):*  
The Holy Spirit, proceeding from the Father, and glorified in the Son, by Whom all things are borne and upheld, and in life are sustained, and live, and abide, and are saved, let us theologize: O incomprehensible Comforter, grant peace unto Thy world!

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
The Holy Spirit, the Source of all grace, came substantially, to fill the ends of the earth with heavenly Power, for the sake of the apostles, and with divine grace: unto Him let us cry: O ineffable Comforter, grant peace unto Thy world!

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
The Holy Spirit God, equal in nature and co-enthroned, is known with the Father and the Word, Light most perfect proceeding from Light, from the unoriginate perfect Father, and through the Son proceeding:[^1031] unto Him let us cry: O Life-Giving Comforter, grant peace unto Thy world!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*  
When Thou didst send down Thy Spirit, O Lord... (see fol. 388)[^1030]

*Then, "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart," the Troparion of the Feast, and the Dismissal.*

## ON THURSDAY AFTER PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*  
Behold, the prophetic sayings are fulfilled: for covered with gloomy radiances in them, the revelation in future things, as God the Comforter, hath now been poured out richly upon the apostles, unto those who faithfully worship the uncreated Trinity. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma...*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́йно):*  
The lovers of the Savior were filled with joy, and they who formerly feared took courage, as the Holy Spirit today descended from on high into the house of the disciples; and different ones spoke different things unto the people, and the tongues were seen being divided as if of fire, and burned them not, but rather bedewed them. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast: Tone 7, with Heirmos, to 8; and for the Saint, in the Menaion, to 4. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast, twice.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тридне́вно воскре́слъ е҆сѝ):*  
The All-Holy Spirit, co-essential with the Father and the Word, having come upon the disciples, made their earthen tongues fiery, enlightening them with divine grace.

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
Renew in us, O God, the Holy Spirit, Whom of old Thou didst send unto Thy disciples, O Compassionate One, and didst strengthen them to fulfill Thy saving purposes in the world.

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
Thou Who didst speak of old in the Prophets, O Comforter, hast now made the divine apostles heavens declaring the glory of God, through whom grant unto us cleansing and great mercy.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 2:*  
In Thy courts, O Lord, the faithful bending the knees... (fol. 308)[^1032]

*Then, the First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On the same Thursday, at the Beatitudes, Refrains:*  
*Tone 4, Ode 4 Heirmos: He Who sits in glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
The pre-legal ordinance of true promise is fulfilled: the light-bearing grace hath come through Pentecost; the glory of the Comforter hath appeared, crying: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

*Troparion:*  
Incomprehensible is the Spirit in His willing, surpassing all intellect, and swift of understanding, as older than all the ages, as ranked together with the Father and the Only-Begotten Son.

*Troparion:*  
Not beginning to be, and not ceasing hereafter, but ever-existing, an abyss of unmeasured riches, the all-powerful and co-eternal Spirit is glorified together with the Father and the Only-Begotten Son.

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
The All-Holy Spirit overshadowed thee, O all-hymned Maiden, beautifully making thee a divinely-comely dwelling in the incarnation of the Son, higher than the heavens.

*Ode 8. Heirmos: O Redeemer of all...*  
*Troparion:*  
Dispersing the gloom of sorrow, the All-Good Comforter, unto Thy servants who devoutly sing unto Thee and faithfully cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Distributing gifts by Thy will unto whom Thou desirest, O Comforter: unto those who know Thee as God, grant Thy grace unto them that cry in faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
As true God the Comforter is faithfully worshipped and served, as we devoutly glorify and unceasingly cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
O thou who didst give birth unto God incarnate, still the tumult of my passions and enlighten my soul, making me worthy to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Eve indeed through ailment...*  
*Troparion:*  
The divine gift of the Spirit hath been poured out upon all flesh that hath believed, as of old the Prophet rejoicingly foreshowed: and we, beholding now the fulfillment of what was spoken of old, are enlightened.

...Thou hast filled Thy divinely-eloquent disciples, O Savior, with the All-Holy Spirit, and as Master and Lord Thou didst send them unto the world promising the Light of grace as rays: therefore all of us magnify Thee.

*Glory... Troparion:*  
The spiritual fire, a cleansing furnace, bedewed the hearts of the disciples; the burning dew from heaven enlightened the eyewitnesses of the Word, glorifying the Trinity that shines forth divine knowledge unto the world.

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Of the Holy Spirit, O pure one, thou didst conceive the Word Who shone forth agelessly from the unbegotten Father, and Him incarnate thou didst bear, through exceeding love for mankind and goodness, O Mother of God, Virgin Mother!

*(Concerning the Finding of the Precious Head of John the Forerunner, see on fol. 717)[^1033]*

*On the same Thursday, in the evening, at "Lord, I have cried", we set 6 verses: 3 of the Feast, and 3 from the Menaion.*

*Stichera of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*  
Today the operation of Thine All-Holy Spirit hath come, O Lord, upon Thine apostles, and showed them all-wise in His understanding, and filled them with Thy blessed teaching: therefore we glorify Thy saving dispensation: O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls!

*Sticheron:*  
Today Thy most powerful Spirit, O Master, is sent from the Father, co-essential with Thee, in fiery tongues, and hath prepared Thine apostles to proclaim Thy magnificent deeds and to speak: therefore we glorify Thy saving dispensation: O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls!

*Sticheron:*  
Today Thou hast poured out the gifts of Thy Spirit the Comforter, O Savior, having granted unto human nature to prophesy, as Thou didst say before, O Word, and hast instructed us together to worship the Trinity undivided: therefore we glorify Thy saving dispensation: O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 7:*  
We hymn the consubstantial Trinity, the Father and the Son, with the Holy Spirit: for this God all the Prophets, and the Apostles with the Martyrs, proclaimed.

*Then, "O Gladsome Light."*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́снымъ чинѡ́мъ):*  
Moses on the Mountain saw in fire Him Who is consubstantial; but now unto the beholders of God and wise apostles, the Spirit of fiery appearance comes down, as He divinely proclaimed: for it is one God Who spoke then and now in identity of nature.

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
In fiery-radiant tongues the divinely-eloquent calling unto the water of divine Baptism, consumed the babbling of godless rhetors with the fire of the Spirit: but do Thou enlighten us also, O Comforter, who faithfully theologize Thee!

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
He Who in material substance served Thee, O my God, having taken on the grossness of matter ineffably: as of old with immaterial fire, Thou dost fashion anew by fiery tongues of the Spirit: for Thou art greatly hymned, for Thou art marvelous in Thy works, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 7:*  
Having Christ as Comforter with the Father... (see fol. 386)[^1034]

*Then, "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart," the Troparion of the Feast, and the Dismissal.*

*Know this also: as for the services of the Saints occurring on the coming Saturday and Sunday, we sing one beforehand, and the other on this present Friday at Compline. (See lower on fol. 717)[^1035]*

## ON FRIDAY AFTER PENTECOST, AT MATINS

*At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast, thrice. After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*  
Behold, the prophetic sayings are fulfilled, for covered with gloomy radiances in them...

...revelation in future things, as God the Comforter, hath now been poured out richly upon the apostles, unto those who faithfully worship the uncreated Trinity. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Guiding unto wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости наста́вниче):*  
The All-Holy Spirit having now descended upon the apostles in the appearance of fire, filled the gatherings of nations with wonder: for as they spoke in fiery tongues, O Lover of mankind, each heard his own language; and the wonder seemed unto the unbelievers as drunkenness, but unto the faithful truly salvation was recognized: therefore we glorify Thy dominion, O Christ God, asking remission of sins to be sent richly upon Thy servants. *Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast: Tone 4, with Heirmos, to 8; and for the Saint, to 4. After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn of the Feast, twice.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*  
Unto the All-Holy Spirit, hymned with the Father, and together with the Son faithfully worshipping unceasingly: glorify the all-pure Mother of God, the cause of good!

*Verse: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.*  
Thee, O Spirit the Comforter, faithfully let us praise with the sacred and divine apostles: for at the third hour, as He promised, Christ sent Thee from the Father of lights.

*Verse: Cast me not away from Thy presence, and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.*  
O Holy Trinity, glory to Thee! In hymns we worship the Tri-hypostatic Godhead, Father, and upright Spirit, with the Son, and singing Thee, O Mother of God, divinely, duly and faithfully honoring thee!

*Glory... Both now... Tone 8:*  
When Thou didst send down Thy Spirit, O Lord... (see on fol. 388)[^1036]

*Then, the First Hour, and the Dismissal.*

*On the same Friday, at the Beatitudes, Refrains:*  
*Tone 5, Ode 5 Heirmos: Thou Who clothest Thyself with light...*[^1037]  
*Troparion:*  
Him Who proceeds from the unoriginate Father unchangeably, and rests upon the Son, the All-Holy Spirit, we the faithful doxologize.

*Troparion:*  
Him Who is renewed in our hearts, edifying and enlightening, in whom He is seen, with the apostles let us brightly receive.

*Troparion:*  
The ineffably mighty and all-powerful, renewing those decayed, and enlightening all, the All-Holy Spirit with loud voice let us theologize!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
O divine Mountain, Mountain overshadowed, rich mountain and curdled, which God hath loved: O Holy Virgin Mother, save thy servants!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Unto Thee, Creator of all...*  
*Troparion:*  
Thou art the abiding of all that exist, O Comforter, and preservation: save those who sing unto Thee in faith!

*Troparion:*  
A distribution of incorruptible gifts, and an ocean of grace, and unspendable wealth art Thou, O divine and holy Spirit, and Thee we sing and exalt above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:*  
Life-Originating and life-bearing grace, renew us by the breath of the divine and Holy Spirit; we sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
The Creator, the Wisdom of God, fashioned for Himself a temple of body, O Virgin; entreat Him to save those who in faith honor thee, O pure one, and exalt Him above all unto all the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: Rejoice, O Isaiah...*  
*Troparion:*  
Thou hast offered our first-fruits unto Thy Father, O Savior, having rendered the wealth of divine nature; unto us Thou hast sent the good and life-creating Holy Spirit, co-unoriginate with Thee, O Master!

*Troparion:*  
The First-fruits of the Godhead He now grants unto the earthly nature...

unto the earthly nature, the Spirit of the Father and of the Only-begotten, given not as a stranger, but abiding as of one nature and of one essence, and of equal honor, and enthroned together with Them!

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast shown Thy divine disciples to be heavens, O Savior, proclaiming in fiery tongues Thy dread descent unto us, now sending down upon them the light-bestowing operation of the Comforter from heaven!

*Theotokion:*  
Thou hast been the chamber of the Holy Spirit, O Mother of God, from whom the Maker, the Father's Word, came forth as an adornment; and having tabernacled among us, He hath now revealed the knowledge of the Trinity!

*On the same Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried":*  
*The entire service is of the Feast, without change, exactly as on the Feast itself, except for the Paroemias and the Entrance.*

*Likewise on Saturday of the same week, at Matins:*  
*The entire service is of the Feast, except for the Polyeleos, the Gradual Antiphons, and the Gospel. The Great Doxology. The First Hour, and the Dismissal. The service of the saint of the day is chanted at Compline (see on fol. 497).*

*On Saturday of the same week, at the Liturgy:*  
*At the Beatitudes, a Four-Ode Canon[^1038]: Tone 6, Ode 6, Heirmos: The sea of life...*  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst beforehand work the sanctification of gifts in the apostolic hosts, enlightening them with the lightning-flashes of the Godhead, O Holy Spirit, and building them into a habitation of holiness!

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst show the prophets able to foresee, having foreknowledge of future things in their hearts, as Thou art good, O All-Holy Comforter; and Thou didst dispose them to perceive things afar off!

*Troparion:*  
Being lifted up from the earth by reason of divine virtues, the apostles of Christ received the sovereign Spirit coming from heaven, and they shone with the radiance of the Godhead!

*Theotokion:*  
The Holy Spirit, having come upon thee, O honorable temple of virginity, fashioned from afar an all-holy house for the Son of the Most High, O blessed one!

*Ode 7. Heirmos: He Who made the furnace sprinkle dew...*  
*Troparion:*  
The unoriginate Father and Begetter, and the one Son before the ages, and the proceeding Holy Spirit, we the faithful harmoniously glorify unceasingly: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
The Comforter, bearing the property of the Godhead, hath now come; for conversing with the apostles in fiery tongues, God was manifestly shown: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
With the heavens shaken by Thy co-honored Spirit, Thou hast established Thy disciples, O Christ, to proclaim Thee, the great Sun, as having risen upon us: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*  
By the incarnation of the Word, honoring the divine Light, the Holy Spirit overshadowed thee, O most pure one, and brightly fashioned thee a divine ark: Blessed art thou who didst bear God in the flesh!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: Out of the flame for the saints...*  
*Troparion:*  
Him Who ineffably proceeds from the Father and rests inconfusedly upon the Son, the honorable and all-powerful Spirit, we exalt above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:*  
Cleanse us from the defilements of the soul, wash us from the filth of sin, grant unto us an upright Spirit, O Christ, O Savior, renewing us unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
Thou Who didst call those dwelling in the graves and dost renew the face of all the earth, do Thou likewise mortify the earthly members of those who worship Thee unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*  
Thou wast revealed as an earthly heaven, O pure one, having contained the Heavenly Word in thy womb, whereby He approached holy ones in the flesh upon the earth, Whom we exalt above all unto the ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: God cannot be seen by men...*

*Troparion:*  
Speaking as it were with fiery tongues, the disciples burned up the deception of idols and enlightened the souls of the faithful through the most radiant divine operation of the Comforter Who manifestly came!

*Troparion:*  
Pure receptacles of divine grace and undefiled mirrors of the divine radiance didst Thou show Thy disciples through the net of the Spirit, by the princely shining of God; and them hast Thou sent forth, O Good One, as Thou art abundant in mercy!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
Grant unto those who sing to Thee to obtain divine blessedness through Thy coming, O Comforter, as the fountain of good things, by the communion of the gift imparted to all, giving as a benefactor, O only Lover of mankind!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Most pure one, thou hast supernaturally transformed nature and interceded for us; for through thee, O most pure one, all things that were previously scattered are gathered together into one, and we have inherited the cause of the divine supper and have been accounted worthy of food!

*After the Entrance, Troparion of the Feast. Glory... Both now... Kontakion of the Feast. Prokeimenon and Alleluia of the Feast.*  
*The Epistle: to the Romans, pericope 74: Brethren, grace to you and peace... unto: in yours and mine. And another for the reposed: to the Thessalonians, pericope 270: Brethren, we would not have you ignorant... the entire pericope. The Gospel: from Matthew, pericope 15: The Lord said: Give to him that asks thee... the entire pericope. And another for the reposed: from John, pericope 16: The Lord said unto the Jews who came to Him: Truly, truly, I say unto you: He that hears My word... and the rest unto: but according to the will of the Father Who sent Me. Communion Hymn of the Feast: Thy good Spirit... And another for the reposed: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and received, O Lord. Alleluia. And the Feast is concluded.*

*Be it known that if the Paschal Key falls on 7, after May 25, the Third Finding of the Head of the Forerunner occurs on the present Sunday; and we sing his service on Friday (see on fol. 495). But if the Paschal Key falls on 50, then the entire Saturday is sung together with the Apodosis of the Feast.*[^1039]

*(Full-page woodcut engraving of Christ in Glory with the Assembly of All Saints, bearing the Cyrillic inscription: "НЕДѢ́ЛꙖ · ВСѢ́ХЪ СВѦТЫ́ХЪ", and engraver's monogram KZ).*[^1040]

## First Sunday after Pentecost: Sunday of All Saints

*On Saturday evening, we celebrate the customary All-Night Vigil.*  
*At Small Vespers: in the Octoechos, for 4: one sticheron, twice. Glory... Both now... Dogmatikon, Tone 8:*[^1041]  
How shall we bless thee, O Mother of God? How shall we praise, O all-blessed one, the incomprehensible mystery of thy childbearing? For every Maker and Fashioner of our nature, having had compassion on His own image, brought Himself down into ineffable emptying: the Son, Who is in the immaterial bosom of the Father, took up His abode in thy womb, O pure one, and unchangeably became flesh from thee who knewest not wedlock, remaining what He was by nature, God. Therefore, we worship Him as perfect God and perfect man, the same in both forms; for both natures truly exist in Him, and we proclaim all His natural properties according to His double essence, honoring two operations and two wills: for being of one essence with God the Father, He sovereignly wills and operates as God; and being also of one essence with us, He sovereignly wills and operates as man. Entreat Him, O pure and all-blessed one, that our souls may be saved!

*At the Aposticha: according to custom, to the Mother of God, with their verses.*

*AT GREAT VESPERS.*  
*After the customary opening: Psalm 103. Kathisma 1: Blessed is the man. At "Lord, I have cried," we set 10 verses, and we sing: 3 Resurrection Stichera, 3 Anatolian Stichera, and 4 Stichera of the Saints.*[^1042]

*Resurrection Stichera, Tone 8:*  
Evening hymn and spiritual service we offer unto Thee, O Christ, for Thou didst deign to have mercy upon us through Thy Resurrection!

O Lord, O Lord, cast us not away from Thy presence, but deign to have mercy upon us through Thy Resurrection!

Rejoice, O holy Zion, Mother of the Churches, the dwelling-place of God: for thou didst first receive remission of sins through the Resurrection!

*Anatolian Stichera:*  
The Word born of God the Father before the ages, in these latter times, by His own will took flesh from her who knew not wedlock, and endured crucifixion unto death; and through His Resurrection, O Savior, He hath raised up man who had been slain of old!

We glorify Thy Resurrection from the dead, O Christ, whereby Thou hast freed the race of Adam from the tyranny of Hades, and as God hast granted unto the world life eternal and great mercy!

Glory to Thee, O Christ Savior, only-begotten Son of God, Who wast nailed upon the Cross, and didst rise from the tomb on the third day!

*Stichera to All Saints, Tone 6, Podoben: "All the hope" (Все ᲊпова́нїе):*  
The spiritual orators, the disciples of the Savior, having become instruments through faith, scattered throughout the ends of the earth the venerable preaching, sowing right belief; and by divine husbandry and grace they sprouted the nations, forming hosts of martyrs wondrously depicting Christ's passions on account of many kinds of diverse wounds and fire; and with boldness they pray for our souls! *(Twice)*

Kindled by the fire of the love of the Lord, they despised fire; and as divine coals ignited in Christ, the ranks of the martyrs burned up the audacious insolence of deceit; and they stopped the mouths of wild beasts by divine invocations; and being beheaded, they struck down all the armies of the enemy, and patiently pouring forth streams of blood, they watered the Church that is enlightened through faith!

Throughout all the ends of the earth, let us worthily praise with sacred hymns those who suffered faithfully: the apostles, the martyrs, the God-wise hierarchs, and the sacred assembly of holy women; for earthly beings were united unto heavenly ones, and through sufferings they received freedom from passion through the grace of Christ; and now, shining as bright stars upon us, with boldness they pray for our souls!

*Glory... Tone 6:*  
O divine choir of martyrs, foundation of the Church, fulfillment of the Gospel: ye have in deed fulfilled the sayings of the Savior! For in you the gates of Hades that were opened against the Church have been shut; the shedding of your blood hath dried up the sacrifices of idols; your slaughter hath brought forth the full assembly of the faithful! Ye have astonished the bodiless powers, standing before God with divine manifestations: entreat Him unceasingly for our souls!

*Both now... Theotokion, Tone 8:*  
The King of heaven through His love for mankind... (see in the Octoechos, Saturday, on fol. 198).

*Then, the Entrance. O Gladsome Light. The Prokeimenon of the day.*

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 43:9–14):*[^1043]  
Thus saith the Lord: All the nations were gathered together, and princes shall be gathered out of them. Who will announce these things, or who will declare to us the things from the beginning? Let them bring forth their witnesses, and let them be justified, and let them hear, and let them speak truth. Be ye My witnesses, and I too am a witness, saith the Lord God, and the servant whom I have chosen, that ye may know and understand that I am He: before Me there was no other God, neither shall there be any after Me. I am God, and beside Me there is no savior. I have declared, and have saved, and have reproached, and there was no strange god among us. Ye are My witnesses, and I am the Lord God. Even from the beginning, and there is none that can deliver out of My hands: I will work, and who shall turn it back? Thus saith the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel Who delivers you.

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 3:1–9):*[^1044]  
The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment shall touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure was taken for misery, and their going from us to be utter destruction; but they are in peace. For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded; for God proved them, and found them worthy of Himself. As gold in the furnace hath He tried them, and received them as a burnt offering of sacrifice. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble. They shall judge nations, and have dominion over peoples, and the Lord shall reign over them unto the ages. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth, and such as be faithful in love shall abide with Him; for grace and mercy are in His saints, and visitation among His elect.

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 5:15–6:3):*[^1045]  
The righteous live unto the ages, and their reward is in the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High. Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord; for with His right hand shall He cover them, and with His arm shall He protect them. He shall take to Him His jealousy for complete armor, and make the creation His weapon for the vengeance of His enemies. He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of a helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. His severe wrath shall He sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the unwise. Then shall the right-aiming thunderbolts go abroad, and from the clouds, as from a well-drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark. And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the floods shall cruelly drown them. A mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storm shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule the multitude, and glory in the nations! For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Most High!

*At the Litiya: the Sticheron of the saint of the temple, and the Idiomela of All Saints.*  
*If, however, for some very grave and unavoidable reason the All-Night Vigil is not celebrated, there are sung at "Lord, I have cried": 3 Resurrection Stichera, 4 Anatolian Stichera, and 6 to All Saints, Podoben: "All the hope": 4 stichera; "The spiritual orators": 2 stichera; "Kindled by the fire": 1 sticheron; "Throughout all the ends": and after this, those written for the Litiya: Tone 4, Idiomelon: "In the harmony of faith": 2 stichera; "Come, all ye faithful": 3 stichera; Tone 2: "Come, let us all spiritually rejoice": and the rest is sung at the Litiya.*[^1046]

*At the Litiya, Idiomelon Stichera, Tone 4:*  
In the harmony of faith, let us spiritually celebrate the earthly feast of those who have pleased God from the beginning: the venerable choir of the Patriarchs and Prophets, the adornment of the Apostles, the assembly of the Martyrs, the boast of the Ascetics, the memory of all the Saints; for they pray unceasingly that peace may be granted unto the world, and unto our souls great mercy!

Come, all ye faithful, in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs let us praise the all-glorious memory of all the saints: the Forerunner of the Savior, the Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs, Hierarchs, Teachers, the Venerable, Ascetics, and Righteous, and the godly assembly of holy women; worthily blessing them, with one accord let us cry aloud: O all-good Christ our God, by their prayers grant peace unto Thy churches, victories over enemies unto our Christ-loving rulers, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Tone 2:*  
Come, all ye people, let us spiritually rejoice in the memory of the Saints: for behold, it hath arrived, bringing unto us wealth-producing gifts! Therefore, with the voice of gladness and a pure conscience, let us cry out, saying: Rejoice, choir of the Prophets, who didst announce the coming of Christ unto the world, and didst make present from afar things that were to come as though near at hand! Rejoice, choir of the Apostles, fishers of the nations and catchers of men! Rejoice, assembly of the Martyrs, gathered from the ends of the earth into one faith, who didst endure the torment of tortures, and didst perfectly receive the crown of suffering! Rejoice, leaders of the Fathers, who didst waste away your bodies through fasting, and having mortified the passions of the flesh, didst wing your minds with divine desire and soar up to the heavens, and dwelling with the angels, do receive eternal good things! But O Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs with the Ascetics, earnestly pray unto Him Who hath crowned you all, that they who faithfully and lovingly celebrate your honorable memory may be delivered from visible and invisible enemies!

*Glory... Tone 6:*  
Let us assemble today, ye faithful, for a spiritual table is set before us, and a mystical cup filled with sweet meats, the gladness of the virtues of the Martyrs! For these patient ones from the ends of the earth, having surrendered their bodies to barbarian wounds, offered unto God a rational sacrifice: some being beheaded, others having their backs scraped, others having their hands and all their members cut off, all together became partakers of Christ's suffering; but O Lord Who didst grant them crowns in recompense for their wounds, account us worthy to live according to their footsteps, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Both now... Theotokion, the same Tone:*

Thou art the temple and the gate, the palace and the throne... (see on fol. 134).

*At the Aposticha, Resurrection Stichera, Tone 8.*  
*Other Anatolian Stichera.*  
*Alphabetical. Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*  
Thou didst ascend the Cross, O Jesus, Who camest down from heaven; Thou camest unto death, O immortal Life, the true Light unto those sitting in darkness, the Resurrection unto all that had fallen: our Illumination and Savior, glory to Thee!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, which shall not be moved.*  
We glorify Christ Who rose from the dead: for having assumed soul and body, He separated one from the other by His passion; while His all-pure soul descended into Hades, which He despoiled, His holy body saw not corruption in the tomb: the Redeemer of our souls!

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.*  
In psalms and hymns we glorify Thy Resurrection from the dead, O Christ, whereby Thou hast delivered us from the tyranny of Hades, and as God hast granted life eternal and great mercy!

O incomprehensible Master of all, Creator of heaven and earth, through the passion of the Cross Thou hast poured forth freedom from passion upon me; and having received burial and risen in glory, Thou didst raise up Adam with Thine all-powerful hand: Glory to Thy third-day rising, whereby Thou hast granted eternal life and cleansing of sins, as Thou alone art merciful!

*Glory... Tone 6:*  
Come, ye faithful, having assembled a choir today, let us celebrate piously; and the all-glorious and honorable memory of all the saints let us gloriously honor, saying: Rejoice, glorious apostles, prophets, martyrs, and hierarchs! Rejoice, assembly of the venerable and righteous! Rejoice, choir of holy women, and pray to Christ for the world, that He grant victories over barbarians unto our sovereign, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
My Maker and Redeemer... (see on fol. 25).

*Then, after the Trisagion: Rejoice, O Virgin Mother of God... (twice), and of the Saints (once): In all the world... Blessing of the loaves. Reading from the General Epistle of James.*

*From this Sunday we begin to read at Sunday Matins the Seven Catholic Epistles with their Commentary, and the Fourteen Epistles of the holy Apostle Paul, the Homilies of Chrysostom, and the Apocalypse of holy John the Theologian with its Commentary. If there be no Commentary or Homilies, then read the Epistles themselves, as also the Apocalypse. And we read them at Sunday Vigils as the earlier readings until Great and Holy Sunday of Pascha. The entire book of Chrysostom's Homilies on the Acts of the Holy Apostles is read at the seats as noted on fol. 207 and 208. From this Vigil we also begin to read the Commentary of John Chrysostom on the Gospel of Matthew, from the holy first homily of the Book. The remaining homilies are read throughout the week after the Gospel reading in the Divine Liturgy, finishing the first and second from this Commentary book at the readings of Matins until the end of the month of August, except when the Life of a God-bearing saint occurs, in which case these are omitted and the Life of the saint is read.*[^1047]

*If, however, the All-Night Vigil is not celebrated, Great Vespers is sung according to custom, and the Dismissal Troparion, Tone 8:*  
Thou didst descend from on high, O Merciful One, and didst accept three days' burial, that Thou mightest free us from the passions: our Life and our Resurrection, O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory... to the Saints, Troparion, Tone 4:*  
Adorned with the blood of Thy martyrs throughout the whole world as with purple and fine linen, Thy Church cries out through them unto Thee, O Christ God: Send down Thy compassions upon Thy people, grant peace unto Thy commonwealth, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
The mystery hidden from the ages and unknown unto the angels was made manifest through thee, O Mother of God, unto those on earth: God incarnate in inconfused union, Who willingly endured the Cross for our sake, whereby having raised up the first-fashioned man, He saved our souls from death! *And the Dismissal.*

*At the Midnight Office, the Triadic Canon from the Octoechos, whereof the acrostic is:*  
*Trias monas soson me ton son oiketin.*  
*Which is: O Trinity, Unity, save me Thy servant.*[^1048]

*ON THE SUNDAY OF ALL SAINTS, AT MATINS.*  
*At "God is the Lord": the Resurrection Troparion (twice). Glory... to the Saints. Both now... Theotokion: The mystery hidden from the ages. After the 1st Kathisma, Resurrection Sessional Hymns, Tone 8:*  
Thou hast risen from the dead, O Life of all, and an angel of light cried unto the women: Cease from tears! Proclaim good tidings to the apostles! Cry out singing that Christ the Lord hath risen, Who was pleased as God to save the human race! *(Twice)*  
*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*  
Having received the commanded mystery in his mind, the bodiless angel stood swiftly in Joseph's dwelling, saying unto her who knew not wedlock: He Who bowed the heavens by His descent is unchangeably contained wholly in thee; and beholding Him in thy womb taking the form of a servant, I am astonished to cry unto thee: Rejoice, unwedded Bride!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 8:*  
Men sealed Thy tomb, O Savior, and an angel rolled away the stone from the doors; and the women beheld Thee risen from the dead, and they proclaimed good tidings to Thy disciples in Zion: that Thou hast risen, O Life of all, and the bonds of death are loosed: O Lord, glory to Thee!  
*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*  
O Good One Who for our sake wast born of a Virgin, and didst endure crucifixion, despoiling death by death, and revealing the Resurrection as God: despise not those whom Thou hast fashioned with Thine own hand; manifest Thy love for mankind, O Merciful One; accept the Mother of God who bare Thee, interceding for us; and save, O our Savior, a despairing people!

*And a reading in the Commentary Gospel. After the Evlogitaria, the Troparia: The angelic assembly... and after them, the Ypakoi, Tone 8:*  
The myrrh-bearing women, standing before the tomb of the Life-Giver, sought the immortal Master among the dead, and having received the joyful tidings from the angel, they proclaimed to the apostles that the Lord hath risen, granting great mercy unto the world!

*Gradual Antiphons, Tone 8. Antiphon 1:*  
From my youth the enemy tempts me and burns me with pleasures; but trusting in Thee, O Lord, I vanquish him!

Let them that hate Zion become as grass before it is plucked up; for Christ shall cut off their necks with the scythe of torments!

Through the Holy Spirit all things live; He is Light of Light, a great God: with the Father let us praise Him, and with the Word!

*Antiphon 2:*  
I cried unto Thee, O Lord, give ear: bow down Thine ear unto me as I cry, and cleanse me before Thou takest me away from hence!

Whoso hath hope in the Lord shall not be afraid when He shall judge all things with fire and torment!

To the Holy Spirit belongs the theology of the Thrice-Holy Unity; for the Father is unoriginate, from Whom the Son was timelessly begotten, and the Spirit, co-enthroned and of one form, shone forth from the Father!

*Antiphon 3:*  
Let my heart be covered with Thy fear, being humble-minded, lest being lifted up it fall from Thee, O All-Compassionate One!

Every one that climbs up in the world of his own land shall go forth again to receive punishments or rewards for having lived well!

Through the Holy Spirit every divine man sees and foretells; he works lofty wonders, singing one God in three Persons; for though He shines in three lights, yet the Godhead holds supreme rule!

*Antiphon 4:*  
Behold now, what is so good or what is so pleasant as for brethren to dwell together in unity? For in this the Lord promised life eternal: He Who adorns our garments like the lilies of the field commands us not to be anxious!

Through the Holy Spirit, as by a single cause, all things are held together in peace-giving concord; for this God is of one essence with the Father and the Son, as is fittingly said!

*Prokeimenon, Tone 8: The Lord shall reign forever, Thy God, O Zion, unto generation and generation!*  
*Verse: Praise the Lord, O my soul! I will praise the Lord in my life!*  
*Let every breath praise the Lord. Matins Resurrection Gospel 1: from Matthew, pericope 121 (Matt. 28:16–20).*  
*From this day we begin to read the Sunday Matins Resurrection Gospels in order.*

*Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ... Psalm 50. Through the prayers of the holy Apostles... and: Through the prayers of the Mother of God... Sticheron: Jesus, having risen from the tomb...*  
*Three Canons: of the Resurrection with its Heirmos, for 4; the second Resurrection Canon, for 2; of the Mother of God, for 2; and of All Saints, for 6.*

*Canon of the Resurrection, Tone 8, Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
*Having armed Pharaoh, the wonder-working rod of Moses submerged him of old, striking the sea crosswise and dividing it; but it saved Israel that fled on foot, as they sent up a hymn unto God!*

*Troparion:*  
How can we not marvel at the almighty Godhead of Christ? For from His sufferings He pours forth passionlessness and incorruption upon all the faithful, and from His holy side He causes a fountain of immortality to trickle, and everlasting life from the tomb!

*Troparion:*  
How magnificent the angel now appeared unto the women, bearing bright and natural images, proclaiming the light of the Resurrection as an image of immaterial purity, crying: The Lord hath risen!

*Theotokion:*  
Glorious things were spoken of thee from generation to generation, O Mary Mother of God, who didst contain God the Word in thy womb, remaining pure: therefore we all honor thee, our true protection after God!

*Second Canon of the Resurrection, Ode 1. Heirmos: Having traversed the water...*  
*Troparion:*  
The gates of weeping were affrighted, and the gatekeepers of Hades trembled, beholding Him Who is on high above all nature descend into the nethermost parts!

*Troparion:*  
The angelic ranks marveled, beholding fallen human nature, which had been shut up in the nethermost parts of the earth, seated upon the Father's throne!

*Another Canon to the Most Holy Mother of God, Ode 1. Heirmos: Let us sing unto the Lord...*  
*Troparion:*  
O most pure Mother of God, who supernaturally didst bear the co-eternal and all-divine Word made flesh, we sing unto thee!

*Troparion:*  
O Virgin, who didst bud forth Christ the life-bearing Cluster of Grapes, dripping sweetness of salvation unto all the world, thou hast borne Him!

*Canon of All Saints, whereof the acrostic is: TON HAGION PANTON POLYONYMA TAGMATA MELPO, which is: I hymn the many-named ranks of all the saints.[^1049] By John of Damascus.*  
*Tone 8, Ode 1. Heirmos: Having armed Pharaoh...*  
*Troparion:*  
As I hymn the ranks of Thy saints, I pray that my soul may be illuminated by Thy light through their prayers; for Thou art the unapproachable Light, driving away the darkness of ignorance, O Word of God, Giver of light, O Christ! *(Twice)*

*Troparion:*  
When Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, O Good One, Thou didst draw the entire heritage of the nations unto Thy knowledge; and Thou didst clarify the light of the Holy Trinity, driving away the mist of deception through Thy holy apostles!

*Troparion:*  
Instructed by Thy legislation, O Christ, Thy glorious apostles cast away all earthly things as refuse, and with the light of grace they enlightened the whole universe, proclaiming Thee according to the Gospel!

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
Rejoicing, the noble martyrs took up Thy Cross, and steadfastly imitating Thy honorable passion, they were not terrified by the tyrant's threats, neither by fire, nor by sword, nor by wounds, nor yet by hunger, nor even by death!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Having assumed a manly resolve, O all-pure Virgin, the holy maidens firmly followed the martyrs' suffering, and walking after thee, O Virgin, rejoicing divinely, they were led unto the King of all!

*Katavasia: I shall open my mouth...*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
*Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens by understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me upon the rock of the Church, O Christ, for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind!*

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst justify Adam, who was condemned through the tasting of sin, by the saving passion of Thy flesh, O Christ: for being Thyself innocent of the trial of death, Thou didst submit Thyself, O Sinless One!

*Troparion:*  
The light of the Resurrection shone forth unto those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, even my God Jesus; and having bound the strong one by His Godhead, He despoiled his vessels!

*Theotokion:*  
Thou hast been shown higher than the Cherubim and Seraphim, O Mother of God; for thou alone, O undefiled one, didst receive the uncontainable God in thy womb: therefore all we the faithful bless thee, O pure one, in hymns!

*Second Canon, Ode 3. Heirmos: O Lord, Builder of the vault of heaven...*  
*Troparion:*  
Him that previously was disobedient to the commandment of the Lord, Thou didst bring near unto Thyself Who didst create me; taking his form upon Thyself and instructing him by Thine own obedience, Thou hast restored him by Thy crucifixion!

*Troparion:*  
Foreseeing all things by Thy wisdom, O Lord, and having established the nethermost parts by understanding, Thou didst not deem it unworthy by Thy descent, O Word of God, to raise up him who was fashioned according to Thine image!

*Third Canon, Ode 3. Heirmos: Thou art the affirmation...*  
*Troparion:*  
Grant us help by thy prayers, O all-pure one, repelling the assaults of grievous adversities!

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast been the restoration of Eve our foremother, having given birth to the Prince of Life for the world, Christ, O Mother of God!

*Fourth Canon (All Saints), Ode 3. Heirmos: The heavens were established...*  
*Troparion:*  
Holily robed as hierarchs and pastors, and having pastored Thy rational flock in a manner pleasing to Thee, O Christ, they worthily adorned the word of teaching, being truly enriched from above! *(Twice)*

*Troparion:*  
Adorned with the beauties of the primary creation of good, and appearing as unerrant stars, ye adorned the Church of Christ, O holy ones, embellishing her in diverse ways! *(Twice)*

*Glory...*  
*Troparion:*  
Yielding obedience unto Thy law, the assemblies of the blessed ones, illuminated by manifold virtues, inherited the heavenly mansions, rejoicing; for diverse ranks worthily filled them!

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
Virgin Earth, who didst bear for us the God Word from God, O Mother of God: Whom the holy virgins divinely loved, and following after thee, they manifestly followed Him in all things!

*Sessional Hymns, Tone 8:*  
Having endured mountains of tortures and standing as spiritual pillars, the all-lauded martyrs of Christ our God, taken up from the earth to the height, became eyewitnesses of heavenly glory by their translation: therefore, having been worthily enriched with the gifts of the Spirit, ye ever bestow healing! O all-lauded passion-bearers, entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who lovingly celebrate your holy memory!

*Another Sessional Hymn, the same Tone. Glory...*
